knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled barrier-reduction and inner-solve tolerance schedule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_{\mu_k}\) be smooth barrier subproblems, let \(x^k\) be their computed approximate solutions, and let \(r(x,\mu)\geq0\) be a stationarity or centrality residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth barrier continuation with residual-based termination of each inner solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inner–outer accuracy schedule is a sequence \(\{(\mu_k,\eta_k)\}_{k\geq0}\) such that \[0<\mu_{k+1}<\mu_k,\qquad \mu_k\to0,\qquad r(x^k,\mu_k)\leq\eta_k,\] where \(\eta_k\geq0\) is the inner tolerance used before reducing the outer barrier parameter. A path-neighborhood schedule uses a dimensionless residual such as the Newton decrement or scaled centrality residual and imposes \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\). A vanishing-error schedule additionally requires \(\eta_k\to0\), often with \(\eta_k=O(\mu_k^p)\) for some \(p>0\). The pair, rather than either sequence alone, specifies how accurately each barrier subproblem must be solved before continuation proceeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner–outer accuracy schedule couples the decreasing barrier parameter with a required quality for each inner subproblem solution. At stage \(k\), the residual at \(x^k\) must not exceed \(\eta_k\). A fixed tolerance below a path-neighborhood threshold supports path tracking, while a tolerance tending to zero defines increasingly accurate subproblem solves.
assumptions_latex: The residual satisfies \(r(x,\mu)=0\) at an exact interior minimizer or central point.
Each outer update occurs only after \(r(x^k,\mu_k)\leq\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(\mu_k,\eta_k)\}\) is an inner–outer accuracy schedule precisely when it jointly prescribes barrier reduction and the accepted residual level for every inner solve.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a positive-definite subproblem Hessian, one may use \(r(x,\mu)=\|\nabla\Phi_\mu(x)\|_{\nabla^2\Phi_\mu(x)^{-1}}\).
For logarithmic linear-programming barriers, a scaled centrality residual \(\|q(x,\mu)\|\leq\eta_k\) gives a dimensionless path-neighborhood criterion.
special_cases_latex: Constant-neighborhood schedules take \(\eta_k=\bar\eta<1\).
Proportional forcing schedules take \(\eta_k=c\mu_k\).
A short-step schedule reduces \(\mu_k\) mildly enough that one Newton correction can restore the same neighborhood.
immediate_consequences_latex: Smaller outer reductions generally permit looser or cheaper corrections while preserving a fixed neighborhood.
Vanishing \(\eta_k\) rules out persistent inner stationarity error.
boundary_notes: The condition \(\eta_k\to0\) alone does not specify its rate relative to \(\mu_k\).
A residual must be scaled consistently; an unscaled Euclidean gradient can be misleading near an ill-conditioned barrier boundary.
Nonconvex subproblems require additional safeguards because a small stationarity residual need not identify a minimum.

notation.meaning: Chosen inner stationarity or centrality residual.
Inner acceptance tolerance at outer stage \(k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional standard normalization with third-derivative constant two and finite barrier parameter \(\nu\).

The function \(F\) is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\) if, for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}Q\) and \(h\in\mathbb R^n\), \[|D^3F(x)[h,h,h]|\leq2 igl(D^2F(x)[h,h] igr)^{3/2},\] \[|DF(x)[h]|\leq\sqrt{

A \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier is a smooth convex boundary barrier whose third derivative is controlled by the three-halves power of its second derivative and whose gradient has dual local norm at most \(\sqrt

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-Concordant Taylor Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-free local value and gradient-remainder estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(r=\|h\|_x<1\), a standard self-concordant function satisfies \[\omega(r)\leq F(x+h)-F(x)-\langle
abla F(x),hangle\leq\omega_*(r),\] where \(\omega(r)=r-\log(1+r)\) and \(\omega_*(r)=-r-\log(1-r)\). It also satisfies \[\|
abla F(x+h)-
abla F(x)-
abla^2F(x)h\|_{x,*}\leq rac{r^2}{1-r}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-concordance gives dimension-free local upper and lower Taylor bounds and a quadratic gradient-linearization remainder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \omega(r)\leq F(x+h)-F(x)-\nabla F(x)^Th\leq\omega_*(r),\qquad \|R_\nabla\|_{x,*}\leq r^2/(1-r).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dikin Ellipsoid and Hessian Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local metric geometry of a standard self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a standard self-concordant barrier on \(C\), let \(x\in\operatorname{int}C\), and put \(r=\|h\|_x<1\). Then \(x+h\in\operatorname{int}C\) and \[(1-r)^2
abla^2F(x)\preceq
abla^2F(x+h)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}
abla^2F(x).\] Hence the open Dikin ellipsoid \(\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}\) lies in the barrier domain.

u\)-self-concordant barrier when it is convex, three-times continuously differentiable, has positive-definite Hessian, satisfies \(\lvert D^3F(x)[h,h,h]vert\leq2(D^2F(x)[h,h])^{3/2}\) and \(\lvert DF(x)[h]vert\leq\sqrt{

abla^2F(x)^{-1}sangle}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard self-concordant barrier has controlled third derivative, bounded gradient in its Hessian metric, positive curvature, and divergence at the feasible-set boundary.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, convex, line-free, and have nonempty interior. Let \(F\in C^3(\operatorname{int}Q)\) be convex with \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A standard self-concordant barrier is a convex \(F\) satisfying \[|D^3F(x)[h,h,h]|\leq2\|h\|_x^3,\qquad \|h\|_x=\langle
abla^2F(x)h,hangle^{1/2},\] for all interior \(x\) and directions \(h\), together with \(F(x_k)	o+\infty\) as \(x_k	o\partial Q\) from the interior. Its dual local norm and Newton decrement are \[\|s\|_x^*=\langle
abla^2F(x)^{-1}s,sangle^{1/2},\qquad \lambda_F(x)=\|
abla F(x)\|_x^*.\] The associated Dikin ellipsoid \(W(x)=\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard family uses the normalization in which the third directional derivative is bounded by twice the cube of the Hessian norm. Together with boundary divergence, this makes \(F\) a standard self-concordant barrier. Its Hessian defines primal and dual local norms, its gradient’s dual norm is the Newton decrement, and its local unit ellipsoid remains inside the barrier domain.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) contains no affine line, so the barrier Hessian is nondegenerate under the stated setting.
\(F\) is convex, three times continuously differentiable, and boundary-divergent.
The standard self-concordance inequality holds at every interior point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized inequality, boundary divergence, and Hessian metric define the standard self-concordant barrier family and its local geometry \((\|\cdot\|_x,\|\cdot\|_x^*,\lambda_F(x),W(x))\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For arbitrary directions \(h_1,h_2,h_3\), standard self-concordance is equivalently \(|D^3F(x)[h_1,h_2,h_3]|\leq2\prod_{i=1}^3\|h_i\|_x\).
A nonstandard self-concordant function can be rescaled to this normalization when its self-concordance constant is positive.
special_cases_latex: The ray barrier \(-\log x\) is standard self-concordant.
The logarithmic barrier of a polyhedron is a sum of standard one-dimensional logarithmic barriers after affine pullback.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any step \(h\) with \(\|h\|_x<1\) remains in the domain.
The Newton step has local length \(\lambda_F(x)\).
The definition and local norms transform covariantly under nonsingular affine changes of variables.
boundary_notes: Standard self-concordance alone does not specify the parameter \(\nu\).
If the domain contains lines, the Hessian may be degenerate along them and relative-space treatment is needed.
The closed unit ellipsoid may touch the boundary; the guaranteed inclusion is for the open unit ellipsoid.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The barrier \(F\) is \(
u\)-self-scaled if, for every \(x,w\in\operatorname{int}K\), \[
abla^2F(w)x\in\operatorname{int}K^*\] and \[F_* igl(
abla^2F(w)x igr)=F(x)-2F(w)-
u.\] Thus every barrier Hessian \(
abla^2F(w):E	o E^*\) maps the primal cone interior into the dual cone interior and intertwines the primal and dual barriers by the stated value identity. The conjugate barrier \(F_*\) is self-scaled for \(K^*\) exactly when \(F\) is self-scaled for \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-scaled barrier is a normal cone barrier whose Hessian at every interior scaling point maps every primal interior point into the dual interior. Evaluating the dual barrier at that Hessian image reproduces the primal barrier values according to an exact scaling identity. This makes the Hessian a global primal–dual scaling map, not merely a local metric.

Self-scaled barriers are closed under passage to the conjugate dual barrier.

The log-determinant barrier on the positive-semidefinite cone is self-scaled.
Lorentz-cone logarithmic barriers provide another canonical self-scaled family.

The admissible cones for self-scaled barriers are symmetric cones up to standard structural qualifications.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Represent a barrier object by a triple \((Q,F,\nu)\), where \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for a convex set \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional constructions generated by sums and affine pullbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The barrier construction calculus is the closure system generated by the following operations on barrier triples. First, if \((Q_i,F_i,
u_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), are defined in a common space, their intersection sum is \[Q= igcap_{i=1}^mQ_i,\qquad F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x),\qquad 
u=\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i,\] on \(\operatorname{int}Q= igcap_i\operatorname{int}Q_i\), provided this interior is nonempty. Second, if \(A(x)=Lx+b\) is affine, the pullback is \[\widetilde Q=A^{-1}(Q),\qquad \widetilde F(x)=F(A(x)),\qquad \widetilde
u=
u,\] on points mapped into \(\operatorname{int}Q\). Finite compositions of these operations are constructed barriers, with parameters propagated by addition and preserved by affine pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier construction calculus treats a barrier and its parameter as a composable object. Barriers for intersected restrictions are added, which adds their parameters. A barrier can also be transported through an affine representation by composition, which preserves its parameter. Repeating these two operations constructs barriers for many represented convex domains.
assumptions_latex: Every input \(F_i\) is a \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q_i\).
The constructed domain has nonempty interior.
Each affine composition is evaluated only where its image lies in the source barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Finite sums over intersections and affine pullbacks preserve self-concordant barrier structure, with parameter rules \(
u_{\mathrm{sum}}=\sum_i
u_i\) and \(
u_{\mathrm{pullback}}=
u\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A represented set \(\{x:A_i(x)\in Q_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) carries the barrier \(\sum_iF_i(A_i(x))\) with parameter \(\sum_i\nu_i\).
Cartesian-product construction is the disjoint-variable special case of the sum operation.
special_cases_latex: Polyhedral logarithmic barriers arise by pulling back \(-\log s\) through each affine slack and summing.
Semidefinite-represented domains use affine matrix maps followed by log-determinant barriers.
immediate_consequences_latex: The parameter can be tracked syntactically through a represented-domain expression.
Affine changes of coordinates do not inflate the barrier parameter.
Independent product blocks contribute additively to the parameter.
boundary_notes: Nonempty interior is essential; inconsistent intersections have no barrier domain.
Nonlinear composition is not covered by the affine pullback rule.
Parameter addition gives a valid construction parameter but need not be the smallest possible parameter for the resulting set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive barrier construction for the lifted formulation using barriers for the base set and the objective and constraint epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F_Q\) is a \(v_Q\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\), \(F_0(x,\xi)\) is a \(v_0\)-self-concordant barrier for the epigraph of \(f_0\), and \(F_j(x,\varkappa)\) is a \(v_j\)-self-concordant barrier for the epigraph of \(f_j\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\). Then the feasible set of the lifted problem has the self-concordant barrier \[\widehat F(x,\xi,\varkappa)=F_Q(x)+F_0(x,\xi)+\sum_{j=1}^mF_j(x,\varkappa)-\ln(\bar\xi-\xi)-\ln(-\varkappa),\] with parameter \[\widehat v=v_Q+v_0+\sum_{j=1}^m v_j+2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of the barriers for Q and the required epigraphs, together with logarithmic barriers for the upper bound on xi and the negativity of varkappa, is a self-concordant barrier for the lifted feasible set. Its parameter is the sum of the component parameters plus two.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(Q_i\subset E_i\) be closed convex sets with nonempty interiors and let \(F_i\) be \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barriers for \(Q_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections in a common space and finite Cartesian products in block spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an intersection in a common space \(E\), if \(Q= igcap_iQ_i\) has nonempty interior, its composite barrier is \[F_{\cap}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x),\qquad x\in igcap_i\operatorname{int}Q_i,\] with parameter \(
u_{\cap}=\sum_i
u_i\). For the Cartesian product \(Q_	imes=Q_1	imes\cdots	imes Q_m\subset E_1	imes\cdots	imes E_m\), the product barrier is \[F_	imes(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x_i),\] again with parameter \(
u_	imes=\sum_i
u_i\). The Hessian of the product barrier is block diagonal with blocks \(
abla^2F_i(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite-set barrier calculus assigns the sum of component barriers to either an intersection of constraints or a Cartesian product of independent blocks. In both cases the certified barrier parameters add. For a product, the local metric separates into block-diagonal component metrics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sum barrier is a \((\sum_i\nu_i)\)-self-concordant barrier for the intersection or Cartesian product, on the corresponding product or common interior.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The product construction is the intersection construction after lifting each component barrier through the coordinate projection \(\pi_i(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=x_i\).
For represented restrictions \(A_i(x)\in Q_i\), the composite barrier is \(\sum_iF_i(A_i(x))\).
special_cases_latex: The positive orthant barrier is the product sum of \(n\) ray barriers \(-\log x_i\).
A block-diagonal semidefinite cone carries the sum of log-determinant barriers of its blocks.
immediate_consequences_latex: The product local norm satisfies \(\|h\|_x^2=\sum_i\|h_i\|_{x_i,i}^2\).
Boundary approach in any component makes the composite barrier diverge.
Independent block structure is retained in the product Hessian.
boundary_notes: An empty-interior intersection is not covered even if the closed sets intersect on a lower-dimensional face.
Summing barriers can overestimate the smallest barrier parameter available for the composite set.
Infinite products or infinitely many intersected constraints require additional functional-analytic conditions.

notation.meaning: Sum barrier for a finite intersection.
Separable sum barrier for a Cartesian product.

children.title: Cartesian-Product Barrier Composition
children.top_down_role: Barrier assembly for feasible regions represented as Cartesian products.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product Local-Metric Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable local norms, Newton steps, and Newton decrements of a Cartesian-product barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x_i)\) with \(H_i=\nabla^2F_i(x_i)\succ0\), \[\|h\|_x^2=\sum_i h_i^TH_ih_i,\qquad \|g\|_{x,*}^2=\sum_i g_i^TH_i^{-1}g_i.\] The Newton step is componentwise, \(d_i=-H_i^{-1}\nabla F_i(x_i)\), and \(\lambda_F(x)^2=\sum_i\lambda_{F_i}(x_i)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The product-barrier metric, Newton step, and squared Newton decrement split exactly across factors.
assumptions_latex: Each component barrier is twice differentiable with positive-definite Hessian at \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_F(x)^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_{F_i}(x_i)^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Product Local-Metric Decomposition
Cartesian-Product Barrier Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable barrier construction for a finite Cartesian product of convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(F_i\) be a standard \(
u_i\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\). On \(C=C_1	imes\cdots	imes C_m\), define \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x_i)\). Then \(\operatorname{int}C=\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{int}C_i\), the Hessian of \(F\) is block diagonal with blocks \(
abla^2F_i(x_i)\), and \(F\) is a standard \((\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i)\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing component barriers yields a barrier on the Cartesian product, with block-diagonal local metric and barrier parameter equal to the sum of component parameters.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_i\) is a standard \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\) is a standard \(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier on \(\prod_{i=1}^m C_i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard separable product rule for self-concordant barriers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind appropriately captures the separable product construction, and the block-diagonal Hessian and summed parameter are mathematically plausible. The finite-product closure rule needs a specific authoritative theorem or proposition locator.

children.title: Intersected-Set Barrier Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Barrier assembly for feasible regions formed by intersecting component domains.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty Common-Interior Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain failure preventing an intersection barrier from being a full-dimensional standard barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{int}C_i=\varnothing\), then \(\sum_iF_i\) has no common open domain and cannot be a standard full-dimensional barrier on \(\bigcap_iC_i\). In particular, \(C_1=[0,\infty)\) and \(C_2=(-\infty,0]\) intersect at \(\{0\}\), but the component barriers \(-\log x\) and \(-\log(-x)\) have no common point of definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty set intersection is insufficient: the component interiors must intersect for the ordinary summed-barrier construction.
assumptions_latex: Barriers are interpreted on Euclidean interiors rather than relative interiors after affine-hull reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_i\operatorname{int}C_i=\varnothing\implies\sum_iF_i\) has no common barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Common-Interior Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intersection Metric Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative and local-metric structure of a summed barrier on a common interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\) on \(D= igcap_i\operatorname{int}C_i\), \[
abla F(x)=\sum_i
abla F_i(x),\qquad 
abla^2F(x)=\sum_i
abla^2F_i(x),\qquad \|h\|_{F,x}^2=\sum_i\|h\|_{F_i,x}^2.\] Unlike the Cartesian-product case, the Newton step generally does not decompose componentwise because all component Hessians act on the same variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersection barriers add their gradients, Hessians, and squared local norms, but generally do not produce independent component Newton steps.
assumptions_latex: All component barriers are twice differentiable at the common interior point \(x\).

notation.meaning: local norm induced by the ith component Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Metric Aggregation
Intersected-Set Barrier Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier construction for intersections represented by simultaneous convex-set constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(F_i\) be a standard \(
u_i\)-self-concordant barrier on a closed convex set \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose \(D= igcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{int}C_i
eq\varnothing\). Define \(C= igcap_{i=1}^m C_i\) and \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^mF_i(x)\) for \(x\in D\). Then \(D=\operatorname{int}C\), and \(F\) is a standard \((\sum_{i=1}^m
u_i)\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the constraint interiors intersect, the sum of their barriers is a barrier for the set intersection, with parameter bounded by the sum of individual parameters.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_i\) is a standard \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\) is a standard \(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier on \(\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-sum rule for self-concordant barriers on intersected domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the intersection construction, and the common-interior hypothesis addresses the domain identity. A source is still required for the finite-sum self-concordance rule, barrier-boundary behavior on the intersection, and summed parameter.

children.title: Composition Parameter Accounting
children.top_down_role: Changes in barrier parameters under product or intersection construction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subunit Scaling Failure for Standard Self-Concordance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of the scaling restriction in standard self-concordant composition rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=-\log x\) on \((0,\infty)\) and \(g=\alpha f\). For \(0<\alpha<1\), \[\frac{|g'''(x)|}{2(g''(x))^{3/2}}=\alpha^{-1/2}>1,\] so \(g\) violates the standard self-concordance inequality at every \(x>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The one-dimensional logarithmic barrier shows that the usual scaling condition α at least one is sharp.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\alpha<1\implies \alpha(-\log x)\) is not standard self-concordant.
knowledge_statements.title: Subunit Scaling Failure for Standard Self-Concordance
Composition Parameter Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter rule for finite sums of scaled standard self-concordant barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_i\) be standard \(
u_i\)-self-concordant barriers on a common nonempty domain \(D\), and let \(\alpha_i\geq1\). The scaled functions \(\alpha_iF_i\) are standard \((\alpha_i
u_i)\)-self-concordant barriers, and their sum \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_iF_i\) is a standard barrier with valid parameter \(
u=\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i
u_i\). This accounting parameter is an upper bound and need not be the smallest admissible parameter of the composite barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling barriers by factors at least one and summing them gives the valid aggregate parameter Σαν, though this bound need not be minimal.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_i\) is a standard \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barrier on the relevant common or product domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu_{\mathrm{comp}}\leq\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i\nu_i\), with the displayed sum always a valid barrier parameter.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scaling and finite-sum calculus for standard self-concordance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits parameter accounting, and the restriction alpha_i at least one is relevant to preserving standard self-concordance under scaling. The exact parameter rule and interpretation of nu_comp as the smallest admissible parameter require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Affine Barrier Transport Calculus
children.top_down_role: Barrier transport through affine representations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine pullback of a self-concordant barrier
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb R\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for \(Q\subset E_1\), and let \(\mathcal A:E\to E_1\) be affine, \(\mathcal A(x)=Ax+b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine preimages; the pullback Hessian may be degenerate when \(A\) has a nontrivial nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine transport of \(F\) through \(\mathcal A\) is \[\Phi(x)=F(\mathcal A(x)),\qquad \operatorname{dom}\Phi=\{x\in E:\mathcal A(x)\in\operatorname{int}Q\}.\] If this domain is nonempty, \(\Phi\) is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier for the affine preimage \(\widetilde Q=\{x:\mathcal A(x)\in Q\}\). Its derivatives are \[
abla\Phi(x)=A^*
abla F(\mathcal A(x)),\qquad 
abla^2\Phi(x)=A^*
abla^2F(\mathcal A(x))A,\] and \(D^3\Phi(x)[h,h,h]=D^3F(\mathcal A(x))[Ah,Ah,Ah]\). The certified parameter remains \(
u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine barrier transport composes a barrier with an affine representation. The resulting function is defined exactly at points whose affine images lie in the original barrier interior, and it is a barrier for the corresponding affine preimage. Gradient, Hessian, and third derivatives follow the affine chain rule, while the barrier parameter is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi=F\circ\mathcal A\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier for \(\mathcal A^{-1}(Q)\), with derivatives transported by \(A\) and \(A^*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a nonsingular affine change of coordinates, affine transport is a reparameterization of the same barrier geometry.
Restriction of a barrier to an affine subspace is obtained by choosing \(\mathcal A\) as an affine embedding of that subspace.
special_cases_latex: The polyhedral barrier \(-\sum_i\log(b_i-a_i^\top x)\) is obtained by transporting orthant logarithmic barriers through affine slack maps.
The semidefinite barrier \(-\log\det(A_0+\sum_ix_iA_i)\) is an affine pullback of the positive-definite-cone barrier.
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine transport preserves the certified barrier parameter.
The induced local norm is \(\|h\|_{x,\Phi}=\|Ah\|_{\mathcal A(x),F}\).
If \(A\) is injective relative to the relevant affine hull, positive definiteness of the source Hessian transfers to the pullback.
boundary_notes: If \(A\) has null directions, the pullback Hessian is singular along them unless the domain is restricted or quotiented.
Nonlinear maps do not satisfy this parameter-preserving rule in general.
An empty affine preimage interior yields no valid transported barrier domain.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the linear part of \(\mathcal A\).

children.title: Affine-Subspace Barrier Restriction
children.top_down_role: Restriction of barriers to feasible affine subspaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Representation of an Affine Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between an intrinsic affine-subspace restriction and a reduced-coordinate pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=a+V\), let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n	imes r}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}U=V\), and set \(x=a+Uz\). The restricted barrier has reduced-coordinate representation \(\widehat F(z)=F(a+Uz)\), with \[
abla\widehat F(z)=U^\mathsf T
abla F(a+Uz),\qquad 
abla^2\widehat F(z)=U^\mathsf T
abla^2F(a+Uz)U.\] For every reduced direction \(d\), \[d^\mathsf T
abla^2\widehat F(z)d=(Ud)^\mathsf T
abla^2F(x)(Ud).\] Replacing \(U\) by \(UR\) for nonsingular \(R\) changes only coordinates and represents the same intrinsic restricted metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine-subspace restriction is equivalently represented through any full-rank basis parametrization; changing the basis changes coordinates but not the intrinsic tangent metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat F=F\circ(a+U\cdot)\) represents \(F|_L\), with the displayed derivative and basis-invariance relations.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the affine direction space

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Representation of an Affine Restriction
Affine-Subspace Barrier Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a barrier and its local metric to a feasible affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a standard \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(L=a+V\) be an affine subspace satisfying \(L\cap\operatorname{int}C
eq\varnothing\). On the relative interior of \(C\cap L\), define \(F_L(x)=F(x)\). Then \(F_L\) is a standard \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier relative to \(L\). For \(x\in L\cap\operatorname{int}C\) and \(h\in V\), its local metric is the restriction \(\|h\|_{x,L}^2=\langle h,
abla^2F(x)hangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a barrier to an affine subspace meeting the original interior preserves self-concordance and the parameter, using the Hessian metric on tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F|_{L\cap\operatorname{int}C}\) is a relative standard \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C\cap L\).

notation.meaning: affine subspace with direction space V

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine restriction invariance of self-concordance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits affine-subspace restriction, and the relative-domain and tangent-metric formulation is coherent. A source must confirm preservation of the same parameter and the precise relative-interior barrier convention.

children.title: Affine Pullback Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barrier transport from a target domain through an affine preimage.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pullback of Local Norms and Dikin Ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric transport induced by an injective affine pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the affine pullback \(G(z)=F(Az+b)\), define \(\|h\|_{G,z}^2=h^\mathsf T\nabla^2G(z)h\) and \(\|u\|_{F,T(z)}^2=u^\mathsf T\nabla^2F(T(z))u\). Then \[\|h\|_{G,z}=\|Ah\|_{F,T(z)}.\] Consequently, \[\{z+h:\|h\|_{G,z}<1\}=\{z+h:\|Ah\|_{F,T(z)}<1\},\] so the unit Dikin ellipsoid of \(G\) is the parameter-space preimage of the target local ellipsoid intersected with the affine image directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An injective affine pullback transports the barrier metric isometrically, and its Dikin ellipsoid is the corresponding parameter-space preimage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|h\|_{G,z}=\|Ah\|_{F,T(z)}\), with the displayed Dikin-ellipsoid correspondence.
knowledge_statements.title: Pullback of Local Norms and Dikin Ellipsoids
Affine Pullback Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier transport through an injective affine parametrization of a preimage set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a standard \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(T(z)=Az+b\) with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes p}\) of full column rank. If \(D=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^p:T(z)\in C\}\) has nonempty interior, then \(G(z)=F(Az+b)\) is a standard \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D\). Its derivatives satisfy \(
abla G(z)=A^\mathsf{T}
abla F(T(z))\) and \(
abla^2G(z)=A^\mathsf{T}
abla^2F(T(z))A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a barrier with an injective affine map gives a barrier for the affine preimage and pulls back the gradient and Hessian by the map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=F\circ T\) is a standard \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(D=T^{-1}(C)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine invariance of standard self-concordance under injective parametrization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits affine pullback barriers, and full column rank makes the pulled-back Hessian positive definite. The claim that the same barrier parameter is preserved on the full preimage requires a specific affine-invariance source locator.

children.title: Projected Image Barriers
children.top_down_role: Barrier representations associated with affine images or projections.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fiber Optimality and Projected Hessian Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential structure of a projected-image value function at a smooth nondegenerate fiber minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(y)=\min\{F(x):Ax=y\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{p	imes n}\) has full row rank. Suppose the unique minimizer \(x(y)\) varies smoothly, \(F\in C^2\), and \(H=
abla^2F(x(y))\succ0\). Under the convention \(
abla F(x(y))=A^T\lambda(y)\), \[
abla G(y)=\lambda(y),\qquad Dx(y)=H^{-1}A^T(AH^{-1}A^T)^{-1},\qquad 
abla^2G(y)=(AH^{-1}A^T)^{-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a smooth nondegenerate fiber minimizer, the projected value gradient is the equality multiplier and its Hessian is the inverse projected inverse-Hessian matrix.
assumptions_latex: The fiber minimizer is unique and locally smooth in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla G(y)=\lambda(y)\) and \(
abla^2G(y)=(A
abla^2F(x(y))^{-1}A^T)^{-1}\).

notation.meaning: Hessian of F at the fiber minimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Fiber Optimality and Projected Hessian Formula
Projected Image Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiberwise partial minimization transports a barrier to a linear image under regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a standard \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be surjective, and set \(D=A(C)\). Suppose that, for every \(y\in\operatorname{int}D\), the problem \(G(y)=\inf\{F(x):x\in\operatorname{int}C,\ Ax=y\}\) has a unique minimizer \(x(y)\), with nonsingular second-order restriction along \(\ker A\), and that \(G(y)\to+\infty\) at \(\partial D\). Then \(G\) is a standard self-concordant barrier on \(D\), with \(\nu\) as a valid parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under fiber attainment, nondegeneracy, and boundary coercivity, minimizing a barrier over each affine fiber yields a barrier on the projected feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is surjective and every interior fiber has a unique nondegenerate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(y)=\inf_{Ax=y}F(x)\) is a standard \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(A(C)\).

notation.meaning: linear image of the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits projected-image barriers, but this is a nontrivial partial-minimization theorem. The listed attainment, nondegeneracy, and boundary conditions—and especially preservation of nu—cannot be accepted without an authoritative theorem supporting these exact hypotheses and conclusion.

children.title: Affine Representation Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Loss of regularity caused by deficient or noninjective affine representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Representation Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a positive-definite local metric under a noninjective affine pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noninjective affine representation creates flat directions, making the pullback Hessian singular; quotienting or removing the kernel is required for a standard barrier metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker A\subseteq\ker\nabla^2G(z)\), so \(G\) is not a standard barrier on the unreduced parameter space.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct Hessian degeneracy mechanism for noninjective affine pullbacks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind exactly fits the degeneracy container, and the kernel calculation correctly identifies flat pullback directions. A cited source or inspectable standard reference is still needed for the asserted consequence under the record's chosen definition of a standard barrier.

children.title: Barrier Duality Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Barrier relationships induced by duality and convex conjugacy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel-dual barrier and inverse gradient correspondence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) be finite-dimensional and let \(F:\operatorname{dom}F\to\mathbb R\) be a closed, strictly convex, self-concordant function on an open line-free domain, with \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Legendre-type self-concordant functions and barriers under the standard Fenchel conjugate convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The dual barrier candidate is the Fenchel conjugate \[F^*(s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{dom}F}\{\langle s,xangle-F(x)\},\qquad \operatorname{dom}F^*=
abla F(\operatorname{dom}F).\] For every \(s\in\operatorname{dom}F^*\), the maximizer \(x(s)\) is uniquely determined by \(s=
abla F(x(s))\), and \[
abla F^*(s)=x(s)=(
abla F)^{-1}(s),\qquad 
abla^2F^*(s)=
abla^2F(x(s))^{-1}.\] The conjugate \(F^*\) is self-concordant with the same self-concordance constant as \(F\). These identities define the barrier duality correspondence between primal points, dual gradients, and mutually inverse local Hessian metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier duality associates a smooth strictly convex barrier with its Fenchel conjugate. The dual domain is the gradient image of the primal domain. The primal gradient and dual gradient are inverse maps, and their Hessians are inverse linear operators at corresponding points. Self-concordance is preserved by conjugacy.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is closed, strictly convex, and self-concordant on an open domain containing no line.
For every \(s\) in the conjugate domain, the displayed supremum is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Fenchel conjugacy yields \(s=
abla F(x)\iff x=
abla F^*(s)\) and \(
abla^2F^*(s)=
abla^2F(x)^{-1}\), while preserving self-concordance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At corresponding points, the Fenchel–Young equality is \(F(x)+F^*(s)=\langle s,x\rangle\).
The gradient maps \(\nabla F:\operatorname{dom}F\to\operatorname{dom}F^*\) and \(\nabla F^*\) are mutual inverses.
special_cases_latex: For a logarithmically homogeneous cone barrier, the gradient image is a signed dual-cone interior; changing to the negative-pairing convention places the dual barrier directly on \(\operatorname{int}K^*\).
For \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log x_i\), the conjugate domain is the negative orthant and the coordinate correspondence is \(s_i=-1/x_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Primal and dual local norms are exchanged by the gradient map.
Newton systems at corresponding primal and dual points use inverse Hessian metrics.
Dualizing twice recovers \(F\) under the stated closed Legendre assumptions.
boundary_notes: A general convex function with a nondifferentiable or non-strictly-convex conjugate does not have the stated inverse-gradient correspondence.
For cone barriers, authors often use \(F_*(s)=F^*(-s)\); signs and the dual domain must be adjusted consistently.
Preservation of a particular finite barrier parameter requires the corresponding barrier hypotheses in addition to self-concordance.

source_refs.locator: §5.1, Fenchel dual definition (5.1.30), Lemma 5.1.6, identities (5.1.31)–(5.1.34), and Theorem 5.1.17

children.title: Dual-Domain Barriers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical Self-Dual Cone Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual-domain barriers for the nonnegative orthant and positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) is an \(n\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier and its negative-pairing dual is \(F_*(s)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log s_i-n\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\). For \(K=\mathbb S_+^m\), \(F(X)=-\log\det X\) is an \(m\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier and \(F_*(S)=-\log\det S-m\) on \(\mathbb S_{++}^m\). Additive constants do not affect barrier derivatives or parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the self-dual orthant and semidefinite cones, negative-pairing conjugacy reproduces the logarithmic barrier up to an additive constant.
assumptions_latex: Vector duality uses the Euclidean pairing and matrix duality uses the trace pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_*\) has the same logarithmic form and barrier parameter as \(F\) on these self-dual cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Self-Dual Cone Barriers
Dual-Domain Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel duality for logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barriers on regular cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a regular cone and let \(F\) be a logarithmically homogeneous \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K\). Define \(F_*(s)=\sup_{x\in\operatorname{int}K}\{-\langle s,xangle-F(x)\}\) for \(s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\). Then \(F_*\) is a logarithmically homogeneous \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K^*\). The gradient maps are mutually inverse with negative sign: \(s=-
abla F(x)\) if and only if \(x=-
abla F_*(s)\), and at paired points \(F(x)+F_*(s)=-\langle s,xangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative-pairing conjugate of a logarithmically homogeneous barrier is a barrier on the dual cone, and the two negative-gradient maps invert each other.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is closed, pointed, full-dimensional, and convex.
\(F\) is a logarithmically homogeneous \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(F_*\) is a logarithmically homogeneous \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(K^*\), with \(-
abla F_* = (-
abla F)^{-1}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-Concordance Under Legendre Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of nondegenerate standard self-concordant functions under Fenchel conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a closed Legendre convex function that is \(C^3\) on \(U=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F\), with \(
abla^2F(x)\succ0\), and suppose \(F\) is standard self-concordant on \(U\). Then \(F^*\) is standard self-concordant on \(U^*=
abla F(U)=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F^*\). At \(y=
abla F(x)\), \(
abla^2F^*(y)=
abla^2F(x)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel conjugacy preserves standard self-concordance under Legendre nondegeneracy on the conjugate gradient-image domain.
assumptions_latex: \(F\in C^3(U)\), is standard self-concordant, and has positive-definite Hessian on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*\) is standard self-concordant on \(\nabla F(U)\).

notation.meaning: interior conjugate domain, equal to the primal gradient image

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Concordance Under Legendre Conjugacy
Convex-Conjugate Barrier Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled and linearly shifted Legendre barriers and their conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\operatorname{int}Q\to\mathbb{R}\) be a Legendre convex barrier, let \(a>0\), and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(H(x)=aF(x)+\langle b,x\rangle\), its Fenchel conjugate is
\[
H^*(y)=aF^*\!\left(\frac{y-b}{a}\right),\qquad \operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}H^*=b+a\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F^*.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\nabla H^*(y)=(\nabla F)^{-1}\!\left(\frac{y-b}{a}\right),
\]
and, wherever the Hessians exist and are positive definite,
\[
\nabla^2H^*(y)=\frac1a\left[\nabla^2F\!\left(\nabla H^*(y)\right)\right]^{-1}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling and linearly shifting a Legendre barrier produces a conjugate family whose domains, gradients, and Hessians follow explicit conjugacy transformations.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, strictly convex, essentially smooth, and twice differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H^*(y)=aF^*((y-b)/a)\), with inverse-gradient and inverse-Hessian correspondence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Fenchel conjugacy under positive scaling and linear perturbation is standard convex analysis.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaling, linear-perturbation, domain, gradient, and inverse-Hessian formulas are mathematically plausible and the representation kind fits the family-oriented leaf. No cited source or inspectable locator supports the exact regularity assumptions and formulas, so the record cannot yet be accepted.

children.title: Primal–Dual Barrier Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between primal-domain and dual-domain barriers.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Barrier Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Legendre-gradient correspondence between primal and conjugate barrier coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a Legendre barrier and let \(F^*(y)=\sup_x\{\langle y,x\rangle-F(x)\}\). For interior points \(x\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F\) and \(y\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F^*\), the following statements are equivalent:
\[
y=\nabla F(x),\qquad x=\nabla F^*(y),\qquad F(x)+F^*(y)=\langle x,y\rangle.
\]
At corresponding points, if \(F\) is twice differentiable with positive-definite Hessian, then
\[
\nabla^2F^*(y)=\nabla^2F(x)^{-1},
\]
so the primal and dual local norms satisfy \(\|u\|_x=\|\nabla^2F(x)u\|_{y,*}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The barrier gradient bijectively matches primal and dual interior points; conjugate values satisfy Fenchel equality, and corresponding Hessians are inverses.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is twice differentiable and \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\) for the Hessian identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla F^*=(\nabla F)^{-1}\), with Fenchel equality and inverse Hessians at corresponding points.

notation.meaning: local norm induced by the primal Hessian
dual local norm induced by the conjugate Hessian

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Legendre reciprocity and Fenchel equality are standard convex-conjugacy results.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Legendre reciprocity, Fenchel equality, and inverse-Hessian claims fit the duality container. The convention for the notation \(\|\cdot\|_{y,*}\) must be defined explicitly enough to verify the displayed norm identity, and an authoritative source with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton-Decrement Invariance Under Conjugacy

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=\nabla F(x)\) and \(H=\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\). The proposal identifies \(y^TH^{-1}y\) with the primal Newton decrement and claims this gives invariance of the Newton decrement across the conjugate pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed record claims that conjugacy preserves the Newton decrement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_F(x)=\lambda_{F^*}(y)\).

notation.meaning: Newton decrement of F at x

review_flags: At corresponding points, λ_F(x)^2=y^TH^{-1}y, whereas λ_{F^*}(y)^2=x^THx; these are not generally equal.
The valid Hessian-metric norm identity is already contained in the immutable seed and should not be regenerated.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Legendre Regularity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity conditions supporting global gradient conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proper closed convex function \(F\) with \(U=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F
e\varnothing\), Legendre regularity means essential smoothness and essential strict convexity. In finite dimensions, essential smoothness requires differentiability on \(U\) and \(\|
abla F(x_k)\|	o\infty\) whenever \(x_k\in U\) converges to a boundary point of \(\operatorname{dom}F\); essential strict convexity requires strict convexity on every convex subset of \(\operatorname{dom}\partial F\). If \(F\) is Legendre, then \(F^*\) is Legendre and \(
abla F:U	o\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F^*\) is bijective with inverse \(
abla F^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Essential smoothness and essential strict convexity form the regularity threshold for global inverse-gradient conjugacy.
assumptions_latex: The displayed full-dimensional correspondence assumes the relevant domain interiors are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla F^*=(\nabla F)^{-1}\) on the corresponding domain interiors.
knowledge_statements.title: Legendre Regularity Boundary
Conjugacy Regularity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failures of full-dimensional smooth barrier duality without Legendre regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Strict convexity and essential smoothness delimit the inverse-gradient barrier correspondence. If strict convexity is removed, the convex function \(F(x_1,x_2)=-\log x_1\) on \((0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\) has singular Hessian and
\[
\operatorname{dom}F^*=(-\infty,0)\times\{0\},
\]
which has empty interior in \(\mathbb{R}^2\). If boundary gradient blow-up is removed, \(G(x)=x^2\) on \((-1,1)\) has bounded gradient image \((-2,2)\), while \(G^*\) remains finite outside that image; hence gradient inversion cannot cover \(\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}G^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strict convexity or boundary gradient blow-up, conjugate domains may lose dimension or exceed the gradient image, destroying global primal–dual barrier correspondence.
assumptions_latex: Conjugates are taken after extending each displayed function by \(+\infty\) outside its stated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing Legendre regularity can make \(\nabla F\) noninvertible or non-surjective onto \(\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}F^*\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The displayed conjugates directly exhibit the two regularity failures.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two examples correctly target failures of strict convexity and essential smoothness, and failure_boundary is appropriate for the leaf. A precise source is still needed for the stated Legendre-regularity boundary and its connection to global inverse-gradient correspondence.

Construction-Based Parameter Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter calculus for sums, affine pullbacks, and positive rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_i\) be \(\nu_i\)-self-concordant barriers on convex sets \(Q_i\). On
\[
Q=\{x:A_ix+b_i\in Q_i\text{ for every }i\},
\]
assume \(Q\) has nonempty interior and the summed pullback Hessian is positive definite. Then
\[
F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m F_i(A_ix+b_i)
\]
is a self-concordant barrier with parameter at most \(\sum_{i=1}^m\nu_i\). In particular, an affine pullback does not increase the inherited parameter. If \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier and \(a\ge1\), then \(aF\) is an \(a\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp universal lower bound for a nontrivial standard self-concordant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a convex set with nonempty interior and nonempty boundary, and let \(F\) be a standard \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(C\). Then \(\nu\geq1\). This is sharp because \(F(x)=-\log x\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}\) has minimum parameter \(1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Universal Unit Parameter Lower Bound
Geometric Limits on Barrier Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp parameter lower bound for logarithmically homogeneous barriers on an orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\mathbb{R}_+^n\), and let \(F:\operatorname{int}K\to\mathbb{R}\) be a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier that is logarithmically homogeneous:
\[
F(tx)=F(x)-\nu\log t\qquad(t>0).
\]
Then the geometry of the \(n\) independent extreme rays imposes
\[
\nu\ge n.
\]
The bound is attained by the logarithmic barrier
\[
F_0(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i,
\]
which is an \(n\)-logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier. Thus no logarithmically homogeneous barrier construction can give the orthant a parameter smaller than its dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier on the nonnegative orthant has parameter at least n; the standard logarithmic barrier attains this limit.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\mathbb{R}_+^n\) is treated as a proper cone.
\(F\) is a logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier with the same homogeneity parameter \(\nu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu\ge n\), with equality achieved by \(F_0(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The orthant logarithmic barrier has parameter n; the universal lower bound requires a precise cone-barrier theorem locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthant lower bound is an exact geometric theorem requiring an authoritative theorem-level locator; the supplied rationale only establishes the parameter of the standard logarithmic barrier, not the universal lower bound. The selected complexity_bound kind is also questionable because this is a barrier-parameter lower-bound theorem rather than an algorithmic complexity estimate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Invariance of Dikin Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation law for local barrier norms and ellipsoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable with positive-definite Hessian, let \(T(z)=Mz+q\) with \(M\) nonsingular, and define \(\widetilde F(z)=F(T(z))\). Then \[ \nabla^2\widetilde F(z)=M^T\nabla^2F(T(z))M \] and, for every direction \(u\), \[ \|u\|_{z,\widetilde F}=\|Mu\|_{T(z),F}. \] Consequently, \(T\) maps the radius-\(r\) Dikin ellipsoid of \(\widetilde F\) at \(z\) exactly onto the radius-\(r\) Dikin ellipsoid of \(F\) at \(T(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible affine coordinate changes preserve Dikin lengths and carry Dikin ellipsoids exactly to their transformed counterparts.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is twice differentiable and has positive-definite Hessian on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(E^{\widetilde F}_z(r))=E^F_{T(z)}(r).

notation.meaning: radius-r Dikin ellipsoid induced by F at x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Dikin Ellipsoid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-scaled local Hessian norm for a logarithmic polyhedral barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[ D=\{x:a_i^Tx<b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\qquad s_i(x)=b_i-a_i^Tx, \] let \(F(x)=-\sum_i\log s_i(x)\). Then \[ \nabla^2F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{a_ia_i^T}{s_i(x)^2},\qquad \|h\|_x^2=h^T\nabla^2F(x)h=\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\frac{a_i^Th}{s_i(x)}\right)^2. \] Thus \(\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}\) consists of steps whose vector of relative linearized slack changes has Euclidean norm below one. In particular, \(|a_i^Th|<s_i(x)\) for every \(i\), so every such step remains strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral log barrier, Dikin length is the Euclidean norm of relative slack changes, and unit Dikin steps remain in the strict interior.
assumptions_latex: The barrier is the stated logarithmic barrier.
For a genuine norm, the constraint normals span \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|h\|_x<1\implies a_i^T(x+h)<b_i\quad\text{for every }i.

notation.meaning: barrier Hessian norm of the step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of the Unit Dikin Radius
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional example showing that no universally larger containment radius is possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For F(x)=-\log x on D=(0,\infty), F''(x)=x^{-2} and \|h\|_x=|h|/x. Hence the open radius-r Dikin ellipsoid is ((1-r)x,(1+r)x). It is contained in D for r\leq1, whereas every r>1 gives an interval containing nonpositive points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit Dikin radius is sharp: every universally larger radius fails even for the one-dimensional logarithmic barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r>1\Longrightarrow\{x+h:\|h\|_x<r\}\not\subset D.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Unit Dikin Radius

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar Dikin Ellipsoid and Dual Local Norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation of Hessian-induced local geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H(x)\succ0 and define \|h\|_x=(h^TH(x)h)^{1/2}. Then \|v\|_{x,*}=(v^TH(x)^{-1}v)^{1/2},\qquad \sup_{\|h\|_x\leq1}v^Th=\|v\|_{x,*},\qquad \{h:\|h\|_x\leq1\}^{\circ}=\{v:\|v\|_{x,*}\leq1\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of a Dikin unit ellipsoid is the ellipsoid induced by the inverse Hessian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Definite Curvature Alone Does Not Give Dikin Containment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unit local-ellipsoid containment without a barrier or self-concordance hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(-\tfrac12,\tfrac12)\) and \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^2\). Then \(F''(0)=1>0\), but the unit Hessian ellipsoid at zero is \[E_0(1)=\{h:|h|<1\}=(-1,1),\] which is not contained in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite Hessian alone does not force the unit local ellipsoid to remain in the function's domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F''(0)>0\quad\text{but}\quad E_0(1)\not\subset D.

Dikin Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian ellipsoids and their distortion inside a self-concordant domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a standard self-concordant barrier on an open convex domain \(D\), and define \(\|h\|_x=(h^\top\nabla^2F(x)h)^{1/2}\). For every \(x\in D\), the open Dikin ellipsoid
\[
E_x=\{x+h:\|h\|_x<1\}
\]
is contained in \(D\). Moreover, if \(y=x+h\) and \(r=\|h\|_x<1\), then
\[
(1-r)^2\nabla^2F(x)\preceq\nabla^2F(y)\preceq(1-r)^{-2}\nabla^2F(x).
\]
Consequently, local norms and ellipsoids vary controllably throughout every unit Dikin neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit Hessian ellipsoid at an interior point stays feasible, and the barrier Hessian changes by explicit multiplicative factors inside it.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a standard self-concordant barrier with \(\nabla^2F(x)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_x\subset D\), with the stated two-sided Hessian comparison for \(\|y-x\|_x<1\).

notation.meaning: unit Dikin ellipsoid centered at x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dikin Ellipsoid of a Polyhedral Interior Point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^Tx<b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be full-dimensional, let \(s_i(x)=b_i-a_i^Tx>0\), and assume the vectors \(a_i\) span \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-dimensional polyhedral logarithmic-barrier geometry; equality-constrained versions restrict all matrices and directions to the equality null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[F(x):=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i(x),\qquad H(x):=\nabla^2F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{a_ia_i^T}{s_i(x)^2}.\] The radius-\(r\) Dikin ellipsoid centered at \(x\in P\) is \[E_D(x,r):=\{x+d:d^TH(x)d<r^2\}.\] The associated Dikin distance at the base point is \(\|d\|_x=\sqrt{d^TH(x)d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly feasible point of a polyhedron, scale each constraint normal by the reciprocal slack and sum the resulting rank-one matrices. The positive-definite matrix obtained is the logarithmic-barrier Hessian. Its norm balls, translated to the point, are the Dikin ellipsoids.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[d^TH(x)d=\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\frac{a_i^Td}{s_i(x)}\right)^2.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(r=1\), the open Dikin ellipsoid is contained in \(P\): if \(d^TH(x)d<1\), then \(|a_i^Td|<s_i(x)\) for every \(i\).
With equalities \(Bx=c\), replace \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) by \(d\in\ker B\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The ellipsoid volume is \(\operatorname{vol}(E_D(x,r))=\operatorname{vol}(B_2^n)r^n/\sqrt{\det H(x)}\).
The construction is invariant under nonsingular affine coordinate changes.
boundary_notes: The ellipsoid is open because the polyhedron was written with strict inequalities.
Redundant constraints alter \(H(x)\), so Dikin geometry depends on the chosen inequality representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Damped-Newton Decrease from the Decrement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal progress bound for standard self-concordant minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f be convex and standard self-concordant with 
abla^2f(x)\succ0. Set p_N=-
abla^2f(x)^{-1}
abla f(x) and \lambda=\lambda_f(x). Then y=x+p_N/(1+\lambda) belongs to \operatorname{dom}f and f(y)\leq f(x)-\omega(\lambda),\qquad \omega(t)=t-\log(1+t).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decrement-scaled damped Newton step remains in the domain and decreases a standard self-concordant objective by a universal amount.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Hessian Destroys the Inverse-Hessian Decrement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertibility boundary for inverse-Hessian proximity geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=x^4\), the global minimizer is \(x^*=0\), but \(f''(0)=0\). Consequently, the inverse-Hessian expression \(
abla f(0)^T
abla^2f(0)^{-1}
abla f(0)\) is not defined.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Full-Newton Decrement Recurrence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic regime for full Newton steps on a standard self-concordant objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex and standard self-concordant, suppose \(
abla^2f(x)\succ0\), and set \(x^+=x-
abla^2f(x)^{-1}
abla f(x)\). If \(\lambda_f(x)<1\), then \(x^+\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \[\lambda_f(x^+)\leq\left( rac{\lambda_f(x)}{1-\lambda_f(x)}ight)^2.\] In particular, \(\lambda_f(x)\leq	frac14\) implies \(\lambda_f(x^+)\leq2\lambda_f(x)^2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Newton Decrement as an Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex optimality test supplied by inverse-Hessian decrement geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:D	o\mathbb R\) be differentiable and convex on an open convex set, and suppose \(H(x)=
abla^2f(x)\succ0\). With \(\lambda_f(x)^2=
abla f(x)^TH(x)^{-1}
abla f(x)\), \[\lambda_f(x)=0\iff 
abla f(x)=0.\] Hence \(\lambda_f(x)=0\) certifies that \(x\) is a global minimizer of \(f\); if \(f\) is strictly convex on \(D\), that minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite inverse-Hessian decrement vanishes exactly at stationary points and therefore certifies global optimality for a convex objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on the open convex domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_f(x)=0\iff\nabla f(x)=0\implies x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in D}f(z).

Newton-Decrement Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton decrement as a local optimality radius for self-concordant objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, standard self-concordant, and satisfy \(\nabla^2f(x)\succ0\). Its Newton decrement is
\[
\lambda_f(x)=\bigl(\nabla f(x)^\top\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\nabla f(x)\bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
If \(f\) has a minimizer \(x^*\) and \(\lambda_f(x)<1\), then
\[
\|x-x^*\|_x\le\frac{\lambda_f(x)}{1-\lambda_f(x)},
\qquad
0\le f(x)-f(x^*)\le-\lambda_f(x)-\log(1-\lambda_f(x)).
\]
Thus sublevel sets of the decrement provide barrier-invariant proximity neighborhoods around the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton decrement below one bounds both local distance to the minimizer and objective suboptimality through universal self-concordant formulas.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and standard self-concordant on the open convex set \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lambda_f(x)<1\), then the displayed local-distance and objective-gap bounds hold.

children.title: Analytic-Center Geometry
children.top_down_role: Barrier centers and their role as path anchors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Equivariance of Analytic Centers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate invariance of barrier minimizers under invertible affine transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\), and suppose \(x_{\rm ac}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}F(x)\). For an invertible affine map \(T(z)=Mz+q\), define \(\widetilde D=T^{-1}(D)\) and \(\widetilde F(z)=F(T(z))\). Then \[ \operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\widetilde D}\widetilde F(z)=T^{-1}\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}F(x)\right). \] In particular, when the analytic center is unique, \(\widetilde x_{\rm ac}=M^{-1}(x_{\rm ac}-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine change of coordinates carries the analytic center to the analytic center of the pulled-back barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde x_{\rm ac}=T^{-1}(x_{\rm ac})\quad\text{when the minimizer is unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Equivariance of Analytic Centers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Analytic-Center Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient and Hessian characterization for the logarithmic center of a full-dimensional polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[ D=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^Tx<b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\qquad s_i(x)=b_i-a_i^Tx, \] and define \(F(x)=-\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i(x)\). Then \[ \nabla F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{a_i}{s_i(x)},\qquad \nabla^2F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{a_ia_i^T}{s_i(x)^2}. \] Hence any attained analytic center \(x_{\rm ac}\) satisfies \[ \sum_{i=1}^m\frac{a_i}{b_i-a_i^Tx_{\rm ac}}=0. \] If \(\{a_i\}_{i=1}^m\) spans \(\mathbb R^n\), the Hessian is positive definite throughout \(D\), so an attained stationary point is the unique minimizer of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral logarithmic barrier, the analytic center balances the constraint normals weighted by inverse slack, and its Hessian is the weighted normal Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: For positive definiteness and uniqueness, the normals span \(\mathbb R^n\) and the barrier minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla F(x_{\rm ac})=0,\qquad \nabla^2F(x)=\sum_i\frac{a_ia_i^T}{s_i(x)^2}\succ0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{On }D=(0,\infty),\quad F(x)=-\log x\to+\infty\text{ as }x\downarrow0,\quad\text{but}\quad \inf_{x>0}F(x)=-\infty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier may diverge at its finite boundary yet have no analytic center because its values escape to minus infinity along an unbounded direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}F(x)=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Blow-Up Does Not Ensure Attainment on an Unbounded Domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence on Bounded Barrier Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient attainment and uniqueness conditions for an analytic center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D\subset\mathbb R^n be nonempty, bounded, open, and convex. Let F:D\to\mathbb R be continuous and strictly convex, and suppose F(x_k)\to+\infty whenever x_k\in D approaches \partial D. Then F attains its minimum at a unique point x_{\rm ac}\in D. If F is differentiable, then \nabla F(x_{\rm ac})=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary blow-up on a bounded convex domain guarantees a unique analytic center for a continuous strictly convex barrier.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ is nonempty, bounded, open, and convex}.
F\text{ is continuous and strictly convex}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,x_{\rm ac}\in D:\ F(x_{\rm ac})=\inf_{x\in D}F(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Existence on Bounded Barrier Domains

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic Center as the Zero-Parameter Path Anchor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local anchoring and first variation of a linear-objective barrier path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:D	o\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\), let \(x_{m ac}\in D\) satisfy \(
abla F(x_{m ac})=0\) and \(
abla^2F(x_{m ac})\succ0\), and let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). The equation \(
abla F(x(t))+tc=0\) has a locally unique \(C^1\) solution near \(t=0\), with \[x(0)=x_{m ac},\qquad x'(0)=-
abla^2F(x_{m ac})^{-1}c.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondegenerate analytic center anchors the local linear-objective barrier path at parameter zero, with initial tangent equal to the inverse-Hessian-scaled negative objective vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x(0)=x_{\rm ac},\qquad x'(0)=-\nabla^2F(x_{\rm ac})^{-1}c.

notation.meaning: local barrier path parameterized by t

knowledge_statements.title: Analytic Center as the Zero-Parameter Path Anchor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic Center and First-Order Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-minimizer definition, including the relative affine-slice formulation; Dikin and Newton-decrement geometry are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let D\subset\mathbb R^n be an open convex domain and let F:D\to\mathbb R be a differentiable convex barrier. An analytic center exists when F attains its infimum on D, and any such center satisfies
\[
x_{\rm ac}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}F(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nabla F(x_{\rm ac})=0.
\]
If F is strictly convex, the center is unique. More generally, on the nonempty affine slice C=D\cap\{x:Ax=b\}, a point x_{\rm ac}\in C is a relative analytic center exactly when
\[
\nabla F(x_{\rm ac})+A^Ty=0
\]
for some y; strict convexity on C makes that center unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analytic center is an attained barrier minimizer. For a differentiable convex barrier it is characterized by zero gradient, or by affine-equality KKT stationarity on a relative slice; strict convexity gives uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ is open and convex, and }F:D\to\mathbb R\text{ is differentiable and convex}.
For the unconstrained equivalence, x_{\rm ac}\in D.
For uniqueness, F\text{ is strictly convex on the relevant feasible set}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\rm ac}\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\iff\nabla F(x_{\rm ac})=0,\qquad x_{\rm ac}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}F\iff\exists y:\nabla F(x_{\rm ac})+A^Ty=0.

notation.meaning: analytic center or relative analytic center
convex barrier whose attained minimizer defines the center

knowledge_statements.title: Analytic Center and First-Order Characterization
Analytic-Center Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier minimizer and its Hessian-centered interior neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be an open convex domain and let \(F:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be a strictly convex barrier. An analytic center is a point
\[
x_{m ac}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}F(x).
\]
When it exists, it is unique and satisfies
\[
\nabla F(x_{m ac})=0.
\]
If \(F\) is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian, its local center geometry is represented by the Dikin ellipsoids
\[
E_{x_{m ac}}(r)=\{x_{\rm ac}+h:\|h\|_{x_{m ac}}<r\},\qquad 0<r\le1,
\]
with \(E_{x_{m ac}}(1)\subset D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The analytic center uniquely minimizes a strictly convex barrier; its Hessian defines nested Dikin ellipsoids that form canonical interior neighborhoods.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is open and convex, and \(F\) is a strictly convex barrier attaining its minimum.
For ellipsoid containment, \(F\) is standard self-concordant with positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{\rm ac}\) is the unique zero-gradient barrier minimizer, and \(E_{x_{\rm ac}}(1)\subset D\).

notation.meaning: radius-r Dikin ellipsoid at the analytic center
Hessian norm at the analytic center

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Analytic centers are barrier minimizers and inherit Dikin geometry.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The analytic-center definition, uniqueness under attained strict convex minimization, first-order condition, and associated Dikin neighborhood fit this leaf. The record still lacks an inspectable source for both the definition and the self-concordant ellipsoid-containment property.

children.title: Volumetric-Center Geometry
children.top_down_role: Center families based on local volume and curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Equivariance of Volumetric Centers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate transformation law for the log-determinant curvature objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For T(z)=Mz+q with M nonsingular, let \widetilde H(z)=M^TH(T(z))M and V(x)=\tfrac12\log\det H(x). Then \widetilde V(z)=\tfrac12\log\det\widetilde H(z)=V(T(z))+\log|\det M|. Therefore \operatorname*{argmin}\widetilde V=T^{-1}(\operatorname*{argmin}V).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine change adds only a constant to the volumetric objective and carries volumetric centers equivariantly.
assumptions_latex: H(x)\succ0\text{ on the domain under consideration}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}\widetilde V=T^{-1}(\operatorname*{argmin}V).
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Equivariance of Volumetric Centers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Volumetric Gradient and Leverage Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order geometry of the polyhedral volumetric objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H(x)=\sum_i a_ia_i^T/s_i(x)^2\succ0,\quad V(x)=\tfrac12\log\det H(x),\quad \sigma_i(x)=\frac{a_i^TH(x)^{-1}a_i}{s_i(x)^2}. Then \nabla V(x)=\sum_i\sigma_i(x)\frac{a_i}{s_i(x)},\qquad 0\leq\sigma_i(x)\leq1,\qquad \sum_i\sigma_i(x)=n. Hence an interior stationary point satisfies \sum_i\sigma_i(x)a_i/s_i(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The volumetric gradient balances inverse-slack normals weighted by local leverage scores whose total equals the dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla V(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i(x)}{s_i(x)}a_i=0.

notation.meaning: local leverage score of inequality i

knowledge_statements.title: Volumetric Gradient and Leverage Scores

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Deficiency Makes the Volumetric Objective Singular
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient-span requirement for a finite log-determinant curvature objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(P=\{(x_1,x_2):0<x_1<1\}\) with inequality normals \(a_1=(1,0)^T\) and \(a_2=(-1,0)^T\). For every \(x\in P\), \[H(x)=\frac{a_1a_1^T}{x_1^2}+\frac{a_2a_2^T}{(1-x_1)^2}\] has rank one. Hence \(\det H(x)=0\), and the finite-valued objective \(\tfrac12\log\det H(x)\) is not defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the constraint normals do not span the ambient space, the logarithmic-barrier Hessian is singular and its volumetric log determinant is not finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}H(x)=1<2,\qquad \det H(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Deficiency Makes the Volumetric Objective Singular

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Boundary Growth of the Polyhedral Volumetric Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and first-order sufficiency for a bounded represented polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax<b\}\) be a nonempty bounded full-dimensional polytope with nonzero row normals \(a_i^T\), let \(s_i(x)=b_i-a_i^Tx\), and set \[H(x)=\sum_i\frac{a_ia_i^T}{s_i(x)^2},\qquad V(x)=\frac12\log\det H(x).\] Then \(V\) is convex on \(P\), and \(V(x_j)\to+\infty\) whenever \(x_j\in P\) approaches \(\partial P\). Consequently, \(V\) attains a minimum in \(P\), and every interior point satisfying \(\nabla V(x)=0\) is a global minimizer of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded full-dimensional represented polytope, the volumetric log-determinant objective is convex, diverges at the boundary, attains a minimum, and has globally sufficient stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Every represented inequality has a nonzero normal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}V(x)\ne\varnothing,\qquad \nabla V(x)=0\Longrightarrow x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in P}V(y).
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Boundary Growth of the Polyhedral Volumetric Objective
Volumetric-Center Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral center defined by minimizing logarithmic local ellipsoid volume.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax<b\}
\]
be full-dimensional, with row vectors \(a_i^\top\), slacks \(s_i(x)=b_i-a_i^\top x\), and logarithmic-barrier Hessian
\[
H(x)=\sum_i\frac{a_i a_i^\top}{s_i(x)^2}.
\]
A volumetric center is any minimizer
\[
x_{\rm vc}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}V(x),
\qquad
V(x)=\frac12\log\det H(x).
\]
Since the Dikin ellipsoid associated with \(H(x)\) has volume proportional to \(\det H(x)^{-1/2}\), minimizing \(V\) selects a point whose local Dikin ellipsoid has maximal volume.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polytope's volumetric center minimizes the log determinant of the logarithmic-barrier Hessian, equivalently maximizing the associated local Dikin-ellipsoid volume.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty full-dimensional bounded polytope.
\(H(x)\succ0\) for every \(x\in P\), and the minimum of \(V\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{\rm vc}\) minimizes \(\tfrac12\log\det H(x)\) and maximizes the corresponding Dikin-ellipsoid volume.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The log-determinant definition and ellipsoid-volume identity are standard volumetric-center constructions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The log-determinant definition and inverse-square-root determinant volume relation fit volumetric-center geometry, with definition as an appropriate kind. A precise volumetric-center source is needed to support the convention, attainment assumptions, and equivalence to maximum local ellipsoid volume.
