children.title: Artificial-Variable Constructions
children.top_down_role: Extended formulations introducing temporary variables for initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Artificial-Variable Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single artificial variable producing an interior auxiliary inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given inequalities \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and a domain point \(x^0\), introduce one artificial variable \(a\) and replace the original system by \(g_i(x)-a\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), with auxiliary objective \(\min a\). Any choice \(a^0>\max_i g_i(x^0)\) makes \((x^0,a^0)\) strictly feasible for the auxiliary inequalities. If an auxiliary solution satisfies \(a<0\), its \(x\)-component is strictly feasible for the original system; if it satisfies \(a=0\), the point is only weakly feasible and may lie on the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared artificial variable relaxes every inequality enough to create an auxiliary interior point; driving it below zero recovers strict original feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The same artificial variable relaxes every original inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^0>\max_i g_i(x^0)\Longrightarrow g_i(x^0)-a^0<0\), and \(a<0\Longrightarrow g_i(x)<0\) for all \(i\).

notation.meaning: Initial point in the common constraint domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically consistent and matches artificial-variable constructions, including the strict-feasibility implications. It nevertheless has no supporting citation, and the shared-variable convention and auxiliary objective require an inspectable textbook or algorithm locator.

children.title: Interior-Start Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of usable interior points from auxiliary initialization models.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Start Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of strictly positive primal and dual variables from unrestricted estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given provisional vectors \(\tilde x,\tilde s\in\mathbb R^n\) and constants \(\delta_x,\delta_s>0\), compute shifts \(\gamma_x=\max\{0,-\min_i\tilde x_i+\delta_x\}\) and \(\gamma_s=\max\{0,-\min_i\tilde s_i+\delta_s\}\). Set \(x^0=\tilde x+\gamma_x e\) and \(s^0=\tilde s+\gamma_s e\), retain or recompute a multiplier estimate \(y^0\), and evaluate the resulting primal and dual residuals. Use \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\) as an infeasible interior start, or apply a Phase-I correction if exact feasibility is required. The output satisfies uniform positivity margins independently of the signs of the provisional components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift provisional primal and slack vectors uniformly above zero, then either use the result as an infeasible interior start or restore feasibility separately.
assumptions_latex: \(\tilde x,\tilde s\in\mathbb R^n\) have finite components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^0\geq\delta_x\quad\text{and}\quad s_i^0\geq\delta_s\quad\text{for every}\ i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shift calculation does guarantee the stated componentwise positivity margins and is suitable as an interior-start recovery algorithm. The choice of uniform shifts, treatment of \(y^0\), and suggestion to apply a Phase-I correction are variant-dependent and unsupported by any citation; a precise initialization source is required.

children.title: Feasibility-Diagnosis Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Status information produced when initialization cannot recover a suitable interior start.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Diagnosis Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interprets a globally solved Phase-I model for continuous equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constraints \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\le 0\) on \(x\in X\), define
\[
\rho^*:=\inf\{\rho:\ x\in X,\ \rho\ge0,\ |h_i(x)|\le\rho\ (i=1,\ldots,p),\ g_j(x)\le\rho\ (j=1,\ldots,q)\}.
\]
An attained solution with \(\rho^*=0\) supplies a feasible point. A certified bound \(\rho^*>0\) certifies infeasibility. If only \(\rho^*=0\) is known without attainment, the outcome establishes approximate feasibility but does not necessarily produce a feasible point; an uncertified local Phase-I minimum yields no global feasibility conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero attained Phase-I violation gives feasibility; a certified positive global minimum proves infeasibility. Zero infimum without attainment or a merely local minimum is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(h:X\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(g:X\to\mathbb R^q\) are well defined.
The reported lower bound on \(\rho^*\) is globally valid when infeasibility is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho^*=0\) with attainment yields feasibility, whereas a certified \(\rho^*>0\) yields infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Optimal maximum constraint violation in the Phase-I model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagnosis is mathematically plausible, including the nonattainment and local-minimum boundaries, but no source supports this exact max-violation Phase-I model or the asserted global certificate. The leaf describes outcome classification, so property may fit better than certificate once sourced.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Warm-Start State Reuse for Related Linear Programs
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((A',b',c')\) define a new standard-form LP related to a previously solved problem, and let \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)\) be a stored approximate primal–dual state from the earlier problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start reuse for sequences of related linear programs; positivity and centrality are restored before applying an infeasible-interior method to the new data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reoptimization state-reuse map selects perturbations \(p_x,p_y,p_s\) and defines \[(x^0,y^0,s^0)=(\bar x+p_x,\bar y+p_y,\bar s+p_s)\] subject to \(x^0>0\), \(s^0>0\), and prescribed quality bounds such as \[x_i^0s_i^0\geq\gamma\mu_0\quad\forall i,\qquad \frac{\|(A'x^0-b',\ A'^Ty^0+s^0-c')\|}{\mu_0}\leq C,\] where \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), \(C>0\), and \(\mu_0=(x^0)^Ts^0/n\). A basic perturbation adds small positive values to components of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar s\) at or near zero, with further adjustments permitted to satisfy the centrality and residual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reoptimization warm start takes a stored primal–dual state from a related problem and perturbs it for the new data. Components at or near their lower bound receive positive shifts. Further changes may be made so that the state is sufficiently centered and its new primal and dual residuals are not too large relative to complementarity. The result is then an admissible interior starting point for the new problem, generally in an infeasible-start regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reused state is admissible when it is strictly positive and satisfies the selected centrality and new-data residual bounds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A simple reuse map is \(x^0=\bar x+\delta_xe\), \(y^0=\bar y\), and \(s^0=\bar s+\delta_se\), followed by optional residual corrections.
Cold initialization is recovered when the stored state is ignored and the perturbations are constructed solely from the new data.
special_cases_latex: If the old state already satisfies the new equality systems and is strictly positive and centered, it may be reused without perturbation.
If only an old optimal basis is retained, reuse may instead initialize a simplex reoptimization phase; that case is outside the state map defined here.
immediate_consequences_latex: The warm start belongs to the interior even if the stored approximate solution contains nearly zero components.
The quality conditions make explicit why positivity alone is insufficient for reliable reuse.
boundary_notes: Small changes in problem data can cause large changes in the solution partition, so a warm state may still be far from the new central path.
This definition does not guarantee that warm starting reduces total work.

notation.meaning: Perturbations applied to the stored primal–dual state.

children.title: Warm-Start Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior solutions for related optimization instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuses a strictly interior primal-dual state after a nearby problem-data change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given changed data defining residual map \(F_{\rm new}(z;\mu)\), an old state \(z^{\rm old}=(x^{\rm old},y^{\rm old},s^{\rm old})\), target parameter \(\mu_0>0\), and neighborhood tolerance \(\eta\), choose \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) and a positive centering shift so that \(x^0>0\), \(s^0>0\), and
\[
\|F_{\rm new}(z^0;\mu_0)\|\le \eta\mu_0,
\qquad z^0=z^{\rm ref}+\alpha(z^{\rm old}-z^{\rm ref}).
\]
Starting from \(z^0\), apply the ordinary primal-dual Newton and fraction-to-boundary updates for the new problem. Stop when the prescribed primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity tolerances hold; otherwise discard the warm start when restoration cannot enter the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interpolate and recenter the previous solution into the new problem’s strict-interior neighborhood, then resume ordinary primal-dual iterations or reject the warm start if restoration fails.
assumptions_latex: The old and new problems use compatible primal and dual coordinates.
A strictly interior reference state \(z^{\rm ref}\) is available.
Residual and complementarity tolerances are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a tolerance-satisfying solution of the changed problem or rejection of the reused state.

notation.meaning: Combined primal, multiplier, and slack state.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is an algorithm-specific warm-start restoration scheme rather than a universal interior-point procedure. The residual scaling, interpolation, centering shift, neighborhood, and rejection rule require a source defining the applicable primal-dual method.

children.title: Partial KKT Updating
children.top_down_role: Selective refresh of interior-point system components after model changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial KKT Updating
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updates a previously factorized KKT matrix when reoptimization changes only a low-rank block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the new Newton matrix be \(K_1=K_0+UV^{\mathsf T}\), where a factorization of nonsingular \(K_0\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) is stored and \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{N\times r}\). For a new right-hand side \(q\), solve \(K_0w=q\), \(K_0W=U\), form \(M=I_r+V^{\mathsf T}W\), and, if \(M\) is safely nonsingular, set
\[
\Delta=w-WM^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}w.
\]
Accept \(\Delta\) only if the computed residual \(\|K_1\Delta-q\|\) meets tolerance; otherwise refactorize \(K_1\). Repeat only while rank, conditioning, and residual safeguards remain satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent the changed KKT matrix as a low-rank correction, apply the stored factorization through the Woodbury formula, and refactorize when stability checks fail.
assumptions_latex: The data change has the displayed rank-\(r\) representation.
Linear-system residuals are evaluated in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted vector \(\Delta\) satisfies \(K_1\Delta=q\) to the prescribed numerical tolerance.

notation.meaning: Factors of the low-rank matrix change.

source_refs.locator: 8.5 Stable and Large-scale Linear Programming p. 168

Source support for this exact reoptimization method must be confirmed.

children.title: Interior-State Reuse Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Perturbation regimes where reused iterates lose interiority or useful centrality.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-State Reuse Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when an old primal-dual interior state cannot directly initialize the changed problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a changed problem with cone \(K_{\rm new}\), dual cone \(K_{\rm new}^*\), and neighborhood \(\mathcal N_{\rm new}(\mu,\eta)\), direct state reuse is admissible only if the mapped state satisfies \(x^{\rm old}\in\operatorname{int}K_{\rm new}\), \(s^{\rm old}\in\operatorname{int}K_{\rm new}^*\), and belongs to \(\mathcal N_{\rm new}(\mu_0,\eta)\) for some allowed \(\mu_0>0\). If dimensions or cone faces change incompatibly, a slack becomes nonpositive, or the new residual exceeds the restoration radius, the old state is not a valid interior initialization and must be projected, shifted, restored, or discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse stops being valid when coordinates or cones are incompatible, strict positivity is lost, or the changed residual lies outside the method’s restoration neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm requires strict primal-dual interiority.
A coordinate map from the old state to the new problem is specified.
The method has a defined central-neighborhood or restoration test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of any admissibility test forbids direct initialization by the old state.

notation.meaning: Primal cone of the changed problem.
Permitted primal-dual neighborhood for the changed problem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Strict cone interiority is relevant for strictly feasible methods, but membership in a specified central neighborhood is not universally necessary for every interior-point initialization. A source must identify the algorithm whose restoration radius and reuse tests make these conditions necessary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Complementarity Embedding
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space, with dual cone \(\mathcal C^*\). Let \(Q\) be a skew-adjoint linear map, so \(Q^*=-Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural definition covering linear and conic homogeneous self-dual formulations; concrete problem data determine the cone, skew map, normalization, and recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A homogeneous self-dual embedding is a conic complementarity system \[v=Qu,\qquad u\in\mathcal C,\quad v\in\mathcal C^*,\quad \langle u,v\rangle=0,\] possibly augmented by one normalization equation that removes scaling. Homogeneity means that, before normalization, \((u,v)\) feasible implies \((tu,tv)\) feasible for every \(t\geq0\). Self-duality means that the primal and dual feasibility equations are represented by the same skew-adjoint system. The variables include a nonnegative scale \(\tau\) and certificate variable \(\kappa\), with recovery rules distinguishing \(\tau>0\), which permits rescaling to a primal–dual solution, from \(\kappa>0\), which yields an infeasibility or unboundedness certificate according to the embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous self-dual embedding rewrites a primal–dual optimization pair as one conic complementarity feasibility system governed by a skew-adjoint linear map. Before normalization, every nonnegative scaling of a feasible embedded point is feasible. The same system represents its own dual. Additional scale and certificate variables allow a nonzero solution either to be rescaled into a primal–dual solution or interpreted as a status certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The embedded variables satisfy \(v=Qu\), \(u\in\mathcal C\), \(v\in\mathcal C^*\), and \(\langle u,v\rangle=0\), with homogeneous scaling and a self-dual skew representation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(Q^*=-Q\), \(\langle u,Qu\rangle=0\); hence complementarity is intrinsic when \(v=Qu\).
A normalized HSD formulation intersects the homogeneous solution cone with an affine hyperplane chosen to exclude the zero solution.
special_cases_latex: For \(\mathcal C=\mathbb R_+^q\times\mathbb R^r\), the system becomes a mixed linear complementarity formulation of a linear program.
Initialized HSD formulations add residual-scaling variables so a strictly feasible embedded starting point is known.
immediate_consequences_latex: The zero point is always feasible in the unnormalized homogeneous system, so a normalization or nonzero-start mechanism is needed computationally.
The embedded trajectory can unify optimization and status determination.
boundary_notes: The exact interpretation of \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\) depends on the chosen sign convention and embedding map.
A homogeneous embedding without strict complementarity may not by itself distinguish all pathological statuses.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the embedding cone.
Skew-adjoint operator defining the self-dual linear relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP specialization of a homogeneous self-dual conic feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the linear program as \(\min c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\), with dual variables \(y\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and equation \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\). Its homogeneous self-dual embedding uses \(u=(x,y,\tau)\), \(v=(r,s,\kappa)\), and
\[
v=Qu,
\qquad
Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&A^{\mathsf T}&c\\-A&0&b\\-c^{\mathsf T}&-b^{\mathsf T}&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
subject to \(r=0\), \(y,s,\tau,\kappa\ge0\), plus a nonzero normalization or central-path normalization. Since \(Q^{\mathsf T}=-Q\), the system is self-dual and simultaneously encodes optimal solutions and alternative certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP and its dual are combined with two homogeneous scalars into one skew-symmetric conic feasibility system whose outcomes encode optimality or infeasibility information.
assumptions_latex: The LP is expressed in the displayed inequality-slack convention.
Primal and dual variables are finite-dimensional.
A normalization excludes the zero embedding solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed skew-symmetric system is a homogeneous self-dual embedding of the stated LP pair.

notation.meaning: Dual-equation residual and primal slack components.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplified Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding of a Linear Program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^T\lambda:A^T\lambda+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The simplified homogeneous self-dual embedding for a standard-form linear-programming primal–dual pair; it is homogeneous but lacks a strictly feasible embedded point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(\tau,\kappa\in\mathbb R_+\), \(x,s\in\mathbb R_+^n\), and free \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\). The simplified LP embedding is \[\begin{bmatrix}\kappa\\s\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-c^T&b^T\\c&0&-A^T\\-b&A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\tau\\x\\\lambda\end{bmatrix},\qquad \tau\kappa+x^Ts=0.\] Equivalently, \(\kappa=-c^Tx+b^T\lambda\), \(s=c\tau-A^T\lambda\), and \(Ax=b\tau\), with all complementary variables nonnegative. The coefficient matrix is skew-symmetric, and the system is homogeneous: every nonnegative multiple of a solution is again a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The simplified linear-programming HSD embedding augments the primal variables and dual multipliers with a nonnegative scale and certificate variable. A single skew-symmetric block matrix encodes the scaled primal equality, scaled dual equality with slack, and objective relation. Nonnegative scale–certificate and primal–slack pairs satisfy one complementarity equation. Because all right-hand sides vanish, every nonnegative scaling of an embedded solution is also a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The embedded variables satisfy the displayed skew-symmetric mixed complementarity system with \((\tau,x,\kappa,s)\geq0\) and \(\tau\kappa+x^Ts=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The same system is the self-dual linear program \(\min 0\) subject to \(-c^Tx+b^T\lambda\geq0\), \(c\tau-A^T\lambda\geq0\), \(Ax-b\tau=0\), \(\lambda\) free, and \((\tau,x)\geq0\).
If \(\tau>0\) and \(\kappa=0\), then \((x/\tau,\lambda/\tau,s/\tau)\) satisfies the original primal–dual KKT conditions.
special_cases_latex: A strictly complementary embedded solution with \(\kappa>0\) has \(\tau=0\) and can encode a primal or dual infeasibility certificate through the signs of \(c^Tx\) and \(-b^T\lambda\).
Setting \(\tau=1\) and \(\kappa=0\) embeds any primal–dual optimal solution.
immediate_consequences_latex: The zero vector is an embedded solution.
Skew symmetry gives \(\tau\kappa+x^Ts=0\) for every exact matrix-equation solution, consistently with the explicit complementarity condition.
boundary_notes: The simplified embedding is not strictly feasible; initialized HSD variants add a row and column tied to a chosen positive starting point.
Recovery requires a nonzero embedded solution and depends on whether \(\tau\) or \(\kappa\) is positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Skew-symmetric homogeneous self-dual representation for a primal-dual conic pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), and its dual \(\max -b^{\mathsf T}y\) subject to \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\), \(y\in K^*\), define
\[
Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&A^{\mathsf T}&c\\-A&0&b\\-c^{\mathsf T}&-b^{\mathsf T}&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The homogeneous self-dual system seeks nonzero \(u=(x,y,\tau)\) and \(v=(r,s,\kappa)=Qu\) with \(r=0\), \(y\in K^*\), \(s\in K\), and \(\tau,\kappa\ge0\), together with a normalization. The identity \(Q^{\mathsf T}=-Q\) gives the self-dual embedding structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual conic pair is encoded as a normalized feasibility problem over product cones using a skew-symmetric linear operator and two nonnegative status scalars.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The product-cone feasibility system defined by \(v=Qu\) homogeneously embeds the conic primal-dual pair.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the primal slack cone.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is plausible under the stated sign convention, but the exact product-cone homogeneous self-dual formulation and normalization need an authoritative source. Dimensions and the free-variable component containing x should also be stated explicitly once the formulation is fixed.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homogeneous self-dual conic embedding
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*\), and let \(A:E\to F\), \(b\in F\), and \(c\in E\). Consider \(\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal-dual conic programs; the cited construction is presented for the positive-semidefinite cone and has the same homogeneous algebraic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogeneous conic embedding is the feasibility system in \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\in K\times F\times K^*\times\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R_+\): \[Ax-b\tau=0,\qquad A^*y+s-c\tau=0,\qquad -\langle c,x\rangle+\langle b,y\rangle-\kappa=0.\] A self-dual embedding augments this homogeneous system, if necessary, by initialization variables so that its primal and dual formulations coincide up to renaming and it possesses a known strictly interior starting point. The scalars \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\) separate solution and certificate outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous self-dual conic embedding places the primal and dual conic systems in one homogeneous feasibility problem. Its variables satisfy \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), \(\tau,\kappa\geq0\), \(Ax=b\tau\), \(A^*y+s=c\tau\), and \(-\langle c,x\rangle+\langle b,y\rangle=\kappa\). Extended self-dual versions add variables that provide a known interior starting point without changing the status information represented by \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal H(A,b,c,K):=\{(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa):x\in K,\ s\in K^*,\ \tau,\kappa\geq0,\ Ax=b\tau,\ A^*y+s=c\tau,\ -\langle c,x\rangle+\langle b,y\rangle=\kappa\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\), cone membership becomes \(X\succeq0\) and \(S\succeq0\), and the equations are the homogeneous semidefinite embedding equations.
The linear equations can be collected into a skew-adjoint block operator after a consistent sign choice for the dual variable; this operator form explains the term self-dual.
special_cases_latex: When \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), the construction is the homogeneous embedding of a linear program.
When \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\), it is a homogeneous semidefinite-programming embedding.
immediate_consequences_latex: If an embedding solution has \(\tau>0\), division of \((x,y,s)\) by \(\tau\) produces primal and dual feasible points.
If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the homogeneous variables encode an improving-ray certificate rather than a finite primal-dual solution.
boundary_notes: The unextended homogeneous system need not have a known strictly interior feasible point; extended self-dual embeddings address initialization.
The case \(\tau=\kappa=0\) does not by itself identify a unique primal-dual status.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the closed convex cone K.
Adjoint of the linear map A.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homogeneous self-dual embedding for conic linear programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded HSD conic formulation. The extract's final sentence conflates feasible points with strictly interior feasible points, so no equality between those sets is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\mathbf X^0\in\operatorname{int}K\) and \(\mathbf S^0\in\operatorname{int}K^*\) forming a central-path pair with \(\mu=1\), and define
\[
\bar{\mathbf b}=\mathbf b-\mathcal A\mathbf X^0,\qquad \bar{\mathbf C}=\mathbf C-\mathbf S^0,\qquad \bar z=\mathbf C\bullet\mathbf X^0+1.
\]
The homogeneous self-dual conic program is
\[
\min\ (n+1)\theta
\]
subject to
\[
\mathcal A\mathbf X-\mathbf b\tau+\bar{\mathbf b}\theta=0,
\]
\[
-\mathcal A^T\mathbf y+\mathbf C\tau-\bar{\mathbf C}\theta=\mathbf S\in K^*,
\]
\[
\mathbf b^T\mathbf y-\mathbf C\bullet\mathbf X+\bar z\theta=\kappa\geq0,
\]
\[
-\bar{\mathbf b}^T\mathbf y+\bar{\mathbf C}\bullet\mathbf X-\bar z\tau=-(n+1),
\]
with \(\mathbf y,\theta\) free, \(\mathbf X\in K\), and \(\tau\geq0\). Strictly interior feasible points additionally have \(\mathbf X\in\operatorname{int}K\), \(\tau>0\), \(\mathbf S\in\operatorname{int}K^*\), and \(\kappa>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior central-path points of a cone and its dual define residual shifts for a homogeneous self-dual conic program. They need not satisfy the original affine constraints. Strict interior feasibility requires interior cone membership and positive tau and kappa.
assumptions_latex: (\mathbf X^0,\mathbf S^0)\text{ forms a central-path pair with }\mu=1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{HSDCLP}\text{ is the displayed conic program with }\mathbf y,\theta\text{ free},\ \mathbf X\in K,\ \tau\geq0,\ \mathbf S\in K^*,\ \kappa\geq0

children.title: Optimality Recovery from Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Recovery of primal-dual solutions from successful embedding outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Recovery from Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery rule for a homogeneous embedding outcome with positive homogenizing scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the conic embedding with \(v=Qu\), \(u=(x,y,\tau)\), \(v=(0,s,\kappa)\), and the sign convention of the conic-embedding record. If an embedding solution satisfies \(\tau>0\) and \(\kappa=0\), then
\[
\widehat x=x/\tau,
\qquad
\widehat y=y/\tau,
\qquad
\widehat s=s/\tau
\]
satisfy \(A\widehat x+\widehat s=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+c=0\), \(\widehat s\in K\), and \(\widehat y\in K^*\). Moreover \(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat x+b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=0\); hence the recovered primal and dual points are optimal whenever weak duality applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the embedding returns positive homogenization and zero certificate scalar, divide primal, dual, and slack variables by the homogenizing scalar to recover an optimal primal-dual pair.
assumptions_latex: The embedding uses the stated conic sign convention.
Weak duality holds for the primal-dual conic pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\widehat x,\widehat s)\) and \(\widehat y\) are primal-dual feasible with zero duality gap and are therefore optimal.

notation.meaning: Dehomogenized primal, dual, and slack variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dehomogenization rule follows algebraically from the proposed embedding, but that embedding and its sign convention remain unsupported. An authoritative HSD source must confirm the conditions under which tau>0 and kappa=0 yield the stated feasible zero-gap pair.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual optimality recovery map
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Use the primal-dual conic pair and homogeneous embedding variables \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) with \(x\in K\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\tau,\kappa\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery from a successful finite-dimensional embedding outcome with a strictly positive homogenizing scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Optimality recovery is the partial map \[\mathcal R(x,y,s,\tau,\kappa):=(\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)=\left(\frac{x}{\tau},\frac{y}{\tau},\frac{s}{\tau}\right),\qquad \tau>0.\] For an exact embedding solution, the homogeneous equations imply \(A\bar x=b\) and \(A^*\bar y+\bar s=c\). Moreover, nonnegativity and the embedding gap equation force \(\kappa=0\), so \(\langle c,\bar x\rangle=\langle b,\bar y\rangle\) and \(\langle\bar x,\bar s\rangle=0\). Thus the recovered pair is primal-dual feasible and optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimality recovery map is defined only when the embedding scale satisfies \(\tau>0\). It divides the embedded primal variable, dual variable, and dual slack by \(\tau\). The resulting variables satisfy the original primal and dual constraints. For an exact embedding solution the certificate scalar is zero, the duality gap is zero, and the recovered primal and dual points are complementary optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\tau>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (\bar x,\bar y,\bar s)=\left(x/\tau,y/\tau,s/\tau\right),\quad A\bar x=b,\quad A^*\bar y+\bar s=c,\quad \langle c,\bar x\rangle-\langle b,\bar y\rangle=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Recovery is projective: every positive rescaling of \((x,y,s,\tau,\kappa)\) gives the same recovered triple.
For semidefinite programming, \(\bar X=X/\tau\) and \(\bar S=S/\tau\) are complementary when \(\bar X\bar S=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), recovery yields the usual primal and dual linear-programming solutions.
For a maximally complementary embedding solution, the recovered solution is maximally complementary for the original pair.
immediate_consequences_latex: Weak duality plus zero recovered gap certifies global optimality without an additional optimization solve.
The recovery map is undefined at \(\tau=0\); such an outcome must be interpreted through the status-certificate system.
boundary_notes: A small positive numerical value of \(\tau\) can amplify residuals under division, so approximate recovery requires scaled residual tests.
Positive \(\tau\) recovers a complementary pair only from an embedding point satisfying the exact embedding equations and cone memberships.

notation.meaning: Recovered primal variable, dual variable, and dual slack.

children.title: Embedding Status Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Status certificates derived from embedding solutions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Embedding outcome certificate classification
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(w^*=(x^*,y^*,s^*,\tau^*,\kappa^*)\) be an exact maximally complementary solution of a homogeneous self-dual embedding, with \(\tau^*,\kappa^*\geq0\) and \(\tau^*\kappa^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact status classification for maximally complementary embedding solutions; numerical thresholding is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The embedding status certificate is the trichotomy \[\operatorname{status}(w^*)=\begin{cases}\mathrm{OPTIMAL},&\tau^*>0,\\ \mathrm{IMPROVING\_RAY},&\tau^*=0,\ \kappa^*>0,\\ \mathrm{UNRESOLVED},&\tau^*=\kappa^*=0.\end{cases}\] In the first case, division by \(\tau^*\) recovers a complementary primal-dual optimal pair. In the second, the zero-homogenization equations yield a nonzero primal or dual improving ray after normalization by \(\kappa^*\). The third case certifies only that neither of the first two alternatives occurs for a maximally complementary solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact maximally complementary embedding solution has one of three statuses. A positive homogenizing scalar gives an optimal primal-dual solution. A zero homogenizing scalar and positive certificate scalar give a primal or dual improving ray. If both status scalars vanish, the basic embedding reports an unresolved boundary status rather than optimality or strong infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\tau^*>0)\ \dot\cup\ (\tau^*=0,\kappa^*>0)\ \dot\cup\ (\tau^*=\kappa^*=0)\] is the exact embedding-status partition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With the semidefinite embedding notation of the cited source, the certificate scalar \(\kappa\) is denoted \(\rho\).
Maximal complementarity makes positivity of a status scalar existentially decisive: if an optimal embedding solution can have that scalar positive, a maximally complementary solution does.
special_cases_latex: A normalized improving-ray certificate may satisfy \(A^*y+s=0\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(\langle b,y\rangle=1\), certifying primal infeasibility.
Alternatively it may satisfy \(Ax=0\), \(x\in K\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle=-1\), certifying dual infeasibility or primal unboundedness.
immediate_consequences_latex: The statuses \(\mathrm{OPTIMAL}\) and \(\mathrm{IMPROVING\_RAY}\) are mutually exclusive because \(\tau^*\kappa^*=0\).
The unresolved status requires additional facial, asymptotic, or extended-dual analysis.
boundary_notes: The classification does not prescribe numerical tolerances for deciding whether a computed scalar is zero.
Without maximal complementarity, a particular optimal embedding solution with zero status scalars may fail to expose a positive scalar available elsewhere on the optimal face.

children.title: Primal Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Embedding outcomes supporting a primal infeasibility status.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable sufficient certificate for infeasibility of a finite-dimensional primal affine-cone system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone. For the primal system \(Ax+s=b\) with \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(s\in K\), any vector \(y\in K^*\) satisfying
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y=0,
\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0
\]
is a certificate that the primal system is infeasible. Verification consists of testing \(y\in K^*\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional affine-cone system, a dual-cone vector orthogonal to the columns of the constraint matrix and having negative pairing with the right-hand side certifies primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of such a vector \(y\) implies \(\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times K:Ax+s=b\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the primal slack cone.

children.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable sufficient certificate excluding feasibility of a finite-dimensional dual conic equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone. For the dual system \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\) with \(y\in K^*\), any vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying
\[
-Ad\in K,
\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d<0
\]
is a certificate that the dual system is infeasible. Verification consists of one matrix-vector product, the cone-membership test \(-Ad\in K\), and the strict inequality \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional conic dual system, a direction whose negative constraint image lies in the primal cone and whose objective pairing is negative certifies dual infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
The dual convention is \(A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\) with \(y\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of such a vector \(d\) implies \(\{y\in K^*:A^{\mathsf T}y+c=0\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone associated with the primal cone.

children.title: Unboundedness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Embedding outcomes supporting unbounded primal or dual behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-ray certificate for unboundedness below of a finite-dimensional conic minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a convex cone. Consider
\[
\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax+s=b,\ x\in\mathbb R^n,\ s\in K\}.
\]
If \((x^0,s^0)\in\mathbb R^n\times K\) satisfies \(Ax^0+s^0=b\) and a vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(-Ad\in K\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then the pair \(((x^0,s^0),d)\) certifies that the problem is unbounded below. The associated feasible ray is
\[
x(t)=x^0+td,
\qquad s(t)=s^0+t(-Ad),
\qquad t\ge0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point together with a cone-preserving recession direction having negative objective slope certifies that the finite-dimensional conic minimization problem is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax+s=b,\ x\in\mathbb R^n,\ s\in K\}=-\infty\).

children.title: Certificate-Separation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where infeasibility and unboundedness statuses are difficult to distinguish robustly.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Separation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates strict finite certificates from weak or nonclosed conic infeasibility phenomena.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine-cone system \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), strict separation by a certificate \(y\in K^*\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) is guaranteed when the set \(A\mathbb R^n+K\) is closed and does not contain \(b\). If \(b\notin A\mathbb R^n+K\) but \(b\in\operatorname{cl}(A\mathbb R^n+K)\), the system is weakly infeasible: its distance to feasibility is zero, and no certificate having the strict displayed inequality exists. Hence certificate absence alone does not establish feasibility without an applicable closedness or strong-alternative condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict certificates characterize infeasibility under a closed-image condition; weak infeasibility at zero distance may admit no strict finite separating certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
The feasibility set is represented by membership of \(b\) in \(A\mathbb R^n+K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(b\in\operatorname{cl}(A\mathbb R^n+K)\setminus(A\mathbb R^n+K)\), strict certificate separation fails.

notation.meaning: Set of right-hand sides attainable by the affine-cone system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed-image versus weak-infeasibility distinction is mathematically plausible and failure_boundary is the correct kind, but this nontrivial conic separation claim requires an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Embedding Status Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Embedding outcomes near weak infeasibility or unresolved status.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unresolved embedding-status boundary
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(w^*\) be a maximally complementary solution of a self-dual embedding for a primal-dual conic pair, and let \(\tau^*\) and \(\kappa^*\) be its homogenizing and improving-ray scalars.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conic status boundary, emphasizing semidefinite programs where weak infeasibility and nonattainment can occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The embedding status failure boundary is \[\mathcal B_{\mathrm{emb}}:=\{w^*:w^*\text{ is maximally complementary and }\tau^*=\kappa^*=0\}.\] Membership means that the embedding yields neither a recoverable complementary pair nor a strong improving-ray certificate. For semidefinite conic pairs this boundary contains at least three distinct regimes: both problems are solvable with a positive duality gap; one or both problems are weakly infeasible; or both are feasible but at least one finite optimum is not attained. Weak primal infeasibility means the primal feasible set is empty while its affine equations admit cone points with arbitrarily small residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The embedding status failure boundary consists of maximally complementary embedding solutions for which both status scalars are zero. Such an outcome supplies neither an optimality recovery scale nor an improving-ray certificate. In semidefinite programming it can represent a positive duality gap, weak infeasibility, or failure of attainment, so the basic embedding status alone cannot distinguish these cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[w^*\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{emb}}\iff \tau^*=0\ \text{and}\ \kappa^*=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an affine conic system \(\mathcal A x=b\), \(x\in K\), weak infeasibility is \(\{x\in K:\mathcal A x=b\}=\varnothing\) together with \(\inf_{x\in K}\|\mathcal A x-b\|=0\).
Strong infeasibility is excluded at this boundary when an improving ray would force a positive certificate scalar in a maximally complementary embedding solution.
special_cases_latex: For linear programming, every infeasible system is strongly infeasible under the standard closed polyhedral formulation, so the weak-infeasibility component is absent.
For semidefinite programming, nonclosed linear images of \(\mathbb S_+^n\) permit weak infeasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: A solver should report an indeterminate or unresolved status rather than infer infeasibility solely from \(\tau\approx0\).
Resolving the boundary can require facial reduction, extended duals, asymptotically improving rays, or perturbation analysis.
boundary_notes: This definition concerns exact zero scalars; finite-precision near-zero values can also arise from ordinary ill-conditioning.
The boundary is a union of mathematically different pathologies and is not itself an infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: Distance of the affine equations from conic feasibility.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5, Definition 5.2.3, Theorem 5.3.2(iii), and §5.8 Remaining Duality and Feasibility Issues

children.title: Ambiguous Status Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Embedding solutions that do not support a decisive optimization status.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Status Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies embedding limits that yield neither recoverable optimality nor a strict infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a normalized homogeneous self-dual embedding produce a limiting state with status scalars \(\tau,\kappa\ge0\). The outcome is status-ambiguous when \(\tau=\kappa=0\), or numerically when both are below their reliability thresholds, because division by \(\tau\) cannot recover a primal-dual solution and normalization by \(\kappa\) cannot produce a strict alternative certificate. Such an outcome may arise from weak infeasibility, ill-posed data, nonattainment, or finite-precision stagnation. It must be reported as indeterminate unless independent residual, separation, or conditioning tests establish a stronger status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If both embedding status scalars vanish or are numerically unreliable, neither solution recovery nor strict certificate recovery is justified; the result remains indeterminate pending independent tests.
assumptions_latex: The embedding assigns solution recovery to \(\tau>0\) and certificate recovery to \(\kappa>0\).
Numerical reliability thresholds are fixed before status classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau=\kappa=0\), or simultaneous numerical insignificance, does not by itself certify optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.

notation.meaning: Embedding scalar used for solution dehomogenization.
Embedding scalar used for certificate normalization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-status warning fits the failure-boundary leaf, but the interpretation of tau and kappa depends on the exact normalized HSD formulation. The asserted causes and numerical reliability classification also require authoritative, algorithm-specific support.

children.title: Weak Infeasibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Near-feasible regimes lacking robust separation certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Infeasibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic feasibility, emphasizing the absence of finite separating certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the primal feasibility system be \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), where \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex cone. It is weakly infeasible when \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\) but \(\inf_{x\in K}\|Ax-b\|=0\). Equivalently, infeasibility holds while the affine set \(\{x:Ax=b\}\) has zero distance from \(K\). In this regime no vector \(y\) can satisfy simultaneously \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\); hence a homogeneous self-dual embedding need not converge to a nonzero strict infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak infeasibility means the conic system has no feasible point but can approach feasibility arbitrarily closely, so no strict finite separating certificate exists.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\), \(\inf_{x\in K}\|Ax-b\|=0\), and no \(y\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\), \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\).

notation.meaning: Transpose of the linear map A.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weak-infeasibility characterization is standard for finite-dimensional conic feasibility, but the claim about homogeneous self-dual embedding behavior requires an inspectable conic-embedding source. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Ill-Posed Embedding Limits
children.top_down_role: Embedding behavior near boundaries between optimization statuses.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Posed Embedding Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for homogeneous self-dual embeddings of finite-dimensional conic systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=(A,b,c)\) denote conic-program data and let \(\Sigma\) be the set of data lying on the boundary between instances having a strict primal-dual solution or strict infeasibility certificate. Define \(\rho(d)=\inf_{\tilde d\in\Sigma}\|d-\tilde d\|\). If \(\rho(d)=0\), arbitrarily small perturbations can change the status represented by the homogeneous self-dual embedding. Consequently, no finite residual threshold can uniformly distinguish feasibility, infeasibility, and limiting ambiguous behavior over all perturbations of such data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero distance from the status boundary, arbitrarily small data changes can alter the embedding outcome, so residual thresholds cannot uniformly identify status.
assumptions_latex: \(d=(A,b,c)\) belongs to a finite-dimensional normed data space.
\(\Sigma\) is the boundary of the well-posed status regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(d)=0\) implies that embedding status is not locally stable under data perturbations.

notation.meaning: Ill-posed status boundary in data space.
Distance from d to the ill-posed set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definitions of the status regions and ill-posed set are not formal enough to validate the perturbation and uniform-residual-threshold conclusions. An embedding-specific conditioning source is required.

children.title: Numerical Status Indeterminacy
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision regimes producing unresolved or unstable status classifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Status Indeterminacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision termination boundary for homogeneous self-dual embedding iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an embedding iterate producing normalized primal residual \(r_p\), dual residual \(r_d\), gap residual \(r_g\), and candidate certificate margins \(m_p,m_d\). Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_c>0\), status is numerically indeterminate whenever \(\max\{r_p,r_d,r_g\}>\varepsilon_f\) and \(\max\{m_p,m_d\}<\varepsilon_c\). Then neither approximate primal-dual feasibility nor a numerically separated primal or dual infeasibility certificate has been verified; returning a definite status requires additional iterations, rescaling, tighter arithmetic, or external validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Status is indeterminate when feasibility residuals remain too large while every candidate infeasibility certificate has too little numerical separation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{r_p,r_d,r_g\}>\varepsilon_f\) and \(\max\{m_p,m_d\}<\varepsilon_c\) certify neither approximate feasibility nor numerical infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Normalized primal, dual, and gap residuals.
Numerical separation margins of candidate infeasibility certificates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual normalizations, certificate margins, and tolerance logic depend on a particular homogeneous self-dual embedding and solver status convention. Without those definitions or a source, the displayed inequalities cannot serve as a general status boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear-programming barrier algorithm
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\geq0\), where \(f,c_E,c_I\) are twice continuously differentiable on an open subset of \(\mathbb R^n\). Introduce \(s>0\) through \(c_I(x)-s=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming, including nonconvex problems; globalization and curvature safeguards are part of the algorithm class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An NLP barrier algorithm is an iteration producing \((x_k,s_k,y_k,z_k,\mu_k)\) with \(s_k>0\), \(z_k>0\), \(\mu_k>0\), and \(\mu_k\to0\), whose step is computed from either a Newton linearization or a trust-region model of the perturbed KKT residual \[F_{\mu}(x,s,y,z)=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla f(x)-A_E(x)^Ty-A_I(x)^Tz\\ Sz-\mu e\\ c_E(x)\\ c_I(x)-s\end{bmatrix}.\] Accepted steps preserve strict positivity and satisfy a specified globalization test, such as merit-function decrease, filter acceptability, or an actual-to-predicted reduction condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-programming barrier algorithm maintains positive inequality slacks and multipliers while driving a positive barrier parameter to zero. At each iteration it computes a Newton-type or trust-region step for the perturbed KKT equations, restricts the step so the slack and multiplier variables remain positive, and accepts the trial point only through a globalization test. The resulting class includes line-search primal-dual and trust-region barrier methods for smooth, possibly nonconvex nonlinear programs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k>0,\quad z_k>0,\quad \mu_k\downarrow0,\quad d_k\ \text{models or linearizes}\ F_{\mu_k}=0,\quad (x_{k+1},s_{k+1},y_{k+1},z_{k+1})=(x_k,s_k,y_k,z_k)+\alpha_kd_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The continuation interpretation approximately solves \(F_{\mu_k}=0\) for decreasing \(\mu_k\).
The barrier interpretation approximately solves \(\min_{x,s}\ f(x)-\mu_k\sum_i\log s_i\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)-s=0\).
special_cases_latex: A line-search method solves a primal-dual Newton system and shortens the step using a fraction-to-the-boundary rule.
A trust-region method approximately minimizes a quadratic barrier model in a scaled region.
immediate_consequences_latex: At \(\mu>0\), perturbed complementarity \(s_i z_i=\mu\) keeps every slack and multiplier strictly positive.
Nonconvexity requires globalization or curvature handling; the raw Newton iteration alone does not define a practical global method.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert convergence without regularity, boundedness, accuracy, and globalization assumptions.
Nonsmooth constraints and infinite-dimensional problems require different formulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual barrier algorithm with residual and curvature stopping tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded outer algorithm using Algorithm 13.6.1; this algorithm statement prescribes a stopping rule but does not itself prove that the inner rule is attained finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given x_0>0,\ z_0>0,\ \mu_0>0 and forcing functions \epsilon^{\mathrm D},\epsilon^{\mathrm E},\epsilon^{\mathrm C}, set k=0. For each k, choose \varsigma_k\in(0,1) and approximately minimize \phi^{\log}(x,\mu_k)=f(x)-\mu_k\langle e,\log x\rangle using Algorithm\ 13.6.1. Stop the inner iteration at the first (x_{k+1},z_{k+1}) satisfying \|\nabla f(x_{k+1})-z_{k+1}\|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm D}(\mu_k),\ \|X_{k+1}Z_{k+1}-\mu_k I\|\le\epsilon^{\mathrm C}(\mu_k),\ \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x_{k+1})+X_{k+1}^{-1}Z_{k+1})\ge-\epsilon^{\mathrm E}(\mu_k),\ x_{k+1}>0,\ z_{k+1}>0. Choose \mu_{k+1}>0 so that \lim_{k\to\infty}\mu_k=0, increment k, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each outer iteration, run the primal-dual inner algorithm for the current log-barrier objective and accept the first inner iterate satisfying the dual-residual, complementarity-residual, curvature, and strict-positivity tests. Then choose a positive barrier parameter so that the barrier-parameter sequence tends to zero.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The outer sequence is generated by the stated inner stopping rule and by positive updates }\mu_{k+1}\text{ satisfying }\lim_{k\to\infty}\mu_k=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent NLP barrier representations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c_E:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(c_I:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be smooth, and consider \(c_E(x)=0\), \(c_I(x)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programs with equalities and inequalities represented by positive slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An NLP barrier representation at parameter \(\mu>0\) is any of the equivalent exact systems obtained from \[\min_{x,s>0}\ f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_E(x)=0,\quad c_I(x)-s=0.\] Its primal first-order representation uses \(z=\mu S^{-1}e\). Its primal-dual representation treats \(z>0\) independently and imposes \[\nabla f-A_E^Ty-A_I^Tz=0,\quad c_E=0,\quad c_I-s=0,\quad Sz=\mu e.\] Variable bounds are included by affine components of \(c_I\), and equality constraints remain unbarriered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NLP barrier representation rewrites every inequality with a positive slack and adds a logarithmic barrier for those slacks while retaining equality constraints explicitly. The primal representation eliminates the inequality multipliers using \(z_i=\mu/s_i\). The primal-dual representation keeps the multipliers and replaces this quotient relation by the perturbed complementarity equations \(s_i z_i=\mu\). These representations have the same exact positive solutions for fixed \(\mu\), although Newton steps formed from them can differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[z=\mu S^{-1}e\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Sz=\mu e\qquad(s>0),\] together with stationarity and the equality and slack equations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating \(s\) gives the primal barrier \(f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log c_{I,i}(x)\) on \(c_I(x)>0\).
Retaining \((s,z)\) gives a polynomial complementarity block whose derivatives remain bounded as individual slacks approach zero.
special_cases_latex: For lower bounds \(x_i\geq l_i\), use slacks \(s_i^L=x_i-l_i\).
For upper bounds \(x_i\leq u_i\), use slacks \(s_i^U=u_i-x_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: At every exact barrier point, \(s_i z_i=\mu>0\), hence \(s_i>0\) and \(z_i>0\).
Eliminating multipliers before linearization yields a primal Newton system; linearizing the coupled equations yields a primal-dual system.
boundary_notes: Equivalence is at the level of exact positive solutions, not necessarily at the level of Newton iterates.
Equalities cannot receive a logarithmic barrier because they have no open feasible side.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slack-variable and logarithmic-barrier representation of inequality constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack reformulation of nonnegative nonlinear inequalities followed by a logarithmic barrier on the slack bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x F(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)\ge 0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Introducing \(w_i\ge 0\) gives the equivalent slack formulation \[\min_{x,w}F(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x)-w_i=0,\quad w_i\ge0,\quad i=1,\ldots,m.\] For \(r>0\), replacing the slack bounds by a logarithmic barrier yields \[\min_{x,w}F(x)-r\sum_{i=1}^m\log(w_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x)-w_i=0,\quad i=1,\ldots,m,\] whose logarithmic terms restrict the domain to \(w_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each constraint c_i(x) ≥ 0 can be represented by c_i(x)−w_i=0 with a nonnegative slack. A positive-parameter logarithmic barrier on the slack bounds produces the equality-constrained B-NLP model and requires strictly positive slacks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:c_i(x)\ge0\ \forall i\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,w):c_i(x)-w_i=0,\ w_i\ge0\ \forall i\},\quad\text{and B-NLP uses }F(x)-r\sum_{i=1}^m\log(w_i)\text{ on }w_i>0.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Log-Barrier NLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth inequality-constrained NLP represented by a primal logarithmic barrier subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). For the nonlinear program \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g_i(x)\ge 0\), the primal log-barrier problem with \(\mu>0\) is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\phi_\mu(x):=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log g_i(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\quad g_i(x)>0\ \text{for all }i.\] With \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\), its first-order equations are \(\nabla f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\nabla g_i(x)/g_i(x)+J_h(x)^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(h(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The logarithmic barrier moves the original nonnegative inequality constraints into the objective on their strict interior, while retaining the equality constraints explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(h\), and every \(g_i\) are continuously differentiable on an open set containing the barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_\mu(x)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log g_i(x)\) represents the inequality constraints on their strict interior while \(h(x)=0\) remains explicit.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality map h.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal logarithmic-barrier nonlinear program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f,c_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) be smooth. The original problem is \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional primal barrier subproblems; convexity is not required for the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), the primal log-barrier NLP is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal D}\ \Phi_\mu(x):=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log c_i(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\] where \(\mathcal D:=\{x:c_i(x)>0\ \forall i\}\). A primal barrier method computes exact or approximate stationary points \(x(\mu_k)\) for a sequence \(\mu_k\downarrow0\). The induced multiplier estimate is \(z_i(\mu)=\mu/c_i(x(\mu))>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal logarithmic-barrier problem replaces each inequality by the term \(-\mu\log c_i(x)\) and restricts its domain to points satisfying every inequality strictly. Equality constraints remain explicit. A primal barrier method solves a sequence of these smooth equality-constrained problems as the positive parameter \(\mu\) tends to zero. The natural inequality-multiplier estimate is \(z_i=\mu/c_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi_\mu(x)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log c_i(x),\qquad \operatorname{dom}\Phi_\mu=\{x:c_i(x)>0\ \forall i\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing \(s=c(x)>0\) gives \(\min f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log s_i\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)-s=0\).
Writing inequalities as \(f_i(x)\leq0\) gives the equivalent barrier \(-\mu\sum_i\log(-f_i(x))\).
special_cases_latex: For affine inequalities, the barrier is a sum of logarithms of affine slacks.
With no equality constraints, each barrier subproblem is unconstrained on its open domain.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(\Phi_\mu(x)\to+\infty\) when any positive slack approaches zero from above.
At a stationary barrier point, \(c_i(x)z_i=\mu\), which is perturbed complementarity.
boundary_notes: The definition requires a nonempty strict interior to use a feasible primal iteration.
For nonconvex data, a barrier subproblem can have multiple stationary points and need not yield a global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistently active subsequences and asymptotically active bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition and associated activity-pattern facts used in the convergence analysis of nonnegative primal log-barrier iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{x_{k_j}\}\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\). It is consistently active with respect to \(x\geq0\) if, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), either \[\lim_{j\to\infty}[x_{k_j}]_i=0\qquad\text{or}\qquad\liminf_{j\to\infty}[x_{k_j}]_i>0.\] Its asymptotically active set is \[\mathcal A\{x_{k_j}\}:=\left\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:\lim_{j\to\infty}[x_{k_j}]_i=0\right\}.\] There are finitely many possible asymptotic activity patterns, and a nonnegative iterate sequence can be partitioned into finitely many disjoint consistently active subsequences. If \(x_{k_j}\to x_*\), then \(\{x_{k_j}\}\) is consistently active and \[\mathcal A\{x_{k_j}\}=\{i:[x_*]_i=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative subsequence is consistently active when each coordinate either tends to zero or remains asymptotically bounded away from zero. Its asymptotically active set contains the coordinates tending to zero. There are finitely many activity patterns, allowing a finite partition by consistent activity; for a convergent subsequence, the active set is exactly the set of zero coordinates of its limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A\{x_{k_j}\}=\{i:\lim_j[x_{k_j}]_i=0\};\quad x_{k_j}\to x_*\Rightarrow\mathcal A\{x_{k_j}\}=\{i:[x_*]_i=0\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perturbed-KKT Representation and Limitations of the Classical Primal Barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connection of primal-barrier equations to a primal-dual perturbed KKT formulation, together with conditioning, initialization, and equality-constraint limitations of the classical primal approach.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C(x)=\operatorname{diag}(c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x))\). The primal-barrier equations can be written as
\[
\nabla f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}z_i\nabla c_i(x)=0,
\qquad
C(x)z-\mu e=0.
\]
After introducing slacks with the corresponding slack equations and nonnegativity conditions, these equations are equivalent to the perturbed KKT conditions. Applying Newton's method in \((x,s,z)\), while temporarily ignoring the bounds \(s,z\ge0\), yields a primal-dual formulation.

On the strictly feasible set, the exact barrier Hessian is
\[
\nabla_{xx}^2P(x;\mu)=\nabla^2f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\frac{\mu}{c_i(x)}\nabla^2c_i(x)+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\frac{\mu}{c_i(x)^2}\nabla c_i(x)\nabla c_i(x)^T.
\]
Using \(z_i^*\approx\mu/c_i(x)\) near a barrier minimizer for small \(\mu\) gives
\[
\nabla_{xx}^2P(x;\mu)\approx\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,z^*)+
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\frac{(z_i^*)^2}{\mu}\nabla c_i(x)\nabla c_i(x)^T.
\]
Near \(x(\mu)\), the barrier Hessian becomes increasingly ill-conditioned as \(\mu\downarrow0\). This ill-conditioning is detrimental to steepest-descent, conjugate-gradient, and quasi-Newton methods. In the stated analysis, Newton's method is not harmed by the ill-conditioning itself, but the high nonlinearity of \(P\) still causes difficulty. The classical primal barrier method also requires a feasible initial point and does not naturally accommodate equality constraints; replacing equalities by quadratic penalties inherits the shortcomings of quadratic-penalty functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing slacks turns the primal-barrier stationarity and scaled-complementarity equations into the perturbed KKT system. Applying Newton's method to the primal, slack, and multiplier variables while temporarily disregarding their nonnegativity bounds gives a primal-dual formulation. The primal barrier Hessian becomes increasingly ill-conditioned near barrier minimizers as the barrier parameter tends to zero, which harms steepest descent, conjugate-gradient, and quasi-Newton methods. According to the extract, Newton's method is not harmed by that ill-conditioning itself, but it still encounters the barrier function's high nonlinearity. Classical primal barriers additionally require a feasible initial point and handle equality constraints poorly; using quadratic penalties for equalities imports the shortcomings of quadratic penalties.
assumptions_latex: The displayed Hessian formula presupposes the required second derivatives of \(f\) and \(c_i\).
For the asymptotic Hessian representation, \(x\) is near \(x(\mu)\), \(\mu\) is small, and \(z_i^*\approx\mu/c_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With slack equations and nonnegativity conditions, the primal stationarity-complementarity equations represent the perturbed KKT system and lead, through a Newton step that temporarily ignores \(s,z\ge0\), to a primal-dual formulation. Meanwhile, \(\nabla_{xx}^2P(x;\mu)\) becomes increasingly ill-conditioned near \(x(\mu)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\), subject to the stated algorithmic and modeling limitations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal log-barrier algorithm with approximate second-order inner solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm for minimizing a smooth objective over the positive orthant; referenced inner algorithms and forcing functions remain identified symbolically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0>0\), \(\mu_0>0\), and forcing functions \(\epsilon^{\mathrm D}(\mu)\) and \(\epsilon^{\mathrm E}(\mu)\), set \(k=0\). At outer iteration \(k\), choose \(\varsigma_k\in(0,1)\) and approximately minimize \(\phi^{\log}(x,\mu_k)=f(x)-\mu_k\langle e,\log x\rangle\) from \(x_k\) using Algorithm 13.2.1 or 13.3.1, with barrier model \[m^b_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s)=\mu_k\left(-\langle e,\log x_{k,j}\rangle-\langle X_{k,j}^{-1}e,s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,X_{k,j}^{-2}s\rangle\right).\] Stop at an iterate \(x_{k+1}>0\) satisfying \[\|\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\mu_kX_{k+1}^{-1}e\|\leq\epsilon^{\mathrm D}(\mu_k),\qquad \lambda_{\min}\!\left(\nabla^2f(x_{k+1})+\mu_kX_{k+1}^{-2}\right)\geq-\epsilon^{\mathrm E}(\mu_k).\] Choose \(\mu_{k+1}>0\) so that \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\mu_k=0\), increment \(k\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a strictly positive point and barrier parameter, approximately minimize each log-barrier subproblem until the stated first- and second-order tests hold at a strictly positive iterate. Update the positive barrier parameters so that they tend to zero and repeat.
assumptions_latex: \epsilon^{\mathrm D}(\mu)\text{ and }\epsilon^{\mathrm E}(\mu)\text{ are given forcing functions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}>0,\quad \|\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\mu_kX_{k+1}^{-1}e\|\leq\epsilon^{\mathrm D}(\mu_k),\quad \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x_{k+1})+\mu_kX_{k+1}^{-2})\geq-\epsilon^{\mathrm E}(\mu_k),\quad \mu_k\to0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unconstrained Primal Barrier Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer barrier-parameter continuation with approximately minimized primal log-barrier subproblems and approximate multiplier recovery; no convergence theorem is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\mu_0>0\), tolerances \(\{\tau_k\}\) satisfying \(\tau_k\to0\), and an initial subproblem starting point \(x_0^s\), repeat for \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\):

1. Starting from \(x_k^s\), find an approximate minimizer \(x_k\) of \(P(\cdot;\mu_k)\), terminating the inner solve when
\[
\|\nabla P(x_k;\mu_k)\|\le\tau_k.
\]
2. Estimate the multipliers using
\[
(z_k)_i\approx\frac{\mu_k}{c_i(x_k)},\qquad i\in\mathcal I.
\]
3. If the final convergence test is satisfied, return \(x_k\). Otherwise choose \(\mu_{k+1}<\mu_k\), choose a new starting point \(x_{k+1}^s\), and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with a positive barrier parameter, inner tolerances tending to zero, and a starting point. At each outer iteration, approximately minimize the current primal log-barrier function until its gradient norm meets the current tolerance, estimate the multipliers from the barrier parameter divided by the constraint values, and apply a final convergence test. If that test fails, decrease the barrier parameter, select the next starting point, and repeat.
assumptions_latex: An initial subproblem starting point \(x_0^s\) is given.
The barrier subproblem and the ratios \(\mu_k/c_i(x_k)\) are evaluated where \(c_i(x_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At each completed outer iteration, \(\|\nabla P(x_k;\mu_k)\|\le\tau_k\) and \((z_k)_i\approx\mu_k/c_i(x_k)\); the framework then either terminates under its final test or proceeds with \(\mu_{k+1}<\mu_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Log-Barrier and Primal Central Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Log-barrier representation for inequality-constrained nonlinear programming, including its strict-interior domain, conditional limiting behavior, and local multiplier estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x)\ge 0\quad(i\in\mathcal I),
\]
and \(\mu>0\), define on the strictly feasible set
\[
P(x;\mu)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\log c_i(x).
\]
If \(x(\mu)\) denotes a minimizer of \(P(\cdot;\mu)\), then
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm p}=\{x(\mu)\mid \mu>0\}
\]
is the primal central path. Under conditions ensuring convergence of the barrier minimizers, \(x(\mu)\) approaches a solution of the constrained problem as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Moreover,
\[
\nabla_xP(x;\mu)=\nabla f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\frac{\mu}{c_i(x)}\nabla c_i(x),
\]
so when \(x\) is close to \(x(\mu)\) and \(\mu\) is small, the optimal multipliers can be estimated by
\[
z_i^*\approx\frac{\mu}{c_i(x)},\qquad i\in\mathcal I.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an inequality-constrained nonlinear program, the primal logarithmic barrier is defined on the strictly feasible interior. Its minimizers trace the primal central path. Under the additional conditions needed for barrier convergence, these minimizers approach a constrained solution as the barrier parameter tends to zero. Near a barrier minimizer for a small parameter, the gradient representation gives the multiplier estimate z_i approximately equal to mu divided by c_i(x).
assumptions_latex: For each relevant \(\mu\), a barrier minimizer \(x(\mu)\) exists.
For the limiting conclusion, the conditions ensuring convergence of barrier minimizers hold.
For the multiplier estimate, \(x\) is close to \(x(\mu)\) and \(\mu\) is small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm p}=\{x(\mu):\mu>0\}\); under the stated convergence conditions, \(x(\mu)\) approaches a constrained solution as \(\mu\downarrow0\), and locally \(z_i^*\approx\mu/c_i(x)\) for small \(\mu\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Barrier NLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-based primal-dual perturbed KKT representation for smooth nonlinear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\). For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\ge0\), introduce \(s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^m\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(z\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^m\). With \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), the primal-dual barrier equations are \[\nabla f(x)+J_h(x)^{\mathsf T}y-J_g(x)^{\mathsf T}z=0,\quad h(x)=0,\quad g(x)-s=0,\quad Sz=\mu\mathbf 1.\] Thus \(s_i z_i=\mu\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\), coupling primal interiority and dual positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual barrier representation couples stationarity, equality feasibility, positive slacks, positive inequality multipliers, and perturbed complementarity products equal to the barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perturbed KKT representation includes \(g(x)-s=0\) and \(s_i z_i=\mu\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).

notation.meaning: Positive slack and inequality-multiplier vectors in R^m.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual perturbed KKT barrier system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)-s=0\), \(s\geq0\), let \(y\) and \(z\geq0\) be equality and inequality multipliers, and set \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming with explicit positive slacks and multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), the primal-dual barrier NLP is the coupled system \[\nabla f(x)-A_E(x)^Ty-A_I(x)^Tz=0,\qquad c_E(x)=0,\qquad c_I(x)-s=0,\qquad Sz=\mu e,\qquad s>0,\ z>0.\] A primal-dual barrier step is a Newton or regularized Newton step for these equations, combined with step lengths that retain positivity. A primal-dual barrier method follows approximate solutions of this system while \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual barrier NLP keeps the primal variables, equality multipliers, inequality slacks, and inequality multipliers as independent variables. It imposes stationarity, equality feasibility, the slack equations, and perturbed complementarity \(s_i z_i=\mu\), with both \(s_i\) and \(z_i\) positive. Its iterations linearize this coupled system and reduce \(\mu\) toward zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_\mu(x,s,y,z)=0,\qquad F_\mu:=\left(\nabla f-A_E^Ty-A_I^Tz,\ Sz-\mu e,\ c_E,\ c_I-s\right),\quad s,z>0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(s>0\), the complementarity equation is equivalent to \(z=\mu S^{-1}e\), which recovers the primal barrier multipliers.
The Newton equations can be written as a full primal-dual KKT system or reduced by eliminating the slack and multiplier steps.
special_cases_latex: With affine constraints and a convex quadratic objective, the system reduces to the standard primal-dual quadratic-programming barrier equations.
For linear programming, all Jacobians are constant and the Lagrangian Hessian vanishes.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every component satisfies \(s_i z_i=\mu>0\), so neither member of a complementary pair is zero before the limit.
As \(\mu\to0\), any convergent sequence with vanishing feasibility and stationarity residuals approaches the ordinary KKT complementarity equations.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require primal feasibility at intermediate iterates, but it does require positive slacks and multipliers.
Singular Jacobians, failed constraint qualifications, and nonconvex curvature require regularization or globalization beyond the defining system.
