knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logarithmic barriers for variable bounds
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(h(x)=0\) denote optional smooth equalities, and let \(l_i\leq x_i\leq u_i\), where either endpoint may be infinite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth optimization with separable lower and upper variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite-bound index sets \(L:=\{i:l_i> -\infty\}\) and \(U:=\{i:u_i<+\infty\}\), the variable-bound log-barrier family is \[\Phi_\mu^{\mathrm{bd}}(x)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i\in L}\log(x_i-l_i)-\mu\sum_{i\in U}\log(u_i-x_i),\qquad \mu>0,\] with domain \(x_i>l_i\) for \(i\in L\) and \(x_i<u_i\) for \(i\in U\), subject to \(h(x)=0\). Distinct positive weights may replace the common \(\mu\) to form a weighted bound-barrier family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-bound barrier adds one logarithmic term for every finite lower bound and one for every finite upper bound. Its domain is the open box obtained by making all finite bounds strict. Unbounded sides contribute no barrier term. A two-sided bound contributes two terms, while a one-sided bound contributes one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi_\mu^{\mathrm{bd}}(x)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i\in L}\log(x_i-l_i)-\mu\sum_{i\in U}\log(u_i-x_i),\quad \operatorname{dom}\Phi_\mu^{\mathrm{bd}}=\{x:l_i<x_i<u_i\text{ for finite bounds}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Set \(s_i^L=x_i-l_i>0\) and \(s_i^U=u_i-x_i>0\); then the barrier is \(-\mu\sum\log s_i^L-\mu\sum\log s_i^U\).
The induced bound multipliers are \(z_i^L=\mu/(x_i-l_i)\) and \(z_i^U=\mu/(u_i-x_i)\).
special_cases_latex: For nonnegativity \(x_i\geq0\), the term is \(-\mu\log x_i\).
For a free variable with \(l_i=-\infty\) and \(u_i=+\infty\), no bound-barrier term is present.
immediate_consequences_latex: The barrier Hessian contribution is diagonal with entries \(\mu/(x_i-l_i)^2+\mu/(u_i-x_i)^2\), omitting absent bounds.
The objective diverges to \(+\infty\) as any finite bound is approached from the interior.
boundary_notes: A fixed variable with \(l_i=u_i\) has no strict interior and should be eliminated or treated as an equality.
This separable barrier addresses variable bounds only; general inequalities require their own slack or barrier representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Box Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable logarithmic barrier for variables with finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the open box \(\mathcal B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell_i<x_i<u_i,\ i=1,\ldots,n\}\), where \(\ell_i<u_i\), the logarithmic box barrier is \[B_{\mathcal B}(x;\mu)=-\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl[\log(x_i-\ell_i)+\log(u_i-x_i)\bigr].\] Its gradient component is \(\mu[(u_i-x_i)^{-1}-(x_i-\ell_i)^{-1}]\), and its Hessian is diagonal with entry \(\mu[(x_i-\ell_i)^{-2}+(u_i-x_i)^{-2}]>0\). Hence the barrier is strictly convex on \(\mathcal B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box barrier sums lower- and upper-distance logarithms; it is separable, strictly convex, and becomes singular at either side of every bounded interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2B_{\mathcal B}(x;\mu)\succ0\) throughout \(\mathcal B\), and \(B_{\mathcal B}(x;\mu)\to+\infty\) at its boundary.

notation.meaning: Finite componentwise lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logarithmic and Reciprocal Barriers for Two-Sided Variable Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representations for finite or infinite componentwise variable bounds, including fixed-variable handling and the bounded-box consequences stated in the source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=\{i:(x_\ell)_i> -\infty\}\), \(U=\{i:(x_u)_i<+\infty\}\), and require \((x_\ell)_i<(x_u)_i\) whenever both bounds are finite. On the strict interior \(x_i>(x_\ell)_i\) for \(i\in L\) and \(x_i<(x_u)_i\) for \(i\in U\), for \(\mu>0\) and \(\alpha>0\),
\[
b^{\log}(x,\mu)=-\mu\left(\sum_{i\in L}\log(x_i-(x_\ell)_i)+\sum_{i\in U}\log((x_u)_i-x_i)\right),
\]
\[
b^{\mathrm R(\alpha)}(x,\mu)=\frac{\mu}{\alpha}\left(\sum_{i\in L}(x_i-(x_\ell)_i)^{-\alpha}+\sum_{i\in U}((x_u)_i-x_i)^{-\alpha}\right).
\]
Thus an infinite bound contributes no barrier term. If \((x_\ell)_i=(x_u)_i\), that variable is fixed and may be eliminated. The primal and primal-dual log-barrier developments for nonnegativity constraints extend to simple bounds, with one dual variable per finite bound and at most \(2n\) bound dual variables. If all bounds are finite and the algorithm keeps iterates strictly feasible, the iterates lie in a bounded domain and therefore have limit points; the bounded-below barrier assumption used in the cited results is then automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each finite lower bound, add a barrier term based on the lower slack; for each finite upper bound, add one based on the upper slack. The logarithmic barrier uses negative logarithms of these slacks, while the reciprocal family uses negative powers. Infinite bounds contribute no term, and a variable with equal lower and upper bounds is fixed and may be eliminated. Barrier developments for nonnegativity constraints extend to simple bounds, with one dual variable for each finite bound. When all bounds are finite and iterates remain strictly feasible, the iterates are bounded and have limit points, and the source's bounded-below barrier assumption is automatic.
assumptions_latex: (x_\ell)_i<(x_u)_i\quad\text{whenever both bounds are finite, after eliminating fixed variables}
\text{For the boundedness and limit-point conclusions, all bounds are finite and every iterate is strictly feasible.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^{\log}(x,\mu)=-\mu\left(\sum_{i\in L}\log(x_i-(x_\ell)_i)+\sum_{i\in U}\log((x_u)_i-x_i)\right),\quad b^{\mathrm R(\alpha)}(x,\mu)=\frac{\mu}{\alpha}\left(\sum_{i\in L}(x_i-(x_\ell)_i)^{-\alpha}+\sum_{i\in U}((x_u)_i-x_i)^{-\alpha}\right),\quad\text{with bounded strictly feasible iterates and limit points when all bounds are finite.}

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Activity Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature and multiplier scaling induced by logarithmic variable-bound barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i,\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\), and fix \(\mu>0\). Define the lower-bound distance and induced multiplier by \(s_i^L=x_i-\ell_i\) and \(z_i^L=\mu/s_i^L\), and define the upper-bound distance and induced multiplier by \(s_i^U=u_i-x_i\) and \(z_i^U=\mu/s_i^U\). Then \(s_i^Lz_i^L=s_i^Uz_i^U=\mu\), while the corresponding diagonal barrier curvatures are \(z_i^L/s_i^L=\mu/(s_i^L)^2\) and \(z_i^U/s_i^U=\mu/(s_i^U)^2\). Consequently, with \(\mu\) fixed, a shrinking distance to either bound makes its induced multiplier grow inversely with distance and its normal curvature grow inversely with squared distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed positive barrier parameter, approaching a bound makes the barrier-induced multiplier grow inversely with distance and the normal curvature grow inversely with squared distance.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu>0\) is fixed in the stated limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(s_i^L\downarrow0\) or \(s_i^U\downarrow0\) with fixed \(\mu>0\), the associated multiplier and barrier curvature diverge to \(+\infty\).

notation.meaning: Positive distances to the lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Reformulated Inequality Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-slack equality representation of smooth nonlinear inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\). The system \(g(x)\ge0\) is equivalent to the existence of \(s\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) such that \(g(x)-s=0\). For \(\mu>0\), its strict-interior barrier form requires \(s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^m\) and uses the objective \(f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i\). With \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and the sign convention \[\mathcal L_\mu(x,s,z)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i-z^{\mathsf T}(g(x)-s),\] stationarity with respect to \(s\) gives \(z_i=\mu/s_i>0\), equivalently \(s_i z_i=\mu\), for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative inequality map is equivalently represented by equality to nonnegative slacks; positive slacks admit a logarithmic barrier, and a stated multiplier-sign convention yields perturbed complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are defined on the NLP domain.
\(s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^m\) and \(\mu>0\) in the strict-interior barrier form.
The multiplier sign convention is the one displayed in \(\mathcal L_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\ge0\iff\exists s\in\mathbb{R}_+^m:g(x)-s=0\), and the displayed positive-slack barrier convention gives \(s_i z_i=\mu\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Slack vector for the nonlinear inequalities.
Multiplier vector under the displayed negative-sign Lagrangian convention.
Slack-barrier Lagrangian with an explicit multiplier-sign convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-slack reformulation of nonlinear inequalities
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c_I:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be a smooth inequality map in the convention \(c_I(x)\geq0\), and let \(c_E(x)=0\) denote any equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional reformulation of componentwise nonlinear inequalities, with strict positivity used by barrier subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The slack reformulation introduces \(s\in\mathbb R^m\) and replaces \(c_I(x)\geq0\) by \[c_I(x)-s=0,\qquad s\geq0.\] Its strict-interior version uses \(s>0\), and the associated barrier subproblem is \[\min_{x,s>0}f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_E(x)=0,\quad c_I(x)-s=0.\] Projection onto the \(x\)-coordinates recovers the original feasible set exactly when nonnegative slacks are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slack-reformulated inequality model assigns one nonnegative slack to each component of the nonlinear inequality and imposes an equality between the constraint value and that slack. The original and slack formulations have the same feasible primal points. Barrier models replace nonnegativity by strict positivity and penalize the slacks logarithmically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[c_I(x)\geq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists s\geq0:\ c_I(x)-s=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the convention \(g(x)\leq0\), the corresponding equality is \(g(x)+s=0\) with \(s\geq0\).
Eliminating \(s\) from the strict barrier model gives \(f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log c_{I,i}(x)\) on \(c_I(x)>0\).
special_cases_latex: An affine inequality \(a_i^Tx\leq b_i\) becomes \(a_i^Tx+s_i=b_i\), \(s_i\geq0\).
A lower variable bound \(x_i\geq l_i\) uses \(s_i=x_i-l_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier-slack complementarity condition is \(s_i z_i=0\) at a KKT point and \(s_i z_i=\mu\) in a barrier system.
The Jacobian of the slack equality with respect to \(s\) is \(-I\), which gives the primal-dual system a structured block.
boundary_notes: Strict slacks represent only strictly feasible inequalities; active inequalities appear only in the limit as \(s_i\downarrow0\).
Introducing slacks for nonlinear convex inequalities does not generally preserve a standard convex equality-constrained formulation, since nonlinear equality constraints are not affine.

notation.meaning: Inequality constraint map in the nonnegative convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Barrier Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier subproblem that preserves smooth equality constraints explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). On the domain where \(g_i(x)>0\) for every \(i\), define \(\phi_\mu(x)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log g_i(x)\) for \(\mu>0\). The equality-constrained barrier model is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\phi_\mu(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0.\] With \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\), its Lagrangian is \(\mathcal L_\mu(x,y)=\phi_\mu(x)+y^{\mathsf T}h(x)\), and its first-order system is \(\nabla_x\mathcal L_\mu(x,y)=0\) and \(h(x)=0\). Equality constraints receive no logarithmic term and remain explicit in the barrier subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The logarithmic barrier absorbs the inequality constraints into the objective on their strict interior, while equality constraints remain explicit and are enforced through equality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i(x)>0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\) on the barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barrier subproblem has objective \(\phi_\mu\), explicit equality constraint \(h(x)=0\), and first-order equations \(\nabla_x\mathcal L_\mu(x,y)=0\) and \(h(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian of the equality-constrained barrier subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local step model for an NLP barrier subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \((x,s,y,z)\) with \(s,z>0\) and \(\mu>0\), let \(\mathcal L(x,s,y,z)=f(x)-y^Tc_E(x)-z^T(c_I(x)-s)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(\Sigma=S^{-1}Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional NLP barrier steps, allowing indefinite Lagrangian Hessians and either line-search or trust-region globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An NLP barrier step model is a local linear-quadratic model whose primal step \(p=(p_x,p_s)\) approximates the barrier objective and linearizes the constraints: \[q_\mu(p)=\nabla f(x)^Tp_x+\tfrac12p_x^TBp_x-\mu e^TS^{-1}p_s+\tfrac12p_s^T\Sigma p_s,\] \[A_Ep_x+c_E=r_E,\qquad A_Ip_x-p_s+c_I-s=r_I.\] The matrix \(B\) is the exact or approximate Lagrangian Hessian. The residual targets \((r_E,r_I)\), a trust region, and positivity bounds determine the particular step architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NLP barrier step model is the quadratic local optimization problem obtained by approximating the barrier objective and linearizing equality and slack constraints at the current positive iterate. It contains the Lagrangian curvature in the primal variables, scaled barrier curvature in the slack variables, and linearized constraint equations. Newton, normal-tangential, and trust-region barrier steps are distinguished by how this common model is constrained and solved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p\in\operatorname*{argmin}q_\mu(p)\quad\text{subject to the selected linearized constraints, positivity safeguard, and optional trust-region bound}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The unconstrained KKT equations of the local model reproduce a scaled form of the primal-dual Newton equations.
Using \(\widetilde p_s=S^{-1}p_s\) changes the slack Hessian block to \(S\Sigma S\) and makes relative slack displacement explicit.
special_cases_latex: Setting residual targets to zero gives a full linearized-feasibility step when the resulting subproblem is consistent.
Adding \(\|(p_x,S^{-1}p_s)\|\leq\Delta\) gives a scaled trust-region barrier model.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(B\) is indefinite, a trust-region restriction can still make the subproblem bounded.
Simple inequality bounds on \(p_s\) can enforce a fraction-to-the-boundary condition.
boundary_notes: The local model does not itself specify step acceptance or barrier-parameter updates.
An approximate Hessian changes the step model but not the underlying perturbed KKT target.

notation.meaning: Exact or approximate Hessian of the Lagrangian.
Relaxed residual targets for the linearized constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second primal inner barrier trust-region algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner trust-region iteration for a barrier objective with boundary-distance safeguards and sufficient first- or second-order model decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_{k,0}\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal C)\), an initial radius \(\Delta_{k,0}\), \(\varsigma_k\in(0,1)\), and constants \(\eta_1,\eta_2,\gamma_1,\gamma_2\) satisfying (6.1.3), set \(j=0\). Form \(m_{k,j}=m^f_{k,j}+m^b_{k,j}\), where both components satisfy AM.1--AM.3, AM.4h, and AM.4i, and let \(d_{k,j}=\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C)\). Choose \(s_{k,j}\) such that \(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\in\mathcal B_{k,j}\cap\mathcal C\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C)\geq\varsigma_kd_{k,j}\), and
\[
m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j})\geq\kappa_{\rm sod}\max\left\{\|g_{k,j}\|\min\left[\frac{\|g_{k,j}\|}{\beta_{k,j}},\Delta_{k,j},(1-\varsigma_k)d_{k,j}\right],-\tau_{k,j}\min\left[\tau_{k,j}^2,\Delta_{k,j}^2,(1-\varsigma_k)^2d_{k,j}^2\right]\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
\rho_{k,j}=\frac{\phi(x_{k,j},\mu_k)-\phi(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\mu_k)}{m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j})}.
\]
Set \(x_{k,j+1}=x_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\) when \(\rho_{k,j}\geq\eta_1\), and set \(x_{k,j+1}=x_{k,j}\) otherwise. Choose
\[
\Delta_{k,j+1}\in\begin{cases}[\Delta_{k,j},\infty),&\rho_{k,j}\geq\eta_2,\\[\gamma_2\Delta_{k,j},\Delta_{k,j}],&\eta_1\leq\rho_{k,j}<\eta_2,\\[\gamma_1\Delta_{k,j},\gamma_2\Delta_{k,j}],&\rho_{k,j}<\eta_1,\end{cases}
\]
increment \(j\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a relative-interior point, repeatedly construct an objective-plus-barrier model, compute a feasible trust-region step that preserves the prescribed boundary-distance fraction and satisfies the stated gradient-or-curvature decrease bound, accept it using actual-to-predicted barrier reduction, and update the radius according to the three ratio regimes.
assumptions_latex: m_{k,j}=m^f_{k,j}+m^b_{k,j},\quad m^f_{k,j},m^b_{k,j}\text{ satisfy AM.1--AM.3, AM.4h, and AM.4i}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x_{k,j},\Delta_{k,j}\}_{j\geq0}\text{ is generated by the stated feasibility, sufficient-decrease, acceptance, and radius-update rules.}

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Newton Barrier Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full Newton step for the KKT equations of an equality-constrained barrier subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be an open barrier domain, let \(\phi_\mu:\mathcal D\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(h:\mathcal D\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and let \(\mu>0\). Given \(x\in\mathcal D\) and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\), form \(r_d=\nabla\phi_\mu(x)+J_h(x)^{\mathsf T}y\), \(r_p=h(x)\), and \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2[\phi_\mu(x)+y^{\mathsf T}h(x)]\). Compute \((p,q)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\) from \[\begin{bmatrix}H&J_h(x)^{\mathsf T}\\J_h(x)&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\q\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{bmatrix}.\] Choose \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) such that \(x+\alpha p\in\mathcal D\) and the prescribed globalization test is satisfied, then update \((x,y)\leftarrow(x+\alpha p,y+\alpha q)\). Stop when the prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the equality-constrained KKT Newton system for primal and multiplier corrections, shorten the step to remain in the barrier domain and pass the prescribed globalization test, and stop when the KKT residual tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open, \(\phi_\mu\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable near the iterate, and \(x\in\mathcal D\).
The displayed KKT matrix is nonsingular.
A specific line-search or trust-region acceptance rule and primal-dual stopping tolerances are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is a domain-preserving globalized Newton correction for \(\nabla\phi_\mu(x)+J_h(x)^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(h(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Open domain on which the barrier objective is finite.
Primal and multiplier Newton corrections in R^n and R^p.
Hessian of the barrier-subproblem Lagrangian with respect to x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton step for an equality-constrained barrier problem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(w=(x,s)\) with \(s>0\), define \(\phi_\mu(w)=f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log s_i\), and collect the equality and slack equations as \(g(w)=(c_E(x),c_I(x)-s)=0\). Let \(\lambda=(y,z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Newton linearization for a fixed smooth equality-constrained barrier subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality-constrained Newton barrier step \((p_w,p_\lambda)\) is any solution of the saddle-point system \[\begin{bmatrix}H_\mu(w,\lambda)&J_g(w)^T\\J_g(w)&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p_w\\p_\lambda\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_w\phi_\mu(w)-J_g(w)^T\lambda\\g(w)\end{bmatrix},\] where \(H_\mu\) is the Hessian of the barrier Lagrangian. In primal-dual scaling, its slack block may be represented by \(\Sigma=S^{-1}Z\). A step length must additionally be chosen so that \(s+\alpha p_s>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained Newton barrier step solves the KKT linear system obtained by linearizing stationarity and the equality and slack equations of a fixed barrier subproblem. The coefficient matrix contains the barrier-Lagrangian Hessian, the constraint Jacobian, and its transpose. The algebraic Newton step is distinct from the positive step length used to update the iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K_\mu(w,\lambda)(p_w,p_\lambda)=-R_\mu(w,\lambda),\qquad s+\alpha p_s>0\ \text{for the accepted update}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating slack-step or multiplier-step blocks yields reduced or condensed Newton systems with the same exact direction when the eliminations are valid.
Linearizing \(Sz=\mu e\) gives the primal-dual Newton form; eliminating \(z=\mu S^{-1}e\) first gives the primal form.
special_cases_latex: With no inequality constraints, the system is the ordinary equality-constrained Newton KKT system.
With affine constraints and quadratic objective, the Newton system is linear with constant primal curvature apart from barrier scaling.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the KKT matrix is nonsingular, the equality-constrained Newton barrier step is unique.
A fraction-to-the-boundary step length preserves strict positivity without altering the defining Newton equation.
boundary_notes: If the Jacobian is rank deficient or the reduced Hessian is singular, regularization or a least-squares interpretation is required.
The raw Newton step need not provide global decrease and therefore normally requires globalization.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality and slack-equation map.
Hessian of the equality-constrained barrier Lagrangian.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal–Tangential Barrier Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite step for an equality-constrained logarithmic-barrier subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the barrier problem \(\min_z \phi_\mu(z)\) subject to \(c(z)=0\), with \(z\) strictly interior, let \(J=\nabla c(z)\), \(g=\nabla\phi_\mu(z)\), and let \(B\) be a symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian model. First compute a normal step \(n\) satisfying \(\|J n+c(z)\|\leq \kappa_n\|c(z)\|\). Then compute a tangential step \(t\) with \(Jt=0\) that approximately minimizes \(g^{\mathsf T}(n+t)+\tfrac12(n+t)^{\mathsf T}B(n+t)\) over the permitted step region while preserving strict interiority. Set \(d=n+t\), and accept or shorten \(d\) according to the globalization rule. Terminate when feasibility and barrier-stationarity residuals meet their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a feasibility-improving normal step, add a linearized-feasible tangential step for optimality, then globalize the combined strictly interior step.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_\mu\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable on an open strictly interior domain.
\(\mu>0\), and the current iterate lies in the barrier domain.
The normal and tangential subproblems are solved to their stated relative accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=n+t\) separates first-order feasibility correction from objective-model reduction along the linearized constraint manifold.

notation.meaning: Logarithmic-barrier objective with fixed parameter mu.
Constraint Jacobian at the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal-tangential decomposition of a barrier step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(r(w)=(c_E(x),c_I(x)-s)\), let \(J=J_r(w)\), use the scaled step \(d=(p_x,S^{-1}p_s)\), and impose \(\|d\|\leq\Delta\) with a positivity bound on its slack component.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite trust-region steps for smooth equality-and-slack barrier subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A normal-tangential barrier step is a decomposition \[d=v+t,\] where the normal step \(v\) approximately minimizes \(\|Jv+r(w)\|^2\) in a contracted trust region and under the slack-positivity bound, while the tangential step \(t\) approximately minimizes the quadratic barrier model subject to \[Jt=0,\qquad \|v+t\|\leq\Delta,\] and the remaining positivity restrictions. Thus \(v\) targets linearized feasibility and \(t\) improves the barrier objective without changing the linearized residual attained by \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal-tangential barrier step is the sum of two components. The normal component reduces the linearized equality and slack residuals within part of the trust region. The tangential component then reduces the quadratic barrier model while lying in the null space of the linearized constraints, so it preserves the residual achieved by the normal component. Both components respect scaled slack-positivity safeguards.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d=v+t,\qquad v\approx\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|v\|\leq\zeta\Delta}\|Jv+r\|^2,\qquad Jt=0,\qquad v+t\approx\operatorname*{argmin}q_\mu(v+t).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The relaxed right-hand side of the tangential quadratic subproblem is defined by the residual left after the normal step.
The tangential component can be computed by projected conjugate gradients in the null space of \(J\).
special_cases_latex: If the current point is linearly feasible, one may take \(v=0\), leaving a purely tangential barrier step.
If the normal step exhausts the trust region, the tangential component may be zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(Jt=0\), \(J(v+t)+r=Jv+r\).
Separate normal and tangential computations prevent an objective step from sacrificing the linearized feasibility improvement already obtained.
boundary_notes: The decomposition depends on the chosen scaling, norm, trust-region split, and accuracy criteria.
Rank deficiency can make the normal or tangential subproblem nonunique.

notation.meaning: Fraction of the trust region reserved for the normal step.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Barrier Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic trust-region step for a fixed-parameter barrier subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a strictly interior point \(z\), form the barrier model \(m(d)=\phi_\mu(z)+g^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Bd\), where \(g=\nabla\phi_\mu(z)\). Compute an approximate solution of \(\min_d m(d)\) subject to \(\|D d\|\leq\Delta\), any linearized equality constraints, and a fraction-to-the-boundary restriction ensuring that \(z+d\) remains strictly interior. Require the computed step to attain at least a prescribed fraction of the decrease achieved by an admissible Cauchy-type step. Stop the inner solve when that decrease condition and the subproblem feasibility tolerances hold; otherwise reduce the step or continue the subproblem iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the local barrier model inside a scaled trust region while respecting linearized constraints, strict interiority, and sufficient model decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_\mu\) is twice continuously differentiable near the current strictly interior point.
\(\Delta>0\), and the admissible step set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(d\) is admissible and provides safeguarded predicted reduction \(m(0)-m(d)>0\) unless the model is stationary on the admissible set.

notation.meaning: Local quadratic model of the fixed-parameter barrier objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled trust-region barrier step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \((x,s,y,z)\) with \(s,z>0\), let \(B\) approximate \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L\), let \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(Z=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\), and \(\Sigma=S^{-1}Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth, possibly nonconvex NLP barrier subproblems with scaled slack displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), radius \(\Delta>0\), and \(\tau\in(0,1)\), a trust-region barrier step is an exact or approximate solution of \[\min_{p_x,p_s}\ \nabla f^Tp_x+\tfrac12p_x^TBp_x-\mu e^TS^{-1}p_s+\tfrac12p_s^T\Sigma p_s\] subject to linearized equality and slack equations, \[\|(p_x,S^{-1}p_s)\|_2\leq\Delta,\qquad p_s\geq-\tau s.\] The scaling restricts relative rather than absolute slack motion, and the last inequality guarantees \(s+p_s\geq(1-\tau)s>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region barrier step minimizes a quadratic model of the fixed-parameter barrier problem under linearized constraints. Its trust region measures slack motion relative to the current slacks, and it includes a componentwise lower bound that keeps the trial slack vector positive. The trust region bounds the subproblem even when the Lagrangian Hessian is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p\approx\operatorname*{argmin}q_\mu(p)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \|(p_x,S^{-1}p_s)\|_2\leq\Delta,\quad p_s\geq-\tau s,\quad \text{linearized constraints}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\widetilde p_s=S^{-1}p_s\), the region is the Euclidean ball \(\|(p_x,\widetilde p_s)\|_2\leq\Delta\) and the positivity bound is \(\widetilde p_s\geq-\tau e\).
The scaled slack Hessian becomes \(S\Sigma S\), which is better balanced near perturbed complementarity.
special_cases_latex: If the unconstrained Newton barrier step lies inside the region and satisfies the positivity bound, it can be the trust-region solution.
Projected or truncated conjugate gradients provide an inexact large-scale step and can terminate at negative curvature or the trust-region boundary.
immediate_consequences_latex: The trust-region constraint makes the quadratic subproblem bounded below even when \(B\) has negative curvature.
Every full accepted model step satisfies strict slack positivity.
boundary_notes: The definition specifies the step subproblem, not the rule for accepting the trial point or updating \(\Delta\).
Multiplier positivity requires a separate update or safeguard in methods that compute only a primal step.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled trust-region barrier step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled Trust-Region SQP Subproblem for a Fixed Barrier Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-specific coupled SQP step model with relaxed linearized constraints, fraction-to-boundary control, and slack-scaled trust-region geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At $(x,s)$ with $s>0$, fixed $\mu>0$, multiplier estimates $(y,z)$, $S=\operatorname{diag}(s)$, primal-dual matrix $\Sigma$, radius $\Delta>0$, and $\tau\in(0,1)$, approximately compute $p=(p_x,p_s)$ from
\[\min_{p_x,p_s}\ \nabla f^Tp_x+\tfrac12p_x^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L\,p_x-\mu e^TS^{-1}p_s+\tfrac12p_s^T\Sigma p_s\]
subject to
\[A_E(x)p_x+c_E(x)=r_E,\qquad A_I(x)p_x-p_s+c_I(x)-s=r_I,\]
\[\|(p_x,S^{-1}p_s)\|_2\le\Delta,\qquad p_s\ge-\tau s.\]
The relaxation $(r_E,r_I)$ is chosen by an auxiliary feasibility computation because zero relaxation can make the linearized constraints incompatible with the trust region or produce inadequate feasibility progress. The bound gives $s+p_s\ge(1-\tau)s>0$. If the relaxed feasible set is nonempty, the trust-region restriction bounds the quadratic model on that set even when $\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L$ is indefinite, while $S^{-1}$ more strongly restricts slack-step components corresponding to small $s_i$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed positive barrier parameter, approximately solve a coupled SQP quadratic model subject to relaxed linearized constraints, an inverse-slack-scaled trust region, and a fraction-to-boundary bound. An auxiliary feasibility computation selects the relaxation because zero relaxation may be incompatible or ineffective. The fraction-to-boundary bound preserves positive slacks; when the relaxed feasible set is nonempty, the trust region keeps the model bounded even with an indefinite Lagrangian Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \text{the relaxed constraints, trust region, and slack bound have a nonempty feasible set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s+p_s\ge(1-\tau)s>0,\qquad \inf\{q(p):p\text{ satisfies the restricted subproblem constraints}\}>-\infty

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order model-adequacy estimate for a trust-region barrier trial step at fixed outer index \(k\), using the boundary-separation constant from the preceding invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose AC.2b, AF.1, AF.3, AC.4c, AM.1--AM.3, AM.4h, and AM.4i hold. If \[\Delta_{k,j}\leq(1-\varsigma_k)\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k),\] then \[\left|\phi(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\mu_k)-m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j})\right|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{ubh}}(k)\Delta_{k,j}^2,\] where \[\kappa_{\mathrm{ubh}}(k):=\max\!\left\{\kappa_{\mathrm{ufh}}+\kappa_{\mathrm{bbh}}(\varsigma_k\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k),\mu_k),\ \kappa_{\mathrm{umh}}+\kappa_{\mathrm{bbmh}}(\varsigma_k\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k),\mu_k)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated smoothness and model assumptions, if the trust-region radius is no larger than the boundary-safe radius, the error between the barrier objective and its model at the trial point is bounded by a specified constant times the squared radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left|\phi(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\mu_k)-m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j})\right|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{ubh}}(k)\Delta_{k,j}^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner trust-region primal-dual barrier algorithm for general constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner iteration at fixed outer barrier parameter; referenced model and sufficient-reduction conditions are defined outside the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_{k,0}\in\operatorname{si}(\mathcal C)\), \(y_{k,0}>0\), an initial radius \(\Delta_{k,0}\), constants \(\eta_1,\eta_2,\gamma_1,\gamma_2\) satisfying (6.1.3), and \(\varsigma_k\in(0,1)\), set \(j=0\). Construct \(m_{k,j}\) as prescribed by (13.9.2)--(13.9.4), with \(m^f_{k,j}\) satisfying AM.1--AM.3 and AM.4i. Compute \(s_{k,j}\) satisfying AA.1/AA.2 and \(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\in\mathcal B_{k,j}\). If
\[
c_i(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j})\geq\varsigma_kc_i(x_{k,j})\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),
\]
define
\[
\rho_{k,j}=\frac{\phi(x_{k,j},\mu_k)-\phi(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\mu_k)}{m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j})};
\]
otherwise set \(\rho_{k,j}=-\infty\). Set \(x_{k,j+1}=x_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\) when \(\rho_{k,j}\geq\eta_1\), and \(x_{k,j+1}=x_{k,j}\) otherwise. Choose
\[
\Delta_{k,j+1}\in
\begin{cases}
[\Delta_{k,j},\infty),&\rho_{k,j}\geq\eta_2,\\
[\gamma_2\Delta_{k,j},\Delta_{k,j}],&\eta_1\leq\rho_{k,j}<\eta_2,\\
[\gamma_1\Delta_{k,j},\gamma_2\Delta_{k,j}],&\rho_{k,j}<\eta_1,
\end{cases}
\]
increment \(j\), and repeat from model construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a trust-region barrier model, compute a sufficiently reducing trial step, and reject any step that violates the prescribed fraction-to-the-boundary test. Otherwise accept according to the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio, update the trust-region radius according to that ratio, and repeat.
assumptions_latex: m^f_{k,j}\text{ satisfies AM.1--AM.3 and AM.4i, and }s_{k,j}\text{ satisfies AA.1/AA.2}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_{k,j+1},\Delta_{k,j+1})\text{ is updated by the stated fraction-to-the-boundary, acceptance-ratio, and trust-region rules at each inner iteration.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a constant \(\kappa_{\mathrm{lch}}\) such that, for every \(k,j\) and all \(x,y\in\mathcal B_{k,j}\), \[\left\|\nabla_{xx}m^b_{k,j}(x)-\nabla_{xx}m^b_{k,j}(y)\right\|\leq \kappa_{\mathrm{lch}}\|x-y\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hessian of each barrier model is Lipschitz continuous on B_kj with one constant kappa_lch uniform over all k and j.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Actual-predicted and feasibility model-decrease safeguards
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi_v\) be a barrier merit function, let \(q_v\) be its local model, let \(m(p)\) measure the linearized constraint residual, and let \(p\) be a candidate trust-region barrier step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region globalization safeguards for smooth NLP barrier steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model-decrease safeguard accepts a trial step only if its actual reduction \[\operatorname{ared}(p):=\phi_v(0)-\phi_v(p)\] is sufficiently large relative to its predicted reduction \[\operatorname{pred}(p):=q_v(0)-q_v(p),\qquad \operatorname{ared}(p)\geq\eta\operatorname{pred}(p),\quad \eta\in(0,1).\] A feasibility-decrease safeguard additionally selects the penalty weight \(v\) so that \[\operatorname{pred}(p)\geq\rho v\bigl(m(0)-m(p)\bigr),\qquad \rho\in(0,1).\] Together these conditions prevent acceptance based on an unreliable model or on objective decrease that inadequately represents the targeted feasibility improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-decrease safeguard compares the decrease observed in the barrier merit function with the decrease predicted by its local model and accepts the step only when the observed decrease is a fixed positive fraction of the prediction. A companion safeguard chooses the penalty weight so the prediction also reflects a fixed fraction of the modeled constraint-residual improvement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{ared}(p)\geq\eta\operatorname{pred}(p),\qquad \operatorname{pred}(p)\geq\rho v\bigl(m(0)-m(p)\bigr),\qquad \eta,\rho\in(0,1).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(\operatorname{pred}(p)>0\), the first test is the ratio condition \(\operatorname{ared}(p)/\operatorname{pred}(p)\geq\eta\).
Rejected steps can be represented by retaining the current iterate and decreasing the trust-region radius.
special_cases_latex: If \(m(p)=m(0)\), the feasibility-decrease lower bound is vacuous, while the actual-predicted test remains active.
Near a well-modeled solution, the ratio can approach one, permitting an unchanged or enlarged trust region.
immediate_consequences_latex: A step with nonpositive predicted reduction cannot satisfy the intended sufficient-decrease role without a separate exceptional rule.
Failure of the ratio test signals that the current model or radius is unreliable at the trial displacement.
boundary_notes: The constants and radius-update thresholds are algorithmic parameters, not universal mathematical constants.
Filter methods use a different acceptance relation and are not included in this merit-ratio definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Cauchy Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient-decrease safeguard relative to a feasible projected-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(d)=g^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Bd\) and \(\mathcal D=\{d:Ad=0,\ \|d\|\leq\Delta,\ z+d\text{ is strictly interior}\}\). With \(P\) the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\), define a constrained Cauchy step by \(d_C=-\alpha_C Pg\), where \(\alpha_C\) minimizes \(m(-\alpha Pg)\) over all \(\alpha\geq0\) for which \(-\alpha Pg\in\mathcal D\). A trial step \(d\in\mathcal D\) satisfies the safeguard when \(m(0)-m(d)\geq\kappa_C\bigl(m(0)-m(d_C)\bigr)\) for a fixed \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible trial step is safeguarded when its model decrease is at least a fixed fraction of constrained projected-gradient Cauchy decrease.
assumptions_latex: The current point is strictly interior and \(\mathcal D\neq\varnothing\).
The projector \(P\) onto \(\ker A\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step cannot provide less than the prescribed fraction \(\kappa_C\) of constrained Cauchy model decrease.

notation.meaning: Admissible linearized-feasible, trust-region, strictly interior step set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Cauchy model-decrease bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order decrease certificate for the boundary-safeguarded Cauchy point of a quadratic barrier model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If
\[
m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s)=m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})+\langle g_{k,j},s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,H_{k,j}s\rangle
\]
and \(x^{\rm cc}_{k,j}\) is defined by (13.3.5)--(13.3.6), then
\[
m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x^{\rm cc}_{k,j})\geq\frac12\|g_{k,j}\|\min\left\{\frac{\|g_{k,j}\|}{\beta_{k,j}},\Delta_{k,j},(1-\varsigma_k)d_{k,j}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the quadratic model, the constrained Cauchy point produces at least one half of the gradient norm times the minimum of the curvature-limited length, trust-region radius, and boundary-safeguarded length.
assumptions_latex: x^{\rm cc}_{k,j}=x_{k,j}-t^{\rm cc}_{k,j}g_{k,j}\text{ is defined by (13.3.5)--(13.3.6)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x^{\rm cc}_{k,j})\geq\frac12\|g_{k,j}\|\min\left\{\frac{\|g_{k,j}\|}{\beta_{k,j}},\Delta_{k,j},(1-\varsigma_k)d_{k,j}\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model-decrease bound for the constrained scaled Cauchy point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient model decrease from the first-order safeguard in a constrained Coleman–Li trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let m_k have form (13.12.5), and define x_k^{\mathrm{CSC}} to minimize m_k(x_k-tS_k^2g_k) over t\geq0 subject to t\|S_k^2g_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k and \operatorname{dist}(x_k-tS_k^2g_k,\partial\mathcal C)\geq\varsigma_k\operatorname{dist}(x_k,\partial\mathcal C). If \|g_k\|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{ubg}} for some \kappa_{\mathrm{ubg}}>0, then there exists \kappa_{\mathrm{msd}}\in(0,1] such that m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k^{\mathrm{CSC}})\geq\frac12\pi_k\min\left\{\frac{\pi_k}{\beta_{\{k\}}},\Delta_k\right\},\qquad \pi_k=\min\{\|g_k^{\mathrm{s}}\|,\kappa_{\mathrm{msd}}\},\text{ where }\beta_{\{k\}}\text{ is defined in (8.1.22)}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated model, the constrained scaled Cauchy point minimizes the model along the scaled negative-gradient ray while satisfying the trust-region and boundary-distance constraints. Under the stated gradient bound, its model reduction has the displayed lower bound in terms of the truncated scaled-gradient measure, curvature quantity, and trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\kappa_{\mathrm{msd}}\in(0,1]\quad m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k^{\mathrm{CSC}})\geq\frac12\pi_k\min\left\{\frac{\pi_k}{\beta_{\{k\}}},\Delta_k\right\},\qquad \pi_k=\min\{\|g_k^{\mathrm{s}}\|,\kappa_{\mathrm{msd}}\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform constrained-Cauchy decrease along the inner barrier iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-iteration decrease certificate expressed through a truncated first-order measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose AC.1c, AC.2b, AC.4c, and AC.8 hold; \(\{x_j\}\) is generated by Algorithm 13.3.1; \(m^f_j\) and \(m^b_j\) satisfy AM.1--AM.3, AM.4h, and AM.4i; the model has form (13.3.4); and the constrained Cauchy point is defined by (13.3.5)--(13.3.6). Then there exist \(\kappa_{\rm mdc}>0\) and \(\kappa_{\rm mdb}>0\), depending only on \(k\), such that, with
\[
\pi_{k,j}=\min\{\|g_{k,j}\|,(1-\varsigma_k)\kappa_{\rm mdb}\},
\]
\[
m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x^{\rm CC}_{k,j})\geq\kappa_{\rm mdc}\pi_{k,j}\min\left\{\frac{\pi_{k,j}}{\beta_{k,j}},\Delta_{k,j}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated algorithmic, constraint, and model assumptions, positive constants depending only on the outer index provide a uniform constrained-Cauchy decrease bound. The first-order measure is the smaller of the gradient norm and a boundary-safeguard threshold.
assumptions_latex: m^f_j,m^b_j\text{ satisfy AM.1--AM.3, AM.4h, and AM.4i}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\kappa_{\rm mdc},\kappa_{\rm mdb}>0\text{ depending only on }k:\quad m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x^{\rm CC}_{k,j})\geq\kappa_{\rm mdc}\pi_{k,j}\min\left\{\frac{\pi_{k,j}}{\beta_{k,j}},\Delta_{k,j}\right\},\quad \pi_{k,j}=\min\{\|g_{k,j}\|,(1-\varsigma_k)\kappa_{\rm mdb}\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Cauchy point for a barrier trust-region model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Steepest-descent reference point subject to both trust-region and conservative boundary-distance restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s)=m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})+\langle g_{k,j},s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,H_{k,j}s\rangle,
\]
let \(d_{k,j}=\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C)\). The constrained Cauchy arc is
\[
\mathcal A^{\rm cc}_{k,j}=\{x_{k,j}-tg_{k,j}:t\geq0,\ t\|g_{k,j}\|\leq(1-\varsigma_k)d_{k,j},\ x_{k,j}-tg_{k,j}\in\mathcal B_{k,j}\}.
\]
The constrained Cauchy point is
\[
x^{\rm cc}_{k,j}=x_{k,j}-t^{\rm cc}_{k,j}g_{k,j},\qquad t^{\rm cc}_{k,j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\substack{t\geq0\\x_{k,j}-tg_{k,j}\in\mathcal B_{k,j}\\t\|g_{k,j}\|\leq(1-\varsigma_k)d_{k,j}}}m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}-tg_{k,j}).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constrained Cauchy point minimizes the quadratic model along the negative-gradient ray, truncated by the trust region and by the conservative radius equal to one minus the safeguard fraction times the current boundary distance. This is stronger than merely requiring the resulting trial point to remain sufficiently far from the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{\rm cc}_{k,j}=x_{k,j}-t^{\rm cc}_{k,j}g_{k,j}\text{ minimizes }m_{k,j}\text{ on the constrained Cauchy arc.}

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenpoint Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-decrease safeguard based on a feasible negative-curvature eigenvector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m(d)=g^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Bd\) on an admissible set \(\mathcal D\), let \(P\) project onto the linearized feasible subspace. Choose a unit vector \(v\in\operatorname{range}(P)\) satisfying \(v^{\mathsf T}Bv\leq\theta\lambda_{\min}(PBP)\) with \(\theta\in(0,1]\), and choose its sign so that \(g^{\mathsf T}v\leq0\). Define \(d_E=\alpha_Ev\), where \(\alpha_E\) minimizes \(m(\alpha v)\) over \(\alpha\geq0\) with \(\alpha v\in\mathcal D\). A trial step \(d\in\mathcal D\) satisfies the eigenpoint safeguard if \(m(0)-m(d)\geq\kappa_E\bigl(m(0)-m(d_E)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trial step must capture a fixed fraction of the model decrease obtainable along an admissible approximate minimum-eigenvalue direction.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is symmetric and the projected feasible subspace is nonzero.
\(\mathcal D\) contains a nonzero segment along either sign of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The safeguard forces the trial step to exploit detectable negative curvature in the linearized feasible subspace.

notation.meaning: Hessian model projected onto the linearized feasible subspace.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained eigenpoint for an indefinite barrier model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-safeguarded trial point exploiting sufficiently negative curvature within the trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s)=m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})+\langle g_{k,j},s\rangle+\tfrac12\langle s,H_{k,j}s\rangle,
\]
where \(H_{k,j}=\nabla_{xx}m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})\) is indefinite and its leftmost eigenvalue is \(\tau_{k,j}<0\). Put
\[
r_{k,j}=\min\{\Delta_{k,j},(1-\varsigma_k)d_{k,j}\}.
\]
For \(\kappa_{\rm snc}\in(0,1]\), choose \(u_{k,j}\) satisfying
\[
\langle u_{k,j},g_{k,j}\rangle\leq0,\qquad \|u_{k,j}\|=r_{k,j},\qquad \langle u_{k,j},H_{k,j}u_{k,j}\rangle\leq\kappa_{\rm snc}\tau_{k,j}r_{k,j}^2.
\]
The constrained eigenpoint is
\[
x^{\rm CE}_{k,j}=x_{k,j}+t^{\rm CE}_{k,j}u_{k,j},\qquad t^{\rm CE}_{k,j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq t\leq1}m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+tu_{k,j}).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an indefinite quadratic barrier model, select a direction of full safeguarded radius that is nonascending to first order and satisfies the prescribed negative-curvature condition. The constrained eigenpoint minimizes the model on the segment from the current point along that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{\rm CE}_{k,j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x=x_{k,j}+tu_{k,j},\ 0\leq t\leq1}m_{k,j}(x),\text{ where }u_{k,j}\text{ satisfies the stated sign, norm, and negative-curvature conditions.}

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Protection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguard preventing termination at nonstationary saddle-like barrier models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) project onto the linearized feasible subspace and suppose a unit admissible direction \(v\in\operatorname{range}(P)\) satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Bv\leq-\varepsilon_H\). A protected barrier step must either produce \(d\) with \(m(0)-m(d)\geq\kappa_{nc}\varepsilon_H\alpha^2\) for some admissible \(\alpha>0\), or return a verifiable certificate that no such direction exists to the requested eigenvalue tolerance. Consequently, a subproblem solver may declare approximate second-order stationarity only if \(\|Pg\|\leq\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(PBP)\geq-\varepsilon_H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When feasible negative curvature is detected, the solver must exploit it or certify its absence before declaring approximate second-order stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is symmetric and the current point is strictly interior.
A nonzero step along the selected direction remains admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate termination requires both \(\|Pg\|\leq\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(PBP)\geq-\varepsilon_H\).

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule selecting Cauchy or eigenpoint decrease tests from local curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a quadratic barrier model with projected gradient \(Pg\), projected Hessian \(PBP\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H>0\), apply the constrained Cauchy safeguard whenever \(\|Pg\|>\varepsilon_g\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(PBP)<-\varepsilon_H\), additionally apply the eigenpoint safeguard and require the trial reduction to be at least a fixed fraction of the larger reference decrease. If neither test is activated, permit approximate subproblem termination. If a required reference direction has no nonzero admissible length because of interiority or trust-region restrictions, shorten the reference step; if every such length is zero, report a degenerate admissible set rather than successful stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use Cauchy protection for large projected gradients, eigenpoint protection for negative curvature, both when necessary, and neither only near second-order stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is symmetric and \(P\) is the feasible-subspace projector.
Reference Cauchy and eigenpoint steps can be computed to prescribed accuracy.
The admissible step set contains the zero step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful termination is allowed only when \(\|Pg\|\leq\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(PBP)\geq-\varepsilon_H\), unless degeneracy is explicitly reported.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact, approximate, and inexact barrier-step computations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_k\) be a barrier Newton equation or constrained quadratic step model at iteration \(k\), with candidate step \(p\), model objective \(q_k\), feasible step set \(\mathcal P_k\), and KKT residual mapping \(R_k(p,\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth NLP barrier steps computed by direct or iterative linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A barrier-step computation model classifies a computed step as follows. It is exact if \(p_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal P_k}q_k(p)\), equivalently its model KKT residual is zero under the applicable regularity conditions. It is approximately solved if it satisfies prescribed model-feasibility and decrease conditions without necessarily minimizing \(q_k\). It is residual-inexact at tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) if \[\|R_k(p_k,\lambda_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_k\] together with the trust-region, positivity, and sufficient-decrease conditions required by the outer barrier method. Truncated projected-CG steps are canonical inexact computations: they may terminate at the trust-region boundary, on negative curvature, or when an accuracy test is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier-step computations are exact when they solve the local Newton or quadratic model completely. They are approximate when they meet stated feasibility and model-decrease requirements without attaining the exact minimizer. They are residual-inexact when the local KKT residual is bounded by a declared tolerance and all outer safeguards remain satisfied. Iterative trust-region solvers commonly stop at sufficient accuracy, negative curvature, or the trust-region boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{exact: }R_k=0;\qquad \text{inexact: }\|R_k\|\leq\varepsilon_k;\qquad \text{acceptable approximate: model feasibility, positivity, and sufficient decrease hold}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a linear Newton system \(K_kd=-F_k\), residual inexactness is \(\|K_kd_k+F_k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\).
For a quadratic trust-region model, exactness means global minimization over the model-feasible region; first-order residual zero alone is insufficient when the model is nonconvex.
special_cases_latex: A stable direct factorization normally targets the exact linear-system step up to floating-point error.
Projected conjugate gradients yield a matrix-free approximate step and avoid factoring the Lagrangian Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: The computational accuracy criterion must be stated independently of the outer barrier stopping test.
A useful inexact step can preserve global progress even when the local model is too expensive to solve exactly.
boundary_notes: No single residual tolerance is canonical; convergence theory determines how \(\varepsilon_k\) relates to barrier and optimality residuals.
Approximate feasibility alone does not guarantee sufficient model decrease, and sufficient decrease alone does not guarantee acceptable constraint residuals.

notation.meaning: KKT or linear-system residual of the local barrier step model.
Local feasible set including linearized constraints, trust region, and positivity bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Hessian Barrier Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order Taylor model using the exact barrier-Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_z\phi_\mu(z)\) subject to \(c(z)=0\), define the barrier Lagrangian \(L_\mu(z,y)=\phi_\mu(z)+y^{\mathsf T}c(z)\). At \((z_k,y_k)\), the exact-Hessian step model is \[m_k(d)=\phi_\mu(z_k)+
abla\phi_\mu(z_k)^{\mathsf T}d+	frac12d^{\mathsf T}
abla_{zz}^2L_\mu(z_k,y_k)d,\] together with the linearized constraint \(c(z_k)+
abla c(z_k)d=0\) and any strict-interiority step restriction. Thus the curvature matrix is formed from the actual second derivatives of the barrier objective and equality constraints, not from a maintained approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic step model uses the exact Hessian of the fixed-parameter barrier Lagrangian and the linearized equality constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_\mu\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(z_k\).
\(z_k\) lies in the strict interior of the barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model curvature is \(B_k=\nabla_{zz}^2L_\mu(z_k,y_k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-Hessian Primal-Dual Barrier Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c_E:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^\ell\), and \(c_I:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable. Introduce slacks \(s\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), equality multipliers \(y\in\mathbb R^\ell\), inequality multipliers \(z\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s)\), and barrier parameter \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming with a primal-dual logarithmic barrier and exact second derivatives of the NLP Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\mathcal L(x,s,y,z)=f(x)-y^Tc_E(x)-z^T(c_I(x)-s)\) and the perturbed KKT residual \[F_\mu(x,s,y,z)= egin{pmatrix}
abla_x\mathcal L(x,s,y,z)\Sz-\mu e\c_E(x)\c_I(x)-s\end{pmatrix}.\] An exact-Hessian barrier model at \(w=(x,s,y,z)\) is the Newton model \[F_\mu(w)+J_\mu^{\mathrm{ex}}(w)p=0,\] whose primal curvature block is exactly \(
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,s,y,z)\). Equivalently, in symmetric primal-dual form its quadratic primal block is \(B=
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L\), while the slack curvature block is \(\Sigma=S^{-1}Z\). The associated step \(p=(p_x,p_s,p_y,p_z)\) is any solution of this exact linearized system, subsequently restricted so that \(s+\alpha_sp_s>0\) and \(z+\alpha_zp_z>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth nonlinear program written with positive slacks, form the perturbed KKT residual and its Newton system. The barrier model is an exact-Hessian model precisely when the primal curvature block in that system is the actual Hessian of the nonlinear-programming Lagrangian at the current primal-dual point, rather than an approximation. The slack curvature is the primal-dual diagonal matrix formed from the current slacks and inequality multipliers. A step solves this model and is shortened when necessary to preserve strict positivity of both slacks and inequality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c_E,c_I\) are twice continuously differentiable at the current point.
The stated Newton system is solvable, possibly after a standard regularization that is not part of the exact-Hessian definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,s,y,z)\) is the defining distinction of the exact-Hessian barrier model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The model is the first-order Newton linearization of \(F_\mu(w)=0\) with the exact derivative \(J_\mu^{\mathrm{ex}}(w)\).
After symmetric scaling, the primal curvature remains \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L\) and the slack block is \(S^{-1}Z\).
special_cases_latex: With no equality constraints, the blocks involving \(c_E\) and \(y\) disappear.
For a primal log-barrier model, the corresponding exact curvature is \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L+A_I(x)^T\mu S^{-2}A_I(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The model contains the true second-order curvature of both the objective and nonlinear constraints through \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L\).
Exactness concerns the mathematical curvature block, not whether the resulting linear system is solved by a direct or iterative method.
boundary_notes: Regularizing an indefinite exact Hessian changes the system used for globalization but does not turn a quasi-Newton approximation into an exact Hessian.
The definition does not assert positive definiteness or global convergence.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian of the slack-form nonlinear program.

children.title: Quasi-Newton Barrier Models

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton Barrier Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier model whose curvature matrix is updated from secant information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), replace the exact barrier-Lagrangian Hessian by a symmetric matrix \(B_k\) in \(m_k(d)=g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\). After an accepted step \(s_k=z_{k+1}-z_k\), form \(q_k=\nabla_zL_\mu(z_{k+1},y_{k+1})-\nabla_zL_\mu(z_k,y_{k+1})\). When \(s_k^{\mathsf T}q_k>0\), the BFGS instance updates \[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^{\mathsf T}B_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k}+\frac{q_kq_k^{\mathsf T}}{s_k^{\mathsf T}q_k}.\] If curvature fails, skip or damp the update according to a stated rule. The next barrier step uses \(B_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a symmetric barrier-Lagrangian curvature approximation satisfying a secant relation, using a BFGS update when its curvature condition holds.
assumptions_latex: The barrier Lagrangian is continuously differentiable at consecutive strictly interior iterates.
Accepted iterates and multiplier estimates are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under \(s_k^{\mathsf T}q_k>0\), the BFGS matrix \(B_{k+1}\) is symmetric positive definite and satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=q_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Newton Primal-Dual Barrier Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Use the smooth slack-form NLP, positive primal-dual variables, Lagrangian \(\mathcal L\), and perturbed KKT system from the exact primal-dual barrier setting. Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) be a maintained curvature approximation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming in which Lagrangian curvature is updated from iterate information rather than recomputed exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quasi-Newton barrier model at iteration \(k\) is the primal-dual barrier system obtained by replacing \(
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_k\) by a symmetric matrix \(B_k\). For consecutive accepted iterates define \[\Delta x_k=x_{k+1}-x_k,\qquad \Delta \ell_k=
abla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},s_{k+1},y_{k+1},z_{k+1})-
abla_x\mathcal L(x_k,s_{k+1},y_{k+1},z_{k+1}).\] The approximation is maintained by a safeguarded quasi-Newton update \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,\Delta x_k,\Delta\ell_k)\), such as BFGS, damped BFGS, SR1, or a limited-memory version. When imposed, its secant condition is \(B_{k+1}\Delta x_k=\Delta\ell_k\). The barrier slack block remains \(\Sigma_k=S_k^{-1}Z_k\); only the Lagrangian Hessian block is approximated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton barrier model is a primal-dual barrier step model in which the exact Hessian of the nonlinear-programming Lagrangian is replaced by a symmetric approximation maintained across iterations. The update uses the accepted displacement in the primal variables and the corresponding change in the Lagrangian gradient evaluated with the new multiplier estimates. BFGS, damped BFGS, SR1, and limited-memory updates are standard instances. The diagonal slack curvature arising from complementarity is retained explicitly and is not absorbed into the quasi-Newton matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c_E,c_I\) are differentiable and their Lagrangian gradients needed for the correction pair exist.
\(B_k\) is symmetric; any curvature or denominator safeguards required by the chosen update are enforced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining model substitution is \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_k\mapsto B_k\), with \(B_k\) updated from \((\Delta x_k,\Delta\ell_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A limited-memory model may represent \(B_k\) implicitly as \(B_k=\xi_k I+W_kM_kW_k^T\).
An inverse-Hessian implementation is equivalent when its maintained operator is the inverse of the same Lagrangian-curvature approximation.
special_cases_latex: BFGS maintains positive definiteness when its curvature condition holds or is enforced by damping.
SR1 can represent indefinite curvature but requires a denominator safeguard.
immediate_consequences_latex: Second derivatives of the objective and constraints need not be evaluated explicitly.
The complementarity scaling \(S_k^{-1}Z_k\) continues to change with every barrier iterate even when \(B_k\) is unchanged.
boundary_notes: The approximation targets the Hessian of the NLP Lagrangian, not the highly varying Hessian of the complete barrier function.
A fixed arbitrary matrix without an update or approximation interpretation is not, by itself, a quasi-Newton model.

notation.meaning: Symmetric approximation to the Lagrangian Hessian.
Quasi-Newton displacement and Lagrangian-gradient correction pair.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Newton Barrier Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled residual condition for an approximate primal-dual barrier Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_\mu(w)=0\) denote the smooth primal-dual optimality system for a fixed barrier parameter, and let \(K_k=F_\mu'(w_k)\). An inexact Newton step \(d_k\) satisfies \[K_kd_k=-F_\mu(w_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F_\mu(w_k)\|,\] where \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\). The step is shortened if necessary to preserve strict positivity of barrier variables. For superlinear local convergence, the forcing terms must satisfy \(\eta_k\to0\); the stronger condition \(\eta_k=O(\|F_\mu(w_k)\|)\) supports quadratic local convergence when the Jacobian is Lipschitz continuous and nonsingular at the solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the primal-dual barrier Newton system only to a relative residual tolerance, tightening that tolerance near a regular solution.
assumptions_latex: \(F_\mu\) is continuously differentiable near a solution \(w_*\), with \(F_\mu'(w_*)\) nonsingular.
The iterates remain in the strict interior.
Residuals are measured in a fixed compatible norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual bound defines an inexact barrier Newton step; vanishing forcing terms yield superlinear local convergence under the stated regularity.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the residual mapping at the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Controlled Inexact Newton Barrier Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F_{\mu_k}(w_k)\) be the perturbed KKT residual for \(w_k=(x_k,s_k,y_k,z_k)\), with \(s_k,z_k>0\), and let \(J_k\) be its exact or selected primal-dual Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional primal-dual barrier iterations whose Newton equations are solved only to a prescribed residual accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact-Newton barrier model chooses a step \(p_k\) and linear-solve residual \(r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\) satisfying \[J_kp_k=-F_{\mu_k}(w_k)+r_k^{\mathrm{lin}},\qquad \|r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\|\leq \eta_k\|F_{\mu_k}(w_k)\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k<1.\] More generally, a preconditioned residual criterion may be used: \(\|M_k^{-1}r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\|\leq\eta_k\|M_k^{-1}F_{\mu_k}(w_k)\|\), where \(M_k\) is nonsingular. The computed step is then truncated by fraction-to-the-boundary bounds so that \(s_k+\alpha_sp_{s,k}>0\) and \(z_k+\alpha_zp_{z,k}>0\). The inexactness belongs to the solution of the Newton system and is distinct from replacing its Hessian block by a quasi-Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact-Newton barrier model uses a step whose residual in the primal-dual Newton equations is controlled relative to the current perturbed KKT residual. A forcing term strictly below one specifies the permitted relative error, optionally in a preconditioned norm. The resulting direction is still shortened to preserve the positivity of slack variables and inequality multipliers. This definition concerns controlled error in solving the linear system; it does not by itself imply that the model uses approximate derivatives.
assumptions_latex: \(F_{\mu_k}\) is differentiable at \(w_k\) and \(J_k\) is the chosen Newton matrix.
The norm and any preconditioner used in the stopping test are fixed for the current linear solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barrier step is inexact Newton precisely when its linear residual obeys the stated forcing inequality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The unpreconditioned criterion is \(\|J_kp_k+F_{\mu_k}(w_k)\|/\|F_{\mu_k}(w_k)\|\leq\eta_k\).
An absolute-relative test \(\|r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\|\leq\eta_k\|F_{\mu_k}(w_k)\|+\varepsilon_k\) is a nearby finite-precision variant when \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) is specified.
special_cases_latex: \(\eta_k=0\) recovers an exact solution of the selected Newton equations.
A sequence \(\eta_k\to0\) requests increasingly accurate Newton solves near a solution.
immediate_consequences_latex: Krylov solvers may terminate before exact solution once the residual test is met.
The Hessian block may independently be exact or quasi-Newton; linear-solve inexactness is a separate modeling axis.
boundary_notes: A fixed iteration count without a residual guarantee does not satisfy this definition.
The definition alone supplies neither a global acceptance rule nor a convergence rate.

notation.meaning: Residual left by the approximate Newton-system solve.
Forcing term controlling relative solve accuracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalization Mechanism for NLP Barrier Steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(w_k=(x_k,s_k,y_k,z_k)\) be a primal-dual barrier iterate with \(s_k,z_k>0\), and let \(p_k\) be a local barrier-model step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear interior-point algorithms that must obtain progress from iterates not assumed to lie near a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An NLP barrier globalization is a rule \(\mathcal G\) that maps \((w_k,p_k,\mu_k,\mathcal H_k)\) to either an accepted interior iterate \(w_{k+1}\) or a recovery action, where \(\mathcal H_k\) is the acceptance history. It must impose \[s_{k+1}>0,\qquad z_{k+1}>0,\] and accept an ordinary trial step only through at least one quantified progress test: sufficient decrease of a barrier merit function, acceptability of the barrier-value/infeasibility pair to a filter, or sufficient agreement between actual and predicted reduction in a trust-region model. If no admissible trial satisfies the selected test, \(\mathcal G\) shortens or recomputes the step, contracts a trust region, or invokes feasibility restoration. Thus globalization is the acceptance-and-recovery layer surrounding the local barrier equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier globalization is the formal acceptance and recovery mechanism placed around a local nonlinear interior-point step. It preserves strict positivity and accepts ordinary trial points only when a merit function, filter, or trust-region agreement test records sufficient progress. When the test fails, it modifies the step or transfers control to a recovery mechanism such as restoration. It is therefore broader than any single line-search or trust-region formula.
assumptions_latex: A local barrier step and a quantitative merit, filter, or model-reduction measure are available.
The current slack and inequality-multiplier vectors are strictly positive.
The globalization parameters defining sufficient progress are fixed or updated by explicit rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is characterized by interior preservation, a quantified acceptance test, and a defined response to rejection.
special_cases_latex: Backtracking with a barrier merit function is a line-search globalization.
Filter line search and trust-region barrier methods are alternative globalization families.
immediate_consequences_latex: A trial point can be rejected even when it solves the local linearized equations accurately.
Restoration is part of globalization when ordinary barrier steps cease to be acceptable.
boundary_notes: Fraction-to-the-boundary truncation alone preserves interiority but does not by itself establish global progress.
The definition does not require monotonic decrease at every accepted iteration when a filter or nonmonotone safeguard is used.

notation.meaning: Stored globalization state such as a filter, reference values, or trust-region radius.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-Search and Trust-Region Families of Practical NLP Interior-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-level classification of globalization mechanisms for practical nonlinear-programming interior-point algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The practical nonlinear-programming interior-point algorithms under discussion fall into two categories: (i) methods that augment a basic primal-dual iteration with a line search, control of the decrease of the slacks \(s\) and inequality multipliers \(z\), and modifications of the primal-dual system when negative curvature is encountered; and (ii) methods that compute steps by minimizing a quadratic model of the barrier formulation subject to a trust-region constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The practical nonlinear interior-point methods under discussion are organized into line-search and trust-region categories. The line-search category controls step acceptance, the decrease of slacks and inequality multipliers, and negative-curvature modifications to the primal-dual system. The trust-region category minimizes a quadratic barrier model within a trust region.
assumptions_latex: \text{The setting is the practical nonlinear-programming interior-point methods under discussion.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Their globalization mechanisms are organized into a line-search primal-dual category and a trust-region quadratic-model category.}

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Function Barrier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-search globalization using a scalar barrier-plus-feasibility merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\mu>0\), define \(\Psi_{\mu,\rho}(z)=\phi_\mu(z)+\rho\|c(z)\|_1\) on the strict barrier domain. Given a computed direction \(d_k\) that is a descent direction for \(\Psi_{\mu,\rho}\), choose the largest trial \(\alpha_k=\beta^j\alpha_{\max}\), with \(j\geq0\), that preserves strict interiority and satisfies \[\Psi_{\mu,\rho}(z_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq\Psi_{\mu,\rho}(z_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\Psi'_{\mu,\rho}(z_k;d_k).\] Increase \(\rho\) when necessary to make the direction descending. Accept \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and terminate the fixed-parameter solve when feasibility and barrier-stationarity residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globalize barrier steps by backtracking on a scalar merit function combining barrier objective and equality-constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_\mu\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable on the strict barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted nonzero step preserves strict interiority and produces Armijo decrease in \(\Psi_{\mu,\rho}\).

notation.meaning: Barrier merit function with feasibility penalty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier Merit-Function Line Search
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\mu>0\), define the slack-form barrier objective \(\psi_\mu(x,s)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i\) on \(s>0\), with equality residuals \(c_E(x)\) and \(c_I(x)-s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth NLP barrier iterations globalized by scalarizing barrier optimality and constraint feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) and penalty weight \(
u>0\), define \[\phi_
u(x,s)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i+
u\|c_E(x)\|+
u\|c_I(x)-s\|.\] A merit-function barrier method computes a primal-dual direction \(p\), chooses \(\alpha_s\in(0,\alpha_s^{\max}]\) and \(\alpha_z\in(0,\alpha_z^{\max}]\) preserving \(s+\alpha_sp_s>0\) and \(z+\alpha_zp_z>0\), and accepts the primal trial point only if it gives quantified sufficient decrease, for example \[\phi_
u(x+\alpha_sp_x,s+\alpha_sp_s)\leq\phi_
u(x,s)+\eta\alpha_sD\phi_
u(x,s;p_x,p_s),\quad 0<\eta<1.\] Rejected trials are backtracked or replaced by a safeguarded direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit-function barrier method combines the logarithmic barrier objective and norm measures of equality and slack-equation violation into one scalar function. It uses a positivity-preserving line search and accepts a trial point only when that scalar function satisfies a sufficient-decrease condition. The penalty weight controls the balance between barrier-objective progress and feasibility progress.
assumptions_latex: The directional derivative of the selected, possibly nonsmooth, merit function exists along the trial direction.
The penalty weight and direction make the sufficient-decrease test meaningful, normally by providing a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is determined by sufficient decrease of the scalar barrier merit function \(\phi_\nu\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The \(\ell_1\) and unsquared \(\ell_2\) norms give standard exact-merit variants.
For a feasible primal method with \(s=c_I(x)\), the logarithmic term becomes \(-\mu\sum_i\log c_i(x)\).
special_cases_latex: An Armijo backtracking line search is obtained by geometrically reducing \(\alpha_s\) until the displayed inequality holds.
Separate primal and dual step lengths may be used subject to their respective fraction-to-the-boundary limits.
immediate_consequences_latex: Both objective and feasibility progress are compared through one scalar quantity.
A trial leaving the barrier domain has infinite barrier value and is rejected.
boundary_notes: Poor penalty-weight choices can overemphasize either feasibility or optimality.
Merit globalization may exhibit the Maratos effect unless augmented by a correction or nonmonotone safeguard.

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of the merit function.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Line-Search Barrier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-search globalization accepting objective or feasibility improvement without scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\mu>0\), associate each strictly interior point \(z\) with \((\theta(z),\phi_\mu(z))\), where \(\theta(z)=\|c(z)\|\). Maintain a filter \(\mathcal F_k\) of nondominated pairs. Along a computed direction \(d_k\), choose a fraction-to-the-boundary trial length and backtrack until the trial \(z^+=z_k+\alpha d_k\) is strictly interior and, for every \((\theta_i,\phi_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), satisfies \(\theta(z^+)\leq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\) or \(\phi_\mu(z^+)\leq\phi_i-\gamma_\phi\theta(z^+)\). Apply an additional sufficient-decrease test near feasibility. Accept the trial, remove dominated entries, and insert its pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a strictly interior trial when it sufficiently improves feasibility or barrier objective relative to every stored nondominated pair.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_\mu\) and \(c\) are continuous on the strict barrier domain.
A separate switching or sufficient-decrease test is specified near feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted pair is not forbidden by \(\mathcal F_k\), and the updated filter contains only mutually nondominated entries.

notation.meaning: Current set of nondominated feasibility-objective pairs.
