knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter Line Search for Barrier Iterations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\psi_\mu(x,s)=f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log s_i\) for \(s>0\), and let \(h(x,s)=\|(c_E(x),c_I(x)-s)\|\geq0\) measure constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier line searches that keep optimality and feasibility as separate acceptance objectives rather than combining them with a penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A barrier filter is a finite set \(\mathcal F_k\subset\mathbb R^2\) of mutually nondominating pairs \((\psi_j,h_j)\), where \((\psi_a,h_a)\) dominates \((\psi_b,h_b)\) when \(\psi_a\leq\psi_b\) and \(h_a\leq h_b\). A filter line-search barrier method accepts a positivity-preserving trial \((x^+,s^+)=(x_k,s_k)+\alpha(p_x,p_s)\) only if its pair \((\psi_\mu(x^+,s^+),h(x^+,s^+))\) is not dominated by any member of \(\mathcal F_k\), ordinarily with a margin such as \[\psi_\mu(x^+,s^+)\leq\psi_j-\beta h_j\quad\text{or}\quad h(x^+,s^+)\leq(1-\beta)h_j\] for every \((\psi_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F_k\), where \(0<\beta<1\). Rejection triggers backtracking; an excessively small step triggers restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter line-search barrier method records nondominated pairs consisting of the barrier objective and a feasibility measure. A positive trial step is acceptable only when no stored pair dominates it, normally with a strict margin requiring adequate improvement in at least one component. Accepted pairs update the filter, while rejected trials cause backtracking; failure to obtain a reasonable step can invoke restoration.
assumptions_latex: The trial slack remains strictly positive, so the logarithmic barrier value is finite.
\(h\geq0\) and \(h=0\) exactly when the slack-form constraints are satisfied.
The filter contains no pair that dominates another stored pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Filter acceptability is nondominance, with sufficient margin, in the two-objective plane \((\psi_\mu,h)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Without a margin, acceptability means that for every stored pair either the barrier value or infeasibility is strictly smaller.
Dominated stored entries may be deleted after adding an accepted pair.
special_cases_latex: Using \(h(x)=\sum_{i\in E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in I}[c_i(x)]^-\) yields the standard NLP infeasibility measure.
A filter may be used with either line-search or trust-region step generation; this slot fixes the line-search form.
immediate_consequences_latex: No scalar penalty parameter is needed to trade barrier value against infeasibility.
An accepted step may worsen one component if it improves the other sufficiently.
boundary_notes: Bare nondominance without a margin can admit arbitrarily small progress.
A restoration phase is needed when backtracking drives the step below a prescribed threshold.

notation.meaning: Current set of mutually nondominating barrier-value/infeasibility pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Barrier Globalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globalization by agreement between actual and predicted barrier-merit reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a strictly interior iterate \(z_k\), compute an admissible approximate minimizer \(d_k\) of a local barrier model inside \(\|D_kd\|\leq\Delta_k\). For a fixed merit or composite acceptance measure \(\Psi_k\), define \[\rho_k=\frac{\Psi_k(z_k)-\Psi_k(z_k+d_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(d_k)},\] whenever the predicted reduction is positive. Reject the step and reduce \(\Delta_k\) if \(\rho_k<\eta_1\); otherwise accept \(z_{k+1}=z_k+d_k\). Increase \(\Delta_k\) only when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\) and the step substantially reaches the trust-region boundary. Preserve strict interiority for every evaluated trial, and stop when feasibility and barrier-stationarity residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept restricted barrier steps according to actual-versus-predicted reduction, shrinking the radius after poor agreement and enlarging it after strong boundary-step agreement.
assumptions_latex: The trial step preserves the strict barrier domain and has positive predicted reduction.
The actual-reduction measure and model use a consistent feasibility treatment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted steps satisfy \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\); rejected steps trigger a smaller trust-region radius, while expansion requires strong model agreement.

notation.meaning: Ratio of actual to predicted reduction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Globalization of a Barrier Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At an interior point \((x,s)\) with \(s>0\), let \(q_k(p)\) be a quadratic model of the barrier objective and let \(m_k(p)\) model the slack-form constraint residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear barrier methods that restrict scaled primal steps and compare actual with predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region barrier method restricts the step in a scaling that becomes tighter for slack components near zero. It also enforces a fraction-to-the-boundary lower bound. The trial step is accepted only when the actual merit-function decrease is a prescribed fraction of the model-predicted decrease. Accepted steps may enlarge the radius, while rejected steps keep the iterate fixed and contract it.
assumptions_latex: The barrier subproblem has a finite approximate solution within the trust region.
The predicted and actual reductions are computed from the same accepted-step model and merit function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair of scaled step restriction and actual-versus-predicted reduction test defines trust-region barrier globalization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using \(\widetilde p_s=S_k^{-1}p_s\) converts the scaled trust region into an ordinary Euclidean ball.
The test may be written \(\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\geq\eta\) when \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\).
special_cases_latex: A composite-step method first computes a normal step for feasibility and then a tangential step for barrier-objective reduction.
Exact or quasi-Newton Lagrangian curvature may be used inside the same globalization framework.
immediate_consequences_latex: An indefinite Hessian need not make the subproblem unbounded because the trust region bounds the step.
Slack scaling discourages premature movement toward the barrier boundary.
boundary_notes: A trust-region constraint without an agreement test is only a step bound, not a complete globalization rule.
The definition does not require exact minimization of the barrier subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small-radius criterion for a very successful barrier iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-specific sufficient condition for a very successful trust-region iteration and a nondecreasing next radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose AC.2b, AF.1, AF.3, AC.1c, AC.4c, AC.8, AM.1--AM.3, AM.4h, AM.4i, and AA.1 hold. If \(g_{k,j}\neq0\) and \[\Delta_{k,j}\leq\min\!\left\{\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{mdc}}\|g_{k,j}\|(1-\eta_2)}{\kappa_{\mathrm{ubh}}(k)},\ (1-\varsigma_k)\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k)\right\},\] then inner iteration \(j\) is very successful and \[\Delta_{k,j+1}\geq\Delta_{k,j}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated algorithmic, smoothness, constraint, and model assumptions, a nonstationary inner iteration is very successful whenever its radius is below both the model-agreement threshold and the boundary-safe threshold. Consequently, the next trust-region radius does not decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: j\text{ is very successful and }\Delta_{k,j+1}\geq\Delta_{k,j}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal inner trust-region algorithm for a barrier function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner algorithm at fixed outer index \(k\), combining barrier-step construction, boundary safeguarding, agreement-ratio acceptance, and trust-region-radius updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_{k,0}\in\operatorname{ri}(\mathcal C)\), \(\Delta_{k,0}\), trust-region parameters \(\eta_1,\eta_2,\gamma_1,\gamma_2\) satisfying the referenced parameter conditions, and \(\varsigma_k\in(0,1)\), repeat for \(j=0,1,\ldots\): form \(m_{k,j}=m^f_{k,j}+m^b_{k,j}\), where \(m^f_{k,j}\) satisfies AM.1--AM.3 and AM.4i and \(m^b_{k,j}\) satisfies AM.1--AM.3 and AM.4h; compute a sufficiently reducing step \(s_{k,j}\) satisfying AA.1/AA.2 and \(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\in\mathcal B_{k,j}\). If \(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\notin\mathcal C\), or if \[\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C)<\varsigma_k\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C),\] set \(\rho_{k,j}=-\infty\) and reject the trial point. Otherwise define \[\rho_{k,j}=\frac{\phi(x_{k,j},\mu_k)-\phi(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\mu_k)}{m_{k,j}(x_{k,j})-m_{k,j}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j})}\] and accept the trial point exactly when \(\rho_{k,j}\geq\eta_1\). Choose \[\Delta_{k,j+1}\in\begin{cases}[\Delta_{k,j},\infty),&\rho_{k,j}\geq\eta_2,\\[\gamma_2\Delta_{k,j},\Delta_{k,j}],&\eta_1\leq\rho_{k,j}<\eta_2,\\[\gamma_1\Delta_{k,j},\gamma_2\Delta_{k,j}],&\rho_{k,j}<\eta_1,\end{cases}\] increment \(j\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed barrier parameter, form objective and barrier models, compute a sufficiently reducing trust-region step, reject infeasible or insufficiently interior trial points, otherwise accept according to actual-versus-predicted reduction, and update the radius according to the agreement ratio.
assumptions_latex: (\eta_1,\eta_2,\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\text{ satisfy the referenced trust-region parameter conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k,j+1}=\begin{cases}x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},&x_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\in\mathcal C,\ \operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j}+s_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C)\geq\varsigma_k\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C),\ \rho_{k,j}\geq\eta_1,\\x_{k,j},&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\quad\text{with }\Delta_{k,j+1}\text{ selected by the stated three ratio regimes}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform separation from the boundary for primal barrier iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-separation invariant and associated Hessian bounds for the primal inner trust-region barrier algorithm at a fixed outer index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(k\). Suppose AC.1c, AC.4c, and AC.8 hold, Algorithm 13.2.1 generates \(\{x_{k,j}\}_{j\geq0}\), and the applicable models satisfy AC.2b, AM.1--AM.3, AM.4h, and AM.4i. Then there exists \(\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k)\in(0,1)\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k)\qquad\text{for all }j.\] Moreover, for every \(j\) and every \(x\) satisfying \[\|x-x_{k,j}\|\leq(1-\varsigma_k)\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C),\] one has \[\|\nabla_{xx}b(x,\mu_k)\|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{bbh}}(\varsigma_k\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k),\mu_k)\] and \[\|\nabla_{xx}m^b_{k,j}(x_{k,j},\mu_k)\|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{bbmh}}(\varsigma_k\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k),\mu_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated constraint, model, and algorithm assumptions, all inner iterates for a fixed barrier subproblem remain a common positive distance from the feasible-set boundary. The barrier Hessian is bounded on the indicated neighborhoods, and the barrier-model Hessian is bounded at each iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k)\in(0,1)\ \forall j:\operatorname{dist}(x_{k,j},\partial\mathcal C)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{mdb}}(k),\text{ together with the stated barrier and barrier-model Hessian bounds}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility-Restoration Phase
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) be a constraint-violation measure, such as \(h(x)=\sum_{i\in E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in I}[c_i(x)]^-\), or its slack-form analogue.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery phases used by globalized nonlinear barrier methods after ordinary line-search or trust-region steps cannot be accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility-restoration phase is a recovery procedure invoked at an iterate \(x_k\) when the ordinary barrier step-generation or acceptance mechanism fails. It seeks an approximate solution of \[\min_x h(x)\] or an equivalent smooth constrained reformulation, and returns \(x_R\) satisfying a quantified decrease condition such as \[h(x_R)\leq(1-\kappa_R)h(x_k),\qquad 0<\kappa_R<1,\] together with compatibility with the globalization state, for example acceptability of \((f(x_R),h(x_R))\) to the current filter. For slack-form barrier methods, the restored point must also provide positive slacks before the ordinary barrier iteration resumes. Restoration terminates either with such a return point, with a feasible point, or at a stationary point of the feasibility problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility restoration is a recovery phase that temporarily makes reduction of constraint violation its primary mathematical objective. It is invoked when an ordinary barrier step cannot be generated or accepted. The phase returns only after obtaining a specified reduction in infeasibility and satisfying the method's re-entry conditions, such as filter compatibility and positive slacks, or after detecting stationarity of the feasibility problem.
assumptions_latex: The ordinary barrier globalization declares a restoration trigger, such as an infeasible subproblem or an excessively small line-search step.
A positive restoration-decrease parameter \(\kappa_R\) or an equivalent termination tolerance is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restoration is defined by approximate minimization of infeasibility and an explicit condition for returning to the ordinary barrier phase.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality and inequality constraints, nonsmooth \(h\) may be replaced by a smooth elastic-variable reformulation.
A least-squares feasibility objective \(\tfrac12\|c(x)\|_2^2\) is a smooth special formulation when appropriate.
special_cases_latex: Filter methods invoke restoration when backtracking produces \(\alpha<\alpha_{\min}\).
Trust-region methods invoke restoration when repeated rejection makes the ordinary subproblem ineffective or infeasible.
immediate_consequences_latex: The original objective may increase during restoration.
A stationary point with positive infeasibility is evidence of local failure to restore feasibility, not an optimal solution of the original NLP.
boundary_notes: Restoration is not merely taking a shorter ordinary barrier step.
Successful reduction of infeasibility does not alone establish optimality.

notation.meaning: Point returned by the restoration phase.

children.title: Soft Restoration
children.top_down_role: Recovery using ordinary directions under alternative acceptance logic.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Restoration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic soft-restoration phase for a primal-dual barrier globalization method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an accepted iterate \(z_k\), a trial direction \(d_k\), a step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), a barrier merit quantity \(\Phi_\mu\), and constraint violation \(\theta\ge 0\), form \(z_k^+=z_k+\alpha_k d_k\). Accept \(z_k^+\) under soft-restoration logic when it satisfies the restoration progress test \(\theta(z_k^+)\le (1-\eta_\theta)\theta(z_k)\) or the ordinary globalization test \(\Phi_\mu(z_k^+)\le \Phi_\mu(z_k)-\eta_\Phi\alpha_k\Delta_k\), where \(\eta_\theta,\eta_\Phi\in(0,1)\) and \(\Delta_k>0\) is predicted reduction. Otherwise reduce \(\alpha_k\); after a prescribed rejection limit, invoke a dedicated restoration subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try ordinary barrier directions under a feasibility-oriented acceptance test; shorten rejected steps and invoke dedicated restoration only after repeated failure.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\) lies in the interior domain of the barrier function.
\(\theta\) and \(\Phi_\mu\) are evaluable at every trial point.
The fraction-to-the-boundary rule preserves strict interiority.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns an accepted interior trial point or transfers control to a dedicated restoration phase.

notation.meaning: barrier merit or acceptance quantity at parameter mu
predicted decrease associated with the ordinary direction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Soft-Restoration Mode
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(w_k\) be an interior primal-dual iterate, \(p_k\) the ordinary barrier direction, and \(h\) a nonnegative feasibility measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier recovery that retains ordinary primal-dual directions but temporarily changes their acceptance test; terminology and thresholds are implementation-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A soft-restoration mode is a recovery state in which the algorithm continues to compute an ordinary barrier direction \(p_k\), rather than solving a dedicated restoration optimization problem, but accepts a positivity-preserving trial \(w_k+\alpha p_k\) under a restoration test dominated by feasibility. A representative defining test is \[h(w_k+\alpha p_k)\leq(1-\kappa_s\alpha)h(w_k),\qquad \kappa_s\in(0,1),\] together with \(s_k+\alpha p_{s,k}>0\) and \(z_k+\alpha p_{z,k}>0\). Soft restoration ends when the trial point is again acceptable to the ordinary merit function or filter; otherwise control passes to a dedicated restoration subproblem after a prescribed failure limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft restoration is an intermediate recovery mode. The method keeps using its ordinary barrier directions, but temporarily judges them mainly by their ability to reduce infeasibility. It returns to normal operation when a point satisfies the ordinary acceptance rule, and escalates to a dedicated restoration subproblem when repeated ordinary directions fail. The term does not denote a new Newton equation by itself.
assumptions_latex: An ordinary barrier direction remains computable.
A feasibility measure, a sufficient-reduction constant, and an escalation limit are specified.
All accepted trials preserve the strict positivity conditions required by the barrier method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Soft restoration is distinguished by ordinary direction generation combined with temporary feasibility-oriented acceptance.
special_cases_latex: A filter method may regard a trial as a restoration step when it achieves sufficient infeasibility reduction even though it fails the normal optimality test.
immediate_consequences_latex: No separate feasibility-minimization model is required while soft restoration succeeds.
Failure of the soft phase can trigger a full restoration subproblem.
boundary_notes: The inspected local source discusses feasibility restoration but does not provide a precise named definition of “soft restoration.”
The displayed decrease rule is a scoped candidate formalization and requires a source specific to the named variant.

notation.meaning: Required fractional feasibility decrease in soft restoration.

children.title: Restoration-Subproblem Methods
children.top_down_role: Dedicated optimization models for feasibility recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration-Subproblem Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elastic feasibility-restoration model preserving the strict interior of inequality slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality residual \(c(x)\in\mathbb R^m\), current point \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and norm \(\|\cdot\|\), solve approximately
\[\min_{x,u,v}\;\mathbf 1^\top(u+v)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x-x_k\|^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x)-u+v=0,\quad u\ge0,\quad v\ge0,\quad\|x-x_k\|\le\Delta_k.\]
Include every original barrier slack among the components of \(x\) and impose its strict positivity. Return a point \(x_R\) only if it achieves \(\|c(x_R)\|\le\kappa_R\|c(x_k)\|\), with \(\kappa_R\in(0,1)\); otherwise report restoration failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize elastic constraint violation near the current iterate, while preserving barrier interiority, and return only a point achieving prescribed feasibility improvement.
assumptions_latex: The restoration solver enforces all barrier-domain restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output \(x_R\) is interior and reduces the selected feasibility residual by the prescribed factor.

notation.meaning: nonnegative elastic variables for equality residuals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elastic feasibility restoration is a standard nonlinear-programming construction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dedicated Restoration-Subproblem Method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h(x)\geq0\) measure infeasibility of the original NLP, and let \(x_k\) be the point from which restoration is invoked.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dedicated optimization models for recovering feasibility, as distinct from reusing an ordinary barrier direction under a modified acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration-subproblem method suspends the ordinary barrier objective and computes a step by approximately solving a separate optimization problem whose objective is constraint violation. Its canonical form is \[\min_x h(x),\] possibly restricted by \(\|x-x_k\|\leq\Delta_R\) and possibly replaced by a smooth elastic formulation. For example, with residual \(c(x)\), an elastic model introduces \(u,v\geq0\) and minimizes \(e^T(u+v)\) subject to \(c(x)+u-v=0\). A computed point \(x_R\) is a successful restoration point only if it attains prescribed infeasibility reduction and is compatible with the ordinary globalization state; otherwise the restoration solver continues or reports stationarity of its own subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration-subproblem method creates and solves a separate optimization model devoted to reducing constraint violation. The model can directly minimize a violation norm or use nonnegative elastic variables to obtain a smooth constrained formulation. A point is returned to the barrier algorithm only when it reduces infeasibility enough and satisfies the normal re-entry conditions. This differs from soft restoration because the step is generated by the dedicated feasibility model.
assumptions_latex: A nonnegative feasibility measure or equivalent elastic formulation is available.
The restoration radius, tolerances, and ordinary-phase re-entry condition are specified.
Any barrier variables reconstructed at the returned point satisfy the required positivity bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining feature is a dedicated optimization subproblem with feasibility, rather than the original barrier objective, as its primary objective.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Nonsmooth norm minimization and smooth elastic-variable formulations represent the same goal of reducing violation.
A trust-region least-squares normal subproblem is a local quadratic instance of dedicated restoration.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(\min_x\tfrac12\|c(x)\|_2^2\) is a standard smooth restoration problem.
For mixed constraints, negative parts of inequality residuals can be included in \(h\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The restoration direction need not be a descent direction for the original barrier objective.
The subproblem can identify a stationary point of infeasibility when the original constraints cannot be locally restored.
boundary_notes: A feasibility-oriented acceptance test applied to an ordinary barrier direction is soft restoration, not a dedicated restoration-subproblem method.
A restoration solution with \(h(x_R)>0\) is not feasible merely because the restoration solver terminated.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative elastic variables representing signed residual correction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correction Safeguard for Rejected Barrier Trials
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p_k\) be a positivity-preserving barrier trial direction that fails the ordinary merit, filter, or trust-region acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery safeguards addressing nonlinear constraint-model mismatch or temporary rejection without changing the NLP itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A globalization correction safeguard is a conditional mapping \[\mathcal C_k:(w_k,p_k,\mathcal H_k)\mapsto\{\widehat p_k,\text{relaxed acceptance state},\text{restoration trigger}\}\] invoked only after an ordinary trial fails. It is valid when every corrected accepted trial preserves \(s>0\) and \(z>0\), satisfies an explicitly selected acceptance test, and obeys bounded-use or rollback rules. Canonical instances are: a second-order correction \(p_k+\widehat p_k\) reducing nonlinear constraint mismatch; a nonmonotone rule allowing a bounded number of relaxed steps before forcing decrease or rollback; and a restoration trigger after repeated rejection or an excessively small admissible step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globalization correction safeguard is the conditional recovery layer used after an ordinary barrier trial is rejected. It may correct the step to compensate for nonlinear constraint mismatch, temporarily relax monotonicity under a finite memory or rollback rule, or transfer control to restoration. Every accepted corrected point must remain interior and pass a stated corrected acceptance test.
assumptions_latex: The ordinary trial has failed a specified acceptance test.
The safeguard has explicit activation, acceptance, termination, and rollback or escalation conditions.
Strict positivity of barrier variables is enforced for every corrected accepted trial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A correction safeguard is characterized by conditional activation after rejection and by controlled correction, relaxation, or escalation.
special_cases_latex: Second-order correction targets constraint linearization error.
Watchdog acceptance targets temporary merit-function increase.
Restoration targets persistent inability to obtain an acceptable ordinary step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The local barrier model can remain unchanged while the globalization response changes.
Safeguards can prevent rejection of steps that are locally fast but fail a first-order acceptance model.
boundary_notes: An unconditional change to the Newton matrix is a step-model modification, not necessarily a globalization correction safeguard.
Unbounded nonmonotone acceptance without rollback is excluded.

children.title: Second-Order Correction Methods
children.top_down_role: Corrections for nonlinear constraint mismatch after trial steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Correction Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint correction after a rejected primal trial step exhibiting nonlinear residual mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(d_k\) be a computed primal step, and set \(x_k^+=x_k+d_k\). Compute a correction \(s_k\) from
\[J_c(x_k)s_k=-c(x_k^+),\]
or from a regularized least-squares approximation when this system is inconsistent. Form \(\widehat x_k=x_k^++s_k\), shorten \(s_k\) if necessary to preserve all strict barrier bounds, and submit \(\widehat x_k\) to the original globalization acceptance test. Accept the corrected point only when \(\|s_k\|\le\kappa_s\|d_k\|\) and that test succeeds; otherwise reject the correction without replacing \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After nonlinear constraints spoil an otherwise promising trial step, solve a linearized residual-correction system and accept the corrected point only under size and globalization safeguards.
assumptions_latex: The correction system is solvable or admits a specified regularized least-squares solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted corrected trial remains in the barrier domain and satisfies the algorithm's original globalization test.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Jacobian-based second-order correction is standard in constrained globalization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and local topic match, but the correction equation using J_c(x_k), the regularized least-squares fallback, the relative-size safeguard, and reuse of the original acceptance test require an authoritative source. The inventory entries concerning other second-order methods do not constitute citations for this globalization correction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Norm Second-Order Constraint Correction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider smooth equality constraints \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\), a current point \(x_k\), Jacobian \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\) of full row rank, and a primary step \(p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constraint form of the standard correction used to overcome nonlinear constraint mismatch and the Maratos effect; mixed-constraint variants require active-set or slack adaptations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The second-order correction associated with \(p_k\) is the minimum-norm vector \(\widehat p_k\) satisfying \[A_k\widehat p_k+c(x_k+p_k)=0.\] When \(A_k\) has full row rank, it is \[\widehat p_k=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k+p_k).\] A second-order correction method first tests the ordinary trial \(x_k+p_k\); when rejection is attributable to increased nonlinear constraint violation, it tests \(x_k+p_k+\widehat p_k\) before backtracking. The corrected trial is accepted only if it satisfies the same merit or filter criterion and any barrier positivity restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After forming a primary step, evaluate the nonlinear constraints at its trial point. The second-order correction is the smallest Euclidean-norm displacement whose linearized effect cancels that residual. A correction method tests the corrected trial before shortening the original step, while retaining the ordinary acceptance and interiority requirements.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is differentiable and \(A_k\) has full row rank.
The constraint residual \(c(x_k+p_k)\) can be evaluated.
The corrected point is tested for both globalization acceptability and required barrier positivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat p_k=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k+p_k)\) is the canonical minimum-norm second-order correction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\widehat p_k\) solves \(\min_d\tfrac12\|d\|_2^2\) subject to \(A_kd=-c(x_k+p_k)\).
A pseudoinverse form is \(\widehat p_k=-A_k^\dagger c(x_k+p_k)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c(x_k+p_k)=0\), then \(\widehat p_k=0\).
Slack-form mixed-constraint methods apply the same idea to the relevant equality residuals.
immediate_consequences_latex: The corrected trial directly addresses curvature-induced constraint mismatch.
The correction is tested selectively because it requires an additional constraint evaluation and linear solve.
boundary_notes: The correction is not guaranteed to be a descent direction when combined with the primary step, so unsuccessful corrected trials are discarded rather than blindly backtracked.
Rank-deficient Jacobians require a generalized inverse or regularized variant outside this canonical definition.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the uncorrected base point.

children.title: Nonmonotone Acceptance Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Temporary nonmonotone acceptance and rollback families.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Nonmonotone Acceptance with Rollback
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi_k\) be the current barrier merit value, \(p_k\) a regular barrier direction, and \(D\phi_k(p_k)\) its directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier globalization safeguards that permit temporary merit increase but retain a finite forcing or rollback mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonmonotone acceptance safeguard permits a relaxed full or partial step even when \(\phi(w_{k+1})>\phi(w_k)\), provided the relaxation lasts for at most \(M\geq1\) consecutive accepted trials and is governed by a stored reference state. By the end of each relaxed cycle it must either obtain sufficient decrease relative to the reference, for example \[\phi(w_{k+j})\leq\phi(w_k)+\eta\alpha_kD\phi(w_k;p_k),\qquad 1\leq j\leq M+1,\] or roll back to \(w_k\) and compute a step satisfying the ordinary decrease test. All intermediate accepted trials preserve barrier positivity. The watchdog strategy is the case in which regular directions are tried during the relaxed cycle and unsuccessful cycles return to the pre-relaxation iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonmonotone safeguard allows the barrier merit function to rise temporarily, but only within a bounded cycle. The method stores a reference iterate, seeks compensating decrease within a prescribed number of later iterations, and otherwise rolls back and forces an ordinary descent step. Positivity restrictions continue to apply throughout the cycle.
assumptions_latex: A finite relaxation limit \(M\), reference iterate, and sufficient-decrease test are specified.
Regular barrier directions remain computable during the relaxed cycle.
Every retained trial satisfies the method's strict interiority conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Temporary merit increase is admissible only under a finite-cycle decrease-or-rollback rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A finite-window rule may compare \(\phi(w_{k+1})\) with \(\max_{0\leq j\leq M}\phi(w_{k-j})\) rather than only \(\phi(w_k)\).
special_cases_latex: The one-relaxed-step watchdog has \(M=1\).
Setting \(M=0\) recovers monotone sufficient-decrease acceptance.
immediate_consequences_latex: A locally rapid barrier step need not be rejected solely because it temporarily increases the merit function.
Rollback prevents an unlimited sequence of unsuccessful relaxed steps.
boundary_notes: Arbitrary acceptance of merit increases without finite memory or rollback is not a safeguarded nonmonotone method.
The safeguard does not alter the defining barrier equations used to compute regular directions.

notation.meaning: Maximum length of a relaxed nonmonotone cycle.

children.title: Watchdog Acceptance Windows
children.top_down_role: Temporary acceptance regimes that postpone strict progress checks.

knowledge_statements.title: Watchdog Acceptance Windows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonmonotone trial window anchored at a previously accepted reference iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a window length \(M\in\mathbb N\), an acceptance measure \(\Psi\), and a sufficient-decrease test \(T(z,z^+)\). At reference iterate \(z_r\), permit at most \(M\) consecutive trial iterates \(z_{r+1},\ldots,z_{r+j}\) without requiring \(T(z_i,z_{i+1})\) at every step, while preserving the barrier domain. End the window successfully at the first \(j\le M\) satisfying \(T(z_r,z_{r+j})\). If no such \(j\) exists, discard the window, restore \(z_r\) and its algorithmic state, and resume with the ordinary monotone acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permit a bounded sequence of nonmonotone steps, but require aggregate progress from the saved reference point or restore that point and resume ordinary globalization.
assumptions_latex: The reference state at \(z_r\) can be restored exactly.
Every provisional iterate remains in the strict barrier domain.
\(T\) is the globalization method's prescribed sufficient-progress predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A watchdog window either produces aggregate accepted progress within \(M\) steps or returns the method to its reference state.

notation.meaning: maximum number of provisional watchdog steps
saved reference iterate and associated state

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Watchdog Acceptance Windows, but the precise finite-window protocol, aggregate test against z_r, exact restoration of algorithmic state, and return to a monotone rule are variant-specific. No cited source with a locator supports them.

children.title: Nonmonotone Acceptance Filters
children.top_down_role: Acceptance criteria permitting bounded temporary deterioration.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Acceptance Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory sufficient decrease relative to recent barrier-globalization values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Psi_k\) be a scalar barrier-globalization measure and let \(m_k=\min\{m_{k-1}+1,M-1\}\), with \(m_0=0\) and memory bound \(M\ge1\). For a trial point producing \(\Psi_k^+\), predicted reduction \(\Delta_k>0\), and step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), the finite-memory nonmonotone acceptance predicate is
\[\Psi_k^+\le \max_{0\le j\le m_k}\Psi_{k-j}-\eta\alpha_k\Delta_k,\]
where \(\eta\in(0,1)\). A trial point is accepted by this filter exactly when it lies in the barrier domain and satisfies the displayed inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a trial when it gives sufficient decrease relative to the worst recent globalization value, rather than requiring decrease from the immediately preceding value.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta_k>0\) is the predicted reduction under the chosen model.
The trial point satisfies every strict barrier bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate allows bounded nonmonotonicity while enforcing sufficient decrease relative to a finite reference window.

notation.meaning: scalar barrier-globalization measure at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-memory nonmonotone sufficient decrease is standard globalization machinery
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate role for this acceptance predicate, and the finite-memory inequality is mathematically coherent. However, the exact memory recursion and sufficient-decrease formula have no cited authoritative source or locator; standard-field rationale is insufficient to validate this particular filter.

children.title: Rollback Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery behavior following unsuccessful watchdog periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Rollback Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State restoration following failure of a provisional nonmonotone sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before starting a provisional nonmonotone sequence, store a checkpoint \(S_r=(z_r,\mu_r,\lambda_r,\mathcal F_r,\mathcal A_r)\) containing the primal-dual iterate, barrier parameter, multipliers, acceptance memory, and algorithmic auxiliary state. If the sequence fails its terminal progress test, replace the current state by \(S_r\), erase all acceptance entries generated after the checkpoint, reduce the step or trust-region parameter by a factor \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and recompute a trial direction at \(z_r\). No provisional iterate is reported as accepted after rollback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checkpoint the complete algorithmic state before nonmonotone trials; on failure, restore it, contract the step control, clear provisional history, and recompute.
assumptions_latex: The stored checkpoint contains every state variable affecting subsequent iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After rollback, the next iteration begins from the last certified state with stricter step control and no provisional acceptance history.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Rollback Recovery, but the checkpoint contents, clearing of acceptance history, mandatory contraction, and direction recomputation are implementation-specific. The symbol A_r is also not explained independently beyond the generic phrase 'algorithmic auxiliary state.' An authoritative algorithm locator is required.

children.title: Persistent-Rejection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where temporary acceptance fails to restore productive globalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Rejection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary at which repeated globalization rejection must trigger recovery or termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_{\max}\in\mathbb N\), \(\alpha_{\min}>0\), and \(\Delta_{\min}>0\). Persistent rejection occurs at iterate \(z_k\) if no admissible trial satisfies the active acceptance predicate before either \(N_{\max}\) consecutive rejections occur, line-search control reaches \(\alpha_k<\alpha_{\min}\), or trust-region control reaches \(\Delta_k<\Delta_{\min}\). At this boundary the algorithm must not continue indefinitely with the same reference state and globalization model: it must roll back, invoke restoration, regularize or rebuild the model, or terminate with an explicit globalization-failure status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated rejection becomes a declared failure once a rejection count, minimum step, or minimum radius is crossed; the method must then recover or terminate.
assumptions_latex: The acceptance predicate and trial-generation model remain fixed during the counted rejection sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Crossing any persistent-rejection threshold forbids another unchanged retry and requires a recovery transition or explicit failure report.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role correctly matches the terminal container. Nevertheless, the three triggering thresholds and the claim that crossing any one forbids another unchanged retry are implementation-level requirements, not a universal mathematical boundary. No source supports the stated alternatives or mandatory transition semantics.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier-Parameter Management Policy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mu_k>0\) parameterize the perturbed KKT condition \(S_kz_k\approx\mu_ke\), and let \(E(w_k;\mu_k)\) measure the residual of the current barrier subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer or adaptive policies governing transitions among nonlinear barrier subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An NLP barrier-parameter management policy is a pair of maps \[(\mu_{k+1},\epsilon_{k+1})=\mathcal U(\mu_k,w_k,E_k,\mathcal H_k)\] with \(\mu_{k+1}>0\), where \(\epsilon_k\) is the required accuracy for the current perturbed KKT system and \(\mathcal H_k\) records progress. The policy must distinguish continuation at the current barrier value from a transition to a new value, specify the eligibility test for that transition, and generate \(\mu_k\to0\) on any successful infinite run intended to solve the original NLP. Canonical policies either hold \(\mu_k\) fixed until \(E(w_k;\mu_k)\leq\epsilon_k\) and then reduce it, or update it at each iteration from complementarity and progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barrier-parameter management is the rule that decides when the algorithm continues solving its current perturbed KKT system, when it moves to a new barrier value, how accurately each barrier subproblem must be solved, and how the barrier values approach zero. It includes both outer monotone continuation and iteration-by-iteration adaptive policies.
assumptions_latex: Every barrier value is strictly positive.
A residual or progress measure and a corresponding barrier-subproblem tolerance are defined.
For convergence to the original NLP, successful parameter updates are required to produce \(\mu_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy jointly specifies barrier updates, subproblem tolerances, and transition eligibility.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Outer-inner management uses an inner loop at fixed \(\mu\) and an outer reduction step.
Single-loop management embeds \(\mu_{k+1}\) directly in each primal-dual iteration.
special_cases_latex: Fiacco–McCormick management reduces \(\mu\) only after the perturbed KKT residual meets a tolerance.
Complementarity-based management sets \(\mu_{k+1}=\sigma_k s_k^Tz_k/m\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A parameter sequence that decreases too slowly may require many outer transitions.
Premature aggressive reduction can drive individual slacks or multipliers toward zero and degrade progress.
boundary_notes: Choosing a centering parameter for one Newton right-hand side is related but does not constitute a complete management policy unless the resulting barrier update is specified.
The definition does not require monotonicity; adaptive policies may change \(\mu\) according to progress.

notation.meaning: Accuracy required for the barrier subproblem at parameter \(\mu_k\).

children.title: Monotone Barrier-Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Prescribed or safeguarded monotone barrier reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Barrier-Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded nonincreasing update rule for the positive barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A barrier-parameter sequence \((\mu_k)_{k\ge0}\) follows a monotone regime if \(\mu_0>0\) and every accepted update satisfies
\[0<\mu_{k+1}\le\mu_k.\]
A standard safeguarded reduction chooses constants \(0<\sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_{\max}<1\) and, whenever the current barrier subproblem meets its prescribed termination test, sets \(\mu_{k+1}=\sigma_k\mu_k\) with \(\sigma_k\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\); otherwise it sets \(\mu_{k+1}=\mu_k\). Consequently, infinitely many reductions imply \(\mu_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep the barrier parameter positive and nonincreasing; reduce it by a uniformly bounded factor only after adequate progress on the current barrier subproblem.
assumptions_latex: The decision to reduce \(\mu_k\) is made only at accepted iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter remains positive and nonincreasing, and it converges to zero if reductions occur infinitely often.

notation.meaning: barrier parameter at accepted iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: safeguarded geometric barrier reduction is standard in interior-point methods
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits a monotone barrier-parameter regime, and the conclusion that infinitely many uniformly contractive reductions force mu_k to zero is correct. Still, no citation supports the prescribed update trigger and safeguarded factor interval, so the complete record lacks required evidence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safeguarded Monotone Barrier Reduction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mu_j>0\) index outer barrier subproblems and let \(E(w;\mu)\) be their perturbed-KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prescribed or safeguarded outer-iteration regimes in which the barrier parameter never increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A monotone barrier-parameter regime is a sequence \(\{\mu_j\}_{j\geq0}\subset\mathbb R_{++}\) and transition rule such that \[0<\mu_{j+1}\leq\sigma_j\mu_j<\mu_j,\qquad 0<\sigma_j<1,\] whenever a transition occurs, while \(\mu\) remains fixed during the inner iterations for subproblem \(j\). A canonical safeguarded transition is permitted only after \[E(w_j;\mu_j)\leq\epsilon_j,\] with tolerances \(\epsilon_j\downarrow0\). The regime is complete when it additionally enforces \(\mu_j\downarrow0\), for example by \(\sigma_j\leq\bar\sigma<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone barrier regime holds the parameter fixed while solving one barrier subproblem and reduces it only after a stated residual test is met. Every actual update is strictly downward, and the safeguards ensure that the positive sequence converges to zero. Constant-factor reduction is the simplest instance, while variable factors may permit more aggressive reductions after strong progress.
assumptions_latex: A barrier transition occurs only when its eligibility test is satisfied.
To guarantee a zero limit, the reduction factors are bounded away from one or another explicit zero-limit condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At outer transitions \(\mu_{j+1}<\mu_j\), and a complete regime satisfies \(\mu_j\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With constant \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), \(\mu_j=\sigma^j\mu_0\).
The Fiacco–McCormick rule is the residual-gated monotone regime \(\mu_{j+1}=\sigma_j\mu_j\).
special_cases_latex: Two-level reduction may select between fixed factors such as \(0.2\) and \(0.1\) based on recent progress.
Allowing \(\sigma_j\to0\) near a regular solution gives a more aggressive monotone regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: The outer parameter history cannot oscillate upward.
Inner iteration accuracy is coupled explicitly to permission to decrease the barrier parameter.
boundary_notes: Monotone decrease alone does not imply \(\mu_j\to0\) if the factors approach one too rapidly.
Iteration-by-iteration complementarity updates belong to the adaptive sibling regime unless they are explicitly constrained by this outer rule.

children.title: Adaptive Barrier-Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Barrier choices informed by current complementarity and progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Barrier-Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier update driven by measured complementarity and current globalization progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At accepted primal-dual iterate \((x_k,s_k,\lambda_k)\) with \(s_k>0\), \(\lambda_k>0\), define average complementarity \(\bar\mu_k=s_k^\top\lambda_k/m\). Given \(0<\sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_{\max}<1\), a progress predicate \(P_k\), and positive bounds \(\mu_{\min}\le\mu_{\max}\), update
\[\mu_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\min\{\mu_k,\max\{\mu_{\min},\sigma_k\bar\mu_k\}\},&P_k\text{ holds},\\ \mu_k,&P_k\text{ fails},\end{cases}\]
where \(\sigma_k\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\) may depend on residual reduction and predicted complementarity. Cap the result above by \(\mu_{\max}\) when initialization requires it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate complementarity from current slacks and multipliers, then reduce the barrier parameter adaptively only when the accepted iterate satisfies a progress test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update keeps \(\mu_{k+1}\) positive, bounded, and nonincreasing while allowing complementarity-dependent reductions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but adaptive barrier updates differ materially among methods. The predicate P_k is unspecified, the rule has a positive floor, and the separate instruction to cap by mu_max is not integrated unambiguously into the displayed update. A source is needed to determine the intended formula and hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementarity-Adaptive Barrier Regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(s_k,z_k\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), define average complementarity \(\bar\mu_k=s_k^Tz_k/m\), and let \(\mathcal H_k\) summarize recent primal-dual progress.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-loop or frequently updated nonlinear interior-point regimes in which the next barrier value responds to current complementarity and progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive barrier-parameter regime selects \[\mu_{k+1}=\sigma_k\frac{s_k^Tz_k}{m},\qquad \sigma_k=\mathcal S(s_k,z_k,E_k,\mathcal H_k),\qquad 0<\sigma_k\leq\bar\sigma<1,\] or an equivalent positive state-dependent update. The map \(\mathcal S\) may use the dispersion of the products \(s_{k,i}z_{k,i}\), predicted affine-scaling complementarity, or recent KKT-residual reduction. Unlike an outer monotone regime, it need not wait for a fixed-\(\mu_k\) subproblem to be solved before changing \(\mu\). Safeguards must prevent nonpositive parameters and overly aggressive updates that destroy useful interiority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive barrier regime computes the next barrier value from the current primal-dual state, most commonly as a centering factor times average complementarity. The centering factor changes with observed balance or progress, and the parameter may be updated at every iteration instead of only after solving a fixed barrier subproblem. Positivity and reduction safeguards constrain the adaptive choice.
assumptions_latex: The state-dependent centering map returns a value in a prescribed positive interval.
The algorithm monitors sufficient progress or applies fallback bounds when the proposed update is too aggressive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next barrier value is an explicit function of current complementarity and algorithmic progress rather than a prescribed outer schedule alone.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A predictor-corrector rule determines \(\sigma_k\) from the complementarity predicted by an affine-scaling step.
A balance rule may use \(\xi_k=\min_i(s_{k,i}z_{k,i})/(s_k^Tz_k/m)\) to make \(\sigma_k\) smaller when complementarity products are well centered.
special_cases_latex: A constant \(\sigma_k=\sigma\) gives the basic average-complementarity update but removes most adaptivity.
LOQO-type rules choose \(\sigma_k\) from the deviation of the smallest complementarity product from the average.
immediate_consequences_latex: The scale of \(\mu_{k+1}\) automatically follows the scale of current complementarity.
Well-centered iterates may permit a more aggressive barrier reduction than poorly centered iterates.
boundary_notes: An adaptive rule is not necessarily monotone unless an additional constraint \(\mu_{k+1}\leq\mu_k\) is imposed.
The parameter update does not replace globalization or fraction-to-the-boundary safeguards.

children.title: Quality-Function Centering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Centering choices based on predicted direction quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Quality-Function Centering Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional selection of a centering factor using predicted residual quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\subset[0,1]\) parameterize a primal-dual search direction \(d(\sigma)\). For each candidate \(\sigma\), compute predicted residuals \(r_d^+(\sigma)\), \(r_p^+(\sigma)\), and predicted complementarity \(\bar\mu^+(\sigma)\), and define
\[Q(\sigma)=w_d\|r_d^+(\sigma)\|+w_p\|r_p^+(\sigma)\|+w_c\bar\mu^+(\sigma),\]
where \(w_d,w_p,w_c>0\). Choose an approximate minimizer \(\sigma_k\) of \(Q\) over the interval, set \(\mu_k=\sigma_k\bar\mu_k\), and compute the corresponding safeguarded interior step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the centering factor by minimizing a scalar prediction of dual residual, primal residual, and complementarity quality, then form the associated interior step.
assumptions_latex: The direction family \(d(\sigma)\) and predicted residuals are defined throughout the search interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected centering factor approximately minimizes the stated predicted-quality function within the safeguarded interval.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Quality-Function Centering Regimes, but the proposed weighted sum of residual norms and complementarity is only one possible quality function. Its weights, prediction definitions, minimization procedure, and assignment mu_k=sigma_k bar-mu_k require a specific authoritative algorithm citation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quality-function centering regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At a strictly interior primal-dual iterate \(v=(x,s,y,z)\), let \(s,z\in\mathbb R_{++}^{m}\), \(\mu=s^Tz/m\), and let \(p(\sigma)=(p_x(\sigma),p_s(\sigma),p_y(\sigma),p_z(\sigma))\) be the solution of the perturbed primal-dual Newton system whose complementarity right-hand side is \(-Sz+\sigma\mu e\), with \(\sigma\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; this slot defines an adaptive centering-parameter selection rule, not a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quality-function centering regime is specified by a nonempty admissible set \(\Sigma\subseteq[0,1]\) and a scalar quality function \(Q:\Sigma\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) computed from the predicted direction \(p(\sigma)\). It selects \(\sigma_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\sigma\in\Sigma}Q(\sigma)\). A canonical residual-balancing form is \[Q(\sigma)=w_d\|r_d^+(\sigma)\|+w_p\|r_p^+(\sigma)\|+w_c\|S^+(\sigma)z^+(\sigma)-\mu^+(\sigma)e\|+w_\mu\mu^+(\sigma),\] where the weights are nonnegative, \(s^+(\sigma)=s+\alpha_s(\sigma)p_s(\sigma)>0\), \(z^+(\sigma)=z+\alpha_z(\sigma)p_z(\sigma)>0\), \(S^+(\sigma)=\operatorname{Diag}(s^+(\sigma))\), and \(\mu^+(\sigma)=s^+(\sigma)^Tz^+(\sigma)/m\). Thus the centering choice is determined by predicted direction quality rather than by a fixed prescribed value of \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a strictly interior primal-dual iterate, a quality-function centering regime evaluates each admissible centering parameter using a scalar function of the corresponding predicted Newton direction. The function may combine predicted dual infeasibility, primal infeasibility, complementarity imbalance, and average complementarity with nonnegative weights. The selected centering parameter is a minimizer of this function over a nonempty subset of the interval from zero to one, subject to fraction-to-the-boundary steps that preserve positive slacks and inequality multipliers. This distinguishes the regime from fixed-centering and simple affine-scaling heuristics: the predicted quality of the direction determines the amount of centering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sigma_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\sigma\in\Sigma}Q(\sigma)\), where \(Q\) evaluates the predicted primal-dual direction and \(\Sigma\subseteq[0,1]\) is nonempty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\Sigma\) is a finite trial set, the same rule is \(\sigma_*\in\{\sigma\in\Sigma:Q(\sigma)\le Q(\widehat\sigma)\ \forall\widehat\sigma\in\Sigma\}\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(Q(\sigma)=\mu^+(\sigma)\) gives a predicted-complementarity rule.
The endpoint \(\sigma=0\) is the affine-scaling choice, whereas values nearer \(1\) emphasize recentering.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition permits discrete search, bounded one-dimensional minimization, or another deterministic minimization procedure over \(\Sigma\).
boundary_notes: The precise quality function, scaling, penalty terms, and tie-breaking rule are implementation-specific and require an exact algorithmic source.
No inspected supplied source stated this quality-function minimization rule with the exact scope used here.

notation.meaning: Direction-quality function minimized when selecting the centering parameter.
Predicted primal and dual residuals after the trial step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex nonlinear-programming barrier regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)-s=0\), \(s\ge0\), where \(f,c_E,c_I\) are twice continuously differentiable and need not be convex. Let \(y,z\) be the equality and inequality multipliers, \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(Z=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth, possibly nonconvex nonlinear programming with logarithmic barriers and primal-dual steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonconvex NLP barrier regime is a sequence \(\{(x_k,s_k,y_k,z_k,\mu_k)\}\) with \(s_k,z_k>0\), \(\mu_k>0\), and \(\mu_k\to0\), whose step is based on the perturbed KKT residual \[F_{\mu}(x,s,y,z)=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla f(x)-A_E(x)^Ty-A_I(x)^Tz\\ Sz-\mu e\\ c_E(x)\\ c_I(x)-s\end{bmatrix}.\] Because \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y,z)\) may be indefinite, the regime must additionally specify a curvature treatment: an inertia-enforcing regularization, an explicit negative-curvature step, or a trust-region model whose subproblem can terminate on negative curvature. The defining distinction from a convex barrier regime is that solving \(F_{\mu}=0\) alone does not distinguish minimizers from other KKT points, so the step mechanism includes a condition aimed at nonnegative reduced Lagrangian curvature or productive model decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex nonlinear-programming barrier regime applies perturbed primal-dual KKT equations to a smooth nonlinear program whose objective or constraints may be nonconvex. It maintains positive slack variables and inequality multipliers while driving a positive barrier parameter to zero. Since the Lagrangian Hessian can be indefinite, the regime also prescribes how curvature is handled—by regularizing the primal-dual matrix to a target inertia, exploiting a negative-curvature direction, or solving a trust-region model that detects negative curvature. Merely solving the perturbed first-order equations is not sufficient to characterize the regime because those equations can lead to maximizers or saddle-type KKT points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime consists of positive primal-dual barrier iterates satisfying \(\mu_k\downarrow0\) together with an explicit rule for indefinite Lagrangian curvature.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(s>0\), the equation \(Sz=\mu e\) is equivalent to stationarity of the logarithmic-barrier problem with respect to \(s\).
special_cases_latex: An inertia-controlled line-search regime replaces \(\nabla_{xx}^2L\) by \(\nabla_{xx}^2L+\delta I\).
A trust-region regime permits indefinite curvature and bounds the step by a trust region.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strict positivity implies that the logarithmic barrier and the diagonal matrices \(S^{-1}\) and \(Z^{-1}\) are well defined.
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert that every generated limit point is a local minimizer.
Nonsmooth constraints and conic barriers require different residual maps and curvature notions.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Barrier Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-step construction using a direction of negative reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For barrier objective \(\phi_\mu\) at an interior point \(x_k\), let \(Z_k\) span the tangent space of the active equality linearization. If the reduced Hessian \(H_k^R=Z_k^\top\nabla^2\phi_\mu(x_k)Z_k\) has \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k^R)<-\varepsilon_H\), choose a unit vector \(v_k\) satisfying \(v_k^\top H_k^Rv_k< -\varepsilon_H\), set \(d_k=Z_kv_k\), and choose its sign so that \(\nabla\phi_\mu(x_k)^\top d_k\le0\). Select a step length preserving strict interiority and satisfying the globalization decrease test; otherwise regularize or invoke restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the reduced barrier Hessian has sufficiently negative curvature, follow a tangent negative-curvature direction with a sign and step length safeguarded for descent and interiority.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_\mu\) is twice continuously differentiable on the strict barrier domain.
\(Z_k\) has columns spanning the null space of the equality Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed direction has negative reduced curvature, is tangent to the linearized equalities, and is oriented as a nonascent direction.

notation.meaning: reduced Hessian of the barrier objective
basis for the linearized equality tangent space

However, the exact reduced Hessian, tangent-space treatment, curvature threshold, sign choice, and fallback behavior need a source specific to nonconvex barrier algorithms; the generic inventory sections on second-order conditions do not support this record.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-curvature barrier method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At a barrier iterate with positive slacks, let \(g_k\) and \(H_k=H_k^T\) be the gradient and Hessian, or the reduced primal-dual gradient and Hessian, of the local barrier model on a step space \(\mathcal T_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonconvex barrier models; curvature is measured on the unconstrained or linearized-feasible step space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A negative-curvature barrier method is an interior method that, whenever \(H_k\) is not positive semidefinite on \(\mathcal T_k\), computes a nonzero direction \(d_k\in\mathcal T_k\) satisfying \[d_k^TH_kd_k<0,\] chooses its sign so that \(g_k^Td_k\le0\), and incorporates \(d_k\) into the trial step or follows it to a trust-region or fraction-to-the-boundary limit. If no such direction is detected, the method uses a Newton, regularized-Newton, or positive-curvature model step. The accepted step must preserve the strict positivity required by the barrier variables and satisfy the method's merit-function, filter, or model-reduction test. Thus negative curvature is used as actionable second-order information rather than being removed solely by positive-definite regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-curvature barrier method is an interior-point method for a nonconvex barrier model that explicitly searches for a feasible or linearized-feasible direction having negative quadratic curvature. When such a direction is found, its sign is chosen not to oppose the first-order model, and it is incorporated into the trial step or followed until a trust-region or positivity boundary is reached. When negative curvature is absent, the method may use an ordinary Newton-type step. Every accepted step must retain strict positivity of the barrier variables and meet the globalization test. The defining feature is the explicit use of a negative-curvature direction, not merely the observation that the primal-dual matrix is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever negative curvature is detected, the method produces \(d_k\in\mathcal T_k\setminus\{0\}\) with \(d_k^TH_kd_k<0\) and uses it in a positivity-preserving trial step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\min}(Z_k^TH_kZ_k)<0\) when the columns of \(Z_k\) span \(\mathcal T_k\).
special_cases_latex: Truncated conjugate gradients can stop when \(d^TH_kd\le0\) and move to the trust-region boundary.
A line-search method may combine a negative-curvature direction with a descent direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: At a point where \(g_k=0\) but \(H_k\) has a negative eigenvalue on \(\mathcal T_k\), the method need not declare first-order termination.
boundary_notes: A direction with zero curvature is not negative curvature under the strict definition.
The definition does not guarantee escape from higher-order degenerate saddles.

notation.meaning: Symmetric Hessian of the barrier or reduced primal-dual model.

children.title: Inertia-Control Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia-Control Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularization of a primal-dual barrier system until its inertia matches the target saddle structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the symmetric primal-dual barrier matrix be
\[K(\delta_p,\delta_d)=\begin{pmatrix}H+\delta_p I&A^\top\\A&-\delta_d I\end{pmatrix},\]
where \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(\delta_p,\delta_d\ge0\). Starting from prescribed regularizations, factor \(K\) and determine its inertia \(\operatorname{In}(K)=(n_+,n_-,n_0)\). Increase the regularizations and refactor until \(\operatorname{In}(K)=(n,m,0)\), or terminate when a regularization limit is exceeded. Solve the accepted system for the primal-dual direction and then apply the usual interiority and globalization safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularize and refactor the primal-dual barrier matrix until it has the desired nonsingular saddle-point inertia, then compute and globalize the resulting direction.
assumptions_latex: The linear solver reports inertia reliably for each symmetric factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the target inertia is attained, the accepted matrix is nonsingular and has exactly \(n\) positive and \(m\) negative eigenvalues.

notation.meaning: counts of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: target saddle-point inertia under symmetric regularization is standard in primal-dual interior methods
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and target inertia (n,m,0) fit an inertia-control method for a full-row-rank saddle system. The precise block regularization, rule for increasing delta_p and delta_d, termination limit, and connection to the barrier direction are algorithm-specific and have no cited source with an inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inertia-controlled primal-dual barrier method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a smooth NLP have \(n\) primal variables, \(l\) equality constraints, and \(m\) inequality slacks. Let \(K_k(\delta,\gamma)\) denote the symmetric regularized primal-dual matrix obtained by adding \(\delta I\) to the primal Hessian block and \(-\gamma I\) to the equality-multiplier block.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-factorization primal-dual methods for smooth, possibly nonconvex nonlinear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inertia-control method chooses regularization parameters \(\delta_k>0\) and \(\gamma_k\ge0\), possibly after repeated factorizations, so that \[\operatorname{inertia}K_k(\delta_k,\gamma_k)=(n+m,\,l+m,\,0).\] Here \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n_+(K),n_-(K),n_0(K))\) counts positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues. The Newton direction is then defined by the regularized system. The target inertia is equivalent to positive definiteness of the block-diagonal primal curvature matrix on the null space of the linearized constraints, while the zero count excludes singularity. A method is inertia controlled only if the factorization's inertia is used as an acceptance condition for the linear system; merely applying an arbitrary diagonal shift is regularization but not inertia control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inertia-control method forms a symmetric regularized primal-dual Newton matrix and chooses its primal and constraint regularizations until the matrix has exactly the prescribed numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues and no zero eigenvalues. For a nonlinear program with the stated dimensions, the target is n plus m positive eigenvalues, l plus m negative eigenvalues, and no zero eigenvalues. The target both certifies nonsingularity and expresses positive curvature on the null space of the linearized constraints. The computed step is accepted as the Newton direction only after this inertia condition is met. A fixed diagonal perturbation that is never checked against the factorization inertia does not, by itself, constitute inertia control.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{inertia}K_k(\delta_k,\gamma_k)=(n+m,l+m,0)\) is the defining linear-algebra certificate for the step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under full row rank of the constraint Jacobian, the target inertia is equivalent to positive definiteness of the primal curvature block on the constraint null space.
special_cases_latex: If the unregularized matrix already has the target inertia, one may take \(\delta_k=\gamma_k=0\).
If only the Lagrangian Hessian is indefinite, increasing \(\delta_k\) can restore the target inertia.
immediate_consequences_latex: The target zero-eigenvalue count implies that the regularized Newton system has a unique solution.
boundary_notes: Excessive regularization can erase useful second-derivative information.
The numerical reliability of an inertia count depends on stable symmetric-indefinite factorization and pivoting.

notation.meaning: Triple of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia-Free Curvature Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A residual-and-descent safeguard replacing explicit inertia tests in nonconvex primal–dual barrier steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a barrier KKT residual map \(F_\mu(w)\), a symmetric model matrix \(K(w)\), and parameters \(0<\gamma<1\), \(\sigma_0>0\), compute \(d_j\) from \((K(w)+\sigma_j I)d_j=-F_\mu(w)\). Accept the first trial satisfying \(\|F_\mu(w)+K(w)d_j\|\leq \gamma\|F_\mu(w)\|\) and \(\langle F_\mu(w),d_j\rangle\leq-\gamma\|F_\mu(w)\|\|d_j\|\); otherwise increase \(\sigma_j\) and resolve. A line search selects \(\alpha>0\) preserving strict inequality slacks and decreasing a primal–dual merit function. The method uses only linear solves, residuals, and inner products, not the inertia of \(K(w)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularize and resolve the barrier KKT system until its step gives sufficient linearized residual reduction and descent, then line-search while preserving interiority; no matrix-inertia computation is required.
assumptions_latex: \(F_\mu\) is continuously differentiable on the strict interior.
The regularized systems are solvable for all sufficiently large \(\sigma_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted direction satisfies the prescribed residual-reduction and descent safeguards without an inertia calculation.

notation.meaning: barrier KKT residual map at parameter mu

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports this inertia-free barrier safeguard or its acceptance inequalities.
Exact implementation variants differ across nonconvex interior-point methods.

However, the particular regularized system, acceptance inequalities, and merit line search describe a nonstandard implementation variant with no cited source; their compatibility and eventual acceptance cannot be assessed reliably from the stated assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inertia-free curvature safeguard
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_k(p)=g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TH_kp\) be a symmetric quadratic barrier-step model on a linearized-feasible subspace \(\mathcal T_k\), possibly with \(\|p\|\le\Delta_k\). Assume only products \(H_kv\) or model values are available; no eigenvalue count from a factorization is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale smooth nonconvex barrier methods using operator-based or black-box linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inertia-free curvature method is a barrier-step method that safeguards indefinite curvature without computing \(\operatorname{inertia}(H_k)\) or the inertia of a primal-dual matrix. Its step procedure must satisfy one of the following detectable alternatives: it returns an approximate stationary model step with a prescribed residual tolerance, it reaches the trust-region boundary, or it produces \(d_k\in\mathcal T_k\) with \(d_k^TH_kd_k\le0\) and truncates or redirects the step along \(d_k\). The resulting trial point must satisfy the fraction-to-the-boundary positivity conditions for slack and multiplier variables. Curvature is therefore certified locally through quadratic forms, Krylov recurrences, or sufficient model reduction, rather than through the eigenvalue signature of a direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inertia-free curvature method protects a nonconvex barrier iteration without obtaining the inertia of the primal-dual matrix. It works with Hessian-vector products or quadratic-model values on the linearized-feasible space. Its inner solver returns either an approximate stationary model step, a step on the trust-region boundary, or a direction whose quadratic curvature is nonpositive; in the last two cases the step is truncated or redirected accordingly. The final trial step must also preserve positivity of the barrier slack and multiplier variables. Thus curvature information is obtained from local quadratic forms or Krylov recurrences, making the definition applicable when the linear solver does not expose a reliable eigenvalue count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Curvature is safeguarded using residual, boundary, and quadratic-form tests, with no requirement to compute a matrix inertia.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Projected truncated conjugate gradients are inertia free when their negative-curvature test uses \(d_j^TH_kd_j\le0\).
special_cases_latex: Steihaug conjugate gradients stop on negative curvature or at the trust-region boundary.
Lanczos-based methods may use a Ritz vector with nonpositive Rayleigh quotient.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only matrix-vector products and projections may be needed, so an explicit symmetric-indefinite factorization is unnecessary.
boundary_notes: Failure to detect negative curvature in a finite Krylov subspace is not a certificate that the full reduced Hessian is positive semidefinite.
This definition excludes methods that rely essentially on a direct factorization's inertia count.

children.top_down_role: First- and second-order convergence targets for nonconvex barrier algorithms.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First- and second-order limit targets for smooth inequality-constrained nonconvex programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\geq0\), a feasible triple \((x,y,z)\) is first-order stationary when \(z\geq0\), \(
abla f(x)+
abla h(x)y-
abla g(x)z=0\), and \(z_i g_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\). It is second-order stationary when additionally \(d^{\mathsf T}
abla_{xx}^2L(x,y,z)d\geq0\) for every critical direction \(d\) satisfying \(
abla h(x)^{\mathsf T}d=0\), \(
abla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d=0\) if \(z_i>0\), and \(
abla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d\geq0\) for active indices with \(z_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order targets satisfy feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity. Second-order targets additionally require nonnegative Lagrangian curvature along every critical direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(h\), and \(g\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicates define the first- and second-order stationarity targets used for nonconvex barrier limit points.
review_flags: A source specifying the critical-cone convention for this inequality orientation is required.

A source is nevertheless required to verify that this precise critical-cone convention and the term second-order stationary match the intended nonconvex barrier target.
