children.title: Residual-Correction Refinement Family
children.top_down_role: Post-solve correction families for primal-dual systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-correction refinement of an interior-point linear solve
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) be a nonsingular primal-dual or reduced KKT matrix, let \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), and let \(z^{(0)}\) be a computed approximation to the exact solution of \(Kz=b\). Computations of residuals and corrections may use different floating-point precisions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic iterative refinement applied after an approximate direct or iterative solve of one interior-point Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A residual-correction refinement family is a sequence \(\{z^{(j)}\}_{j\geq0}\) satisfying, for every accepted refinement index \(j\), \[r^{(j)}=b-Kz^{(j)},\qquad Kd^{(j)}=r^{(j)}+e^{(j)},\qquad z^{(j+1)}=z^{(j)}+d^{(j)},\] where \(e^{(j)}\) is the correction-equation residual. A member of the family is specified by the residual precision, correction solver, acceptance test, and stopping rule. A standard stopping rule accepts \(z^{(j)}\) when \[\eta^{(j)}=\frac{\|b-Kz^{(j)}\|}{\|K\|\,\|z^{(j)}\|+\|b\|}\leq\tau,\] with the quotient interpreted as zero when numerator and denominator vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-correction refinement repeatedly forms the residual of an approximate interior-point linear-system solution, approximately solves the same coefficient system with that residual as right-hand side, and adds the correction. The family is determined by the precisions, correction solver, acceptance test, and stopping tolerance. Its canonical quality measure is a normwise backward residual normalized by the matrix, solution, and right-hand-side norms.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is fixed during the refinement of the current Newton system and is nonsingular in exact arithmetic.
Each computed correction \(d^{(j)}\) has a defined correction residual \(e^{(j)}=Kd^{(j)}-r^{(j)}\).
The chosen vector and induced matrix norms are compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{(j+1)}=z^{(j)}+d^{(j)}\) with \(Kd^{(j)}=b-Kz^{(j)}+e^{(j)}\), and acceptance is determined by \(\eta^{(j)}\leq\tau\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update is equivalently characterized by \(b-Kz^{(j+1)}=-e^{(j)}\) in exact update arithmetic.
special_cases_latex: Exact correction corresponds to \(e^{(j)}=0\), yielding the exact solution after one accepted correction in exact arithmetic.
Factorization-reuse refinement solves every correction equation with the factors already computed for \(K\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The refinement changes the computed Newton direction without changing the barrier model or the coefficient matrix \(K\).
The normalized residual \(\eta^{(j)}\) is invariant under common nonzero scaling of both sides of \(Kz=b\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert convergence when \(K\) is singular or when correction errors are uncontrolled.
Predictor-corrector optimization steps are not residual refinement unless the corrector right-hand side is the linear-solve residual.

notation.meaning: linear-system residual at refinement index j
residual left by the inexact correction solve

children.title: Classical Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Repeated correction of factorization-based interior-point solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based correction of a computed linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given nonsingular \(A\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), a reusable factorization of an approximation \(M\) to \(A\), an initial \(x_0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), iterate
\[
r_k=b-Ax_k,\qquad Mc_k=r_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+c_k.
\]
Stop and return \(x_k\) when \(\|r_k\|\le\varepsilon(\|A\|\|x_k\|+\|b\|)\), or report stagnation when the residual no longer decreases. In exact arithmetic, the error satisfies \(e_{k+1}=(I-M^{-1}A)e_k\), so convergence for every initial vector follows when \(\rho(I-M^{-1}A)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement recomputes the residual, solves a correction equation with reused factors, and adds the correction until backward error is small or progress stagnates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns a backward-error-qualified approximation; in exact arithmetic it converges if \(\rho(I-M^{-1}A)<1\).

notation.meaning: matrix represented by the reused factorization

children.title: Primal–Dual Residual Correction
children.top_down_role: Corrections organized around residual blocks of coupled primal–dual systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Residual Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise refinement of an interior-point Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\Delta z=b\) be a primal–dual Newton system, with \(\Delta z=(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\). Starting from \(\Delta z_0\), compute the block residual
\[
r_k=b-K\Delta z_k=(r_k^{\mathrm p},r_k^{\mathrm d},r_k^{\mathrm c}).
\]
Using the same regularized factors employed for the Newton solve, compute \(K_{\mathrm{reg}}c_k=r_k\) and set \(\Delta z_{k+1}=\Delta z_k+c_k\). Accept only when every scaled block residual satisfies \(\|W_i r_k^i\|\le\varepsilon_i\); otherwise continue until a correction limit or stagnation test is reached. The acceptance test is evaluated against the unregularized matrix \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal, dual, and complementarity residual blocks are recomputed and jointly corrected with reused factors, while acceptance is tested against the original Newton equations.
assumptions_latex: \(K\Delta z=b\) has a defined primal–dual block partition.
\(K_{\mathrm{reg}}\) is nonsingular and reusable for correction solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted direction satisfies \(\|W_i r_k^i\|\le\varepsilon_i\) for each primal–dual residual block \(i\).

notation.meaning: primal, dual, and complementarity residual blocks
regularized matrix represented by the reused factors

children.title: Mixed-Precision Refinement
children.top_down_role: Refinement regimes combining lower-precision solves with higher-precision residual evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Precision Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-precision residuals with lower-precision correction solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_\ell>u_h\) be low- and high-precision unit roundoffs. Factor nonsingular \(A\) and solve for \(x_0\) in precision \(u_\ell\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate \(r_k=b-Ax_k\) in precision \(u_h\), round \(r_k\) to the low format, solve \(Ac_k=r_k\) using the low-precision factors, and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+c_k\) in precision \(u_h\). Stop when the high-precision normwise backward error is at most \(\varepsilon\). A standard sufficient regime for contraction is \(u_\ell\kappa(A)<1\), subject to stable factorization and absence of overflow or underflow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-precision refinement uses inexpensive low-precision factors for corrections while computing residuals and accumulating the solution in higher precision.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonsingular and its low-precision factorization is backward stable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the correction iteration contracts, it returns an approximation whose high-precision backward error does not exceed \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: condition number in the chosen subordinate norm
low-precision correction accumulated in high precision

children.title: Correction Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Conditioning or rounding regimes where refinement ceases to improve residual quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Correction Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detectable loss of progress in residual-correction iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For residuals \(r_k=b-Ax_k\), window length \(p\ge1\), and reduction threshold \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), correction stagnation at iteration \(k\ge p\) is the predicate
\[
\|r_k\|>\sigma\|r_{k-p}\|
\]
together with either \(x_k+c_k=x_k\) in working arithmetic or \(\|c_k\|\le u\|x_k\|\). Once this predicate holds, further corrections computed with the unchanged factors and precision are not certified to reduce the residual. The algorithm must terminate, increase precision, rescale, or replace/refactor the correction matrix rather than declare convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement stagnates when residual reduction over a fixed window is inadequate and corrections are too small to change the stored solution.
assumptions_latex: \(r_k=b-Ax_k\) and \(c_k\) are generated by a residual-correction iteration.
\(p\ge1\), \(0<\sigma<1\), and \(u\) is the update precision's unit roundoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the stagnation predicate holds, convergence cannot be certified without changing precision, scaling, or factors.

notation.meaning: unit roundoff used for the solution update

children.title: Barrier-System Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Static model scaling and iteration-dependent barrier scaling.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Static and barrier-dependent scaling of primal-dual systems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K(\mu)z=b(\mu)\) be a family of nonsingular interior-point Newton systems indexed by \(\mu>0\). Let \(L(\mu)\) and \(R(\mu)\) be nonsingular, usually diagonal or block-diagonal, scaling matrices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal-dual Newton systems, distinguishing model scaling fixed across iterations from scaling that changes with the barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A barrier-system scaling regime is a pair of nonsingular matrix families \((L(\mu),R(\mu))\) that represents \(K(\mu)z=b(\mu)\) as \[\widehat K(\mu)\widehat z=\widehat b(\mu),\qquad \widehat K=LKR,\quad \widehat b=Lb,\quad z=R\widehat z.\] It is static when \(L(\mu)=L_0\) and \(R(\mu)=R_0\) for all iterations. It is barrier-dependent when at least one factor depends on the current slacks, multipliers, or \(\mu\). It is asymptotically balancing on a subspace \(V\) when constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\), independent of sufficiently small \(\mu\), satisfy \[c\|v\|\leq\|\widehat K(mu)v\|\leq C\|v\|\quad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier-system scaling regime applies invertible left and right transformations to each Newton system while preserving its exact solution under the inverse variable transformation. Static scaling is fixed for the whole optimization run. Barrier-dependent scaling changes with slacks, multipliers, or the barrier parameter. An asymptotically balancing regime keeps the transformed operator uniformly bounded above and away from singularity on the specified subspace as the barrier parameter tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(L(\mu)\) and \(R(\mu)\) are nonsingular for every \(\mu>0\) under consideration.
For asymptotic balancing, the subspace \(V\) is fixed and the constants are independent of sufficiently small \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(mu)z=b(mu)\) and \(L(mu)K(mu)R(mu)\widehat z=L(mu)b(mu)\) have corresponding exact solutions \(z=R(mu)\widehat z\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the Euclidean norm and square \(\widehat K|_V\), asymptotic balancing is equivalent to uniformly bounding its largest singular value and bounding its smallest singular value away from zero.
special_cases_latex: For positive diagonal slack and multiplier matrices \(S,Z\), the substitution \(\widetilde p_s=S^{-1}p_s\) changes a diagonal barrier block \(\Sigma=S^{-1}Z\) into \(S\Sigma S=SZ\).
A common scalar multiple of \(L\) and its reciprocal applied to \(R\) leaves \(LKR\) unchanged.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact primal-dual directions are invariant under the scaling after mapping back by \(R\).
Static model equilibration and iteration-dependent barrier preconditioning are distinct regimes even when both use diagonal matrices.
boundary_notes: Uniform balancing may fail because of rank-deficient constraint Jacobians or singular reduced Hessians unrelated to barrier scaling.
The definition does not claim that a favorable condition number guarantees small componentwise error.

notation.meaning: subspace on which uniform balancing is required

source_refs.locator: Section 19.3, discussion following the symmetric primal-dual systems (19.12), (19.15), and (19.16), including the substitutions that transform the barrier diagonal block

children.title: Static Model Scaling
children.top_down_role: Problem-data scaling chosen before or between interior-point solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Static Model Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed diagonal change of coordinates for the Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Kz=b\) be a Newton system and let \(T\) be a fixed nonsingular diagonal matrix selected from model data before the barrier iterations. Under the coordinate change \(z=T\widehat z\), the symmetrically scaled system is
\[
(T^\top K T)\widehat z=T^\top b,
\qquad z=T\widehat z.
\]
This representation is algebraically equivalent to the original system in exact arithmetic. Static model scaling means that \(T\) is not changed with the barrier parameter or current primal–dual iterate; consequently, stopping residuals must either be evaluated in original coordinates or transformed consistently by \(T^{-\top}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static scaling applies one fixed diagonal coordinate transformation to every Newton system and recovers the original direction by the inverse coordinate map.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), and \(T\) is fixed, diagonal, and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving \((T^\top K T)\widehat z=T^\top b\) and setting \(z=T\widehat z\) is exactly equivalent to solving \(Kz=b\).

children.title: Dynamic Barrier-Metric Scaling
children.top_down_role: Iteration-dependent scaling induced by barrier geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Barrier-Metric Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterate-dependent diagonal balancing of complementarity equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For positive orthant variables \(x,s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), define \(X=\operatorname{diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s)\), and
\[
D=(XS^{-1})^{1/2}.
\]
With \(\Delta x=D\Delta u\) and \(\Delta s=D^{-1}\Delta v\), the linearized complementarity term satisfies
\[
S\Delta x+X\Delta s=(XS)^{1/2}(\Delta u+\Delta v).
\]
Because \(D\) changes with the current strictly positive iterate, this is dynamic barrier-metric scaling. It balances the two complementarity coefficients componentwise, while all remaining Newton blocks and residual norms must be transformed consistently with the same coordinate change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic barrier scaling uses current positive primal and dual variables to balance the two coefficients in each linearized complementarity equation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(S\) are diagonal matrices formed from the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution yields \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=(XS)^{1/2}(\Delta u+\Delta v)\), with equal componentwise coefficients.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices of current primal and dual slack variables
scaled primal and dual direction components

children.title: Scaling Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Combined effects of model scaling and barrier-metric scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning bounds for composed static and dynamic scalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_s\) be a fixed static scaling, let \(T_d(\mu)\) be a barrier-dependent scaling, and set \(T(\mu)=T_sT_d(\mu)\). For nonsingular \(K(\mu)\), the congruently scaled matrix \(\widehat K(\mu)=T(\mu)^\top K(\mu)T(\mu)\) satisfies
\[
\frac{\kappa_2(K(\mu))}{\kappa_2(T(\mu))^2}
\le \kappa_2(\widehat K(\mu))
\le \kappa_2(T(\mu))^2\kappa_2(K(\mu)).
\]
Thus static and dynamic scalings may reinforce or undo each other. Their interaction is benign when both \(\kappa_2(T(\mu))\) and \(\kappa_2(\widehat K(\mu))\) remain controlled, and adverse when their product creates extreme component ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static and barrier-dependent transformations compose multiplicatively; their combined condition number determines whether scaling improves or worsens the Newton system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed two-sided condition-number bounds govern reinforcement and cancellation between the two scaling regimes.

notation.meaning: Newton matrix after the composed congruence scaling

children.title: Extreme-Scaling Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where scale disparities undermine stability or solution accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Scaling Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of recoverable accuracy under an ill-conditioned coordinate map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z=T\widehat z\) with nonsingular diagonal \(T\), and suppose the scaled solution is perturbed to \(\widehat z+\delta\widehat z\). Then
\[
\frac{\|T\delta\widehat z\|}{\|T\widehat z\|}
\le \kappa(T)\frac{\|\delta\widehat z\|}{\|\widehat z\|}.
\]
Consequently, if scaled arithmetic introduces relative errors of order \(u\), the boundary \(u\kappa(T)\gtrsim1\) admits order-one relative error after unscaling and provides no uniform digit-accuracy guarantee. Scaling is also invalid when forming \(T\), \(T^{-1}\), or transformed matrix entries overflows, underflows to zero, or produces nonfinite values. These are extreme-scaling failure boundaries independently of scaled residual size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the scaling map is too ill-conditioned, small scaled-coordinate errors become order-one original-coordinate errors; overflow and underflow are additional hard boundaries.
assumptions_latex: \(u\) is the unit roundoff of the relevant arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(u\kappa(T)\gtrsim1\), unscaled accuracy is not uniformly guaranteed; overflow, zero underflow, or nonfinite transformed data invalidates the scaling.

notation.meaning: condition number of the scaling map

children.title: Near-Singular Factorization Boundary
children.top_down_role: Stability regimes caused by dependent constraints and near-singularity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical boundary for a nearly singular interior-point factorization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be a symmetric positive-semidefinite normal-equations matrix, such as \(M_k=A D_k^2A^T\), and let a Cholesky-type elimination produce candidate pivots \(p_{k,1},\ldots,p_{k,m}\). Fix a relative pivot tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point sparse direct factorization of normal equations near rank deficiency or severe barrier-induced ill conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The near-singular factorization boundary at iteration \(k\) is the event set \[\mathcal S_{\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}}=\left\{M_k:\min_i p_{k,i}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}\max_{j<i}p_{k,j}\right\},\] with a nonpositive computed pivot included automatically. Equivalently, a factorization crosses the boundary at the first index \(i\) for which no remaining diagonal candidate satisfies \[p_{k,i}\geq\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}\max_{j<i}p_{k,j}.\] A spectral near-singularity indicator is \(\sigma_{min}(M_k)\leq	au_{spec}\sigma_{max}(M_k)\); it defines the same qualitative regime but is not identical to a pivot test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The near-singular factorization boundary is reached when a pivot in the evolving factorization is too small relative to previously accepted pivots, or becomes nonpositive through singularity or roundoff. A related spectral boundary compares the smallest and largest singular values. The pivot and spectral versions diagnose the same numerical regime but need not trigger at exactly the same matrix because pivot sizes also depend on ordering and elimination history.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\) is symmetric and positive semidefinite in exact arithmetic.
Candidate pivots are measured after the chosen symmetric ordering and all preceding elimination updates.
\(\tau_{\mathrm{piv}}>0\) is fixed before classifying a factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Crossing \(\mathcal S_{tau_{\mathrm{piv}}}\) classifies the current factorization as numerically near singular under the stated pivot rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The spectral indicator is \(\kappa_2(M_k)\geq1/\tau_{spec}\) when \(M_k\) is nonsingular.
special_cases_latex: An exactly zero pivot caused by dependent constraint rows lies on the boundary for every positive tolerance.
For \(M_k=AD_k^2A^T\), loss of rank in the limiting basic-column submatrix can drive the system into this regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: A boundary crossing calls for a declared numerical rank, regularization, delayed pivoting, or a different system formulation before an ordinary Cholesky solve can be trusted.
The classification depends on scaling and ordering; it is not an invariant statement about the original optimization model.
boundary_notes: Small pivots caused solely by poor scaling are numerically important even if \(M_k\) is nonsingular in exact arithmetic.
This definition does not identify a unique universal tolerance.

notation.meaning: candidate diagonal pivot at elimination index i

children.title: Constraint Rank Deficiency
children.top_down_role: Dependent constraint structures affecting interior-point linear systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Rank Deficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exact row dependence in an equality-constraint Jacobian and its effect on an unregularized KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) be the equality-constraint Jacobian. Constraint rank deficiency means
\[
\operatorname{rank}(A)<m,
\]
equivalently, there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\). Consequently, for every symmetric \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), the unregularized saddle-point matrix
\[
K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
is singular because \(K(0,y)^{\mathsf T}=0\). Thus nonsingularity of this KKT form requires full row rank of \(A\), although full row rank alone does not ensure nonsingularity without an appropriate condition on \(H\) over \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent constraint rows create a nonzero null vector in the multiplier block, making the unregularized KKT matrix singular. Full row rank is necessary but not by itself sufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\Longrightarrow K\text{ is singular}.\)
review_flags: Exact saddle-point rank claim is standard, but no supplied locator directly addresses rank-deficient KKT systems.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition and KKT singularity implication are mathematically precise and fit the terminal container, but the nontrivial saddle-point claim has no cited source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatibility and Multiplier Nonuniqueness Under Row Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of exact equality-row dependence for linearized feasibility and stationarity multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\). The equation \(Ap=c\) is solvable if and only if
\[
y^{\mathsf T}c=0\quad\text{for every }y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T}).
\]
Moreover, if a stationarity equation contains \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) and \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\setminus\{0\}\), then every \(\lambda+t y\), \(t\in\mathbb R\), produces the same stationarity term. Thus compatible dependent constraints generally admit nonunique multipliers, while violation of the compatibility condition makes the linearized constraint equations inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent constraint rows impose compatibility conditions on the constraint right-hand side and make multipliers nonunique along the left null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ap=c\) is solvable exactly when \(c\perp\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}(\lambda+ty)=A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) for every \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: left null space encoding equality-row dependencies

children.title: Small-Pivot Detection
children.top_down_role: Numerical identification of weak or unstable factorization pivots.

knowledge_statements.title: Small-Pivot Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scale-aware numerical condition for flagging unstable pivots during symmetric indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a symmetric matrix \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is factorized with permutations as \(P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), where each diagonal pivot block \(D_j\) is of order one or two. Given a relative threshold \(\tau>0\) and scale \(s_j>0\), declare pivot block \(D_j\) small when
\[
\sigma_{\min}(D_j)\leq \tau s_j.
\]
For a scalar pivot this reduces to \(|d_j|\leq\tau s_j\). A permissible scale is the norm of the active frontal matrix before the pivot is accepted. The test is scale invariant when both \(D_j\) and \(s_j\) scale identically; it diagnoses potential numerical instability rather than proving exact singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pivot is flagged when its smallest singular value is small relative to the active matrix scale. The test warns of instability but does not certify exact singularity.
assumptions_latex: \(P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) uses one-by-one or two-by-two pivot blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\min}(D_j)\leq\tau s_j\) flags the pivot block as numerically small.

notation.meaning: Current scalar or two-by-two pivot block.

review_flags: The supplied stability locator does not directly specify a symmetric-indefinite small-pivot test.
Threshold and scaling convention require solver-specific source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scale-relative test is plausible and correctly distinguished from an exact singularity certificate, but the threshold, scale choice, and block-pivot convention are solver-dependent and unsupported by a source.

children.title: Dependency Handling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural treatments for redundant or nearly dependent constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency Handling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-revealing elimination and regularization alternatives for dependent equality constraints in interior-point linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), right-hand side \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and tolerance \(\tau\), compute a rank-revealing factorization and estimate \(r=\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(A)\). If \(r=m\), retain all rows. If \(r<m\) and the equations are consistent to tolerance, select \(r\) independent rows, solve the reduced KKT system, and reconstruct or report nonunique multipliers. Otherwise retain the rows and replace the zero multiplier block by \(-\delta I\), where \(\delta>0\), then solve the regularized system. Stop when the factorization accepts all pivots; output the primal step, the chosen independent-row set or regularization parameter, and the multiplier convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detect numerical rank, retain full-rank systems, eliminate consistent dependent rows when possible, or regularize the multiplier block. Report the chosen regime because multipliers may be nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output uses either an independent-row KKT system or a dual-regularized KKT system with accepted numerical pivots.

notation.meaning: Estimated numerical row rank of the constraint Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Regularization Is Not Exact Constraint Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between equivalence-preserving dependency removal and perturbative dual regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\delta>0\), the dual-regularized system
\[
\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\delta I\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}b_p\\b_c\end{pmatrix}
\]
has second block equation
\[
Ap-b_c=\delta\lambda.
\]
Therefore it solves the original constraint equation \(Ap=b_c\) only when \(\lambda=0\) or when the resulting residual is otherwise accepted as an inexact solve. Dual regularization can make a singular saddle-point matrix nonsingular, but it does not repair an inconsistent equality right-hand side and is not algebraically equivalent to removing redundant compatible rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive multiplier-block regularization perturbs the constraint equation; it stabilizes a solve but is not an exact substitute for consistent redundant-row removal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original constraint residual equals \(\delta\lambda\), so dual regularization is generally perturbative rather than equivalence-preserving.

notation.meaning: residual in the original linearized equality equation

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Regularization Is Not Exact Constraint Elimination

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Independent-Row Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving removal of exactly redundant linearized equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_I\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) be a selected full-row-rank submatrix whose rows span the row space of \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Then there is a full-column-rank matrix \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) with
\[
A=RA_I.
\]
Writing \(c_I\) for the selected components of \(c\), the systems \(Ap=c\) and \(A_Ip=c_I\) are equivalent if and only if \(c=Rc_I\). In that compatible regime,
\[
A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=A_I^{\mathsf T}(R^{\mathsf T}\lambda),
\]
so a reduced multiplier is \(\nu=R^{\mathsf T}\lambda\); full multipliers are generally nonunique when \(r<m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly redundant rows may be removed without changing primal steps only when their right-hand sides obey the same dependencies; reduced multipliers aggregate the original multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(A=RA_I\) and \(c_I\) selects the matching entries of \(c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ap=c\Longleftrightarrow A_Ip=c_I\) exactly when \(c=Rc_I\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=A_I^{\mathsf T}R^{\mathsf T}\lambda\).

children.top_down_role: Regimes where rank ambiguity or pivot collapse compromises reliable linear solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singularity Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise perturbation boundary for linear solves approaching singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, \(Mx=b\), and \((M+\Delta M)(x+\Delta x)=b+\Delta b\). For a subordinate norm, set \(\varepsilon=\|\Delta M\|/\|M\|\) and \(\kappa(M)=\|M\|\|M^{-1}\|\). If \(\kappa(M)\varepsilon<1\) and \(b\neq0\), then
\[
\frac{\|\Delta x\|}{\|x\|}\leq
\frac{\kappa(M)}{1-\kappa(M)\varepsilon}
\left(\varepsilon+\frac{\|\Delta b\|}{\|b\|}\right).
\]
As \(\kappa(M)\varepsilon\) approaches one, this guarantee diverges. At or beyond that boundary, normwise perturbation analysis no longer ensures that the perturbed matrix is nonsingular or that the computed step is accurate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-solve sensitivity grows with the condition number and loses its finite guarantee when the matrix perturbation reaches the reciprocal-condition-number boundary.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is subordinate to the vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed relative-error bound holds, and its stability boundary is \(\kappa(M)\varepsilon=1\).

notation.meaning: Normwise condition number of the linear system matrix.
Change in the exact solution under data perturbation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-to-Forward-Error Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy boundary for a computed solution of a fixed near-singular linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, \(Mx=b\) with \(b\ne0\), and let \(\widehat x\) have residual \(r=b-M\widehat x\). For any subordinate norm,
\[
\frac{\|\widehat x-x\|}{\|x\|}
\le \kappa(M)\frac{\|r\|}{\|b\|},
\qquad \kappa(M)=\|M\|\,\|M^{-1}\|.
\]
Thus a small relative residual is not a uniform forward-accuracy certificate when \(\kappa(M)\) is large; at singularity, no finite inverse-based bound exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near singularity, the condition number can amplify a small linear residual into a large step error, and singularity removes the inverse-based guarantee entirely.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is subordinate to the vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat x-x\|/\|x\|\le\kappa(M)\|r\|/\|b\|\), with no finite inverse-based extension to singular \(M\).

notation.meaning: original-system residual of the computed solution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compositional calculus of reversible presolve reductions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=(f,c,\ell,u)\) denote a finite-dimensional optimization model with feasible set \(F(P)\) and objective value function \(f\). A structural reduction acts on the model data rather than on a barrier iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact presolve transformations equipped with explicit recovery maps; numerical tolerances and heuristic eliminations are excluded from the exact equivalence clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structural presolve rule is a triple \(T=(P',\rho_T,delta_T)\), where \(P'=T(P)\) is a reduced model, \(\rho_T:F(P')\to F(P)\) is a primal recovery map, and \(\delta_T\) is a dual or certificate recovery map, such that \[f(\rho_T(y))=f'(y)+\kappa_T\quad\text{for every }y\in F(P')\] for a stored constant \(\kappa_T\), and every optimal solution of \(P'\) recovers to an optimal solution of \(P\). The structural presolve calculus is the closure of such rules under composition: \[T_r\circ\cdots\circ T_1=(P_r,rho_{T_1}\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{T_r},delta_{T_1}\circ\cdots\circ\delta_{T_r}).\] A rule may instead terminate with an exact certificate of infeasibility or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural presolve calculus consists of composable exact model reductions. Each reduction stores enough information to recover primal solutions and, where applicable, dual variables or certificates. Objective values are preserved up to a stored additive constant. Recovery maps compose in reverse reduction order. A presolver may also terminate early when a reduction yields a valid infeasibility or unboundedness certificate.
assumptions_latex: Every reduction rule states the domain conditions under which it is exact.
Every eliminated quantity needed after the solve is retained in the recovery data.
Composed recovery maps are defined on the feasible set of the final reduced model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimal solutions and supported certificates of the terminal reduced model map back to corresponding objects for the original model through the composed recovery maps.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For minimization, exact value preservation may be written \(\inf P=inf P_r+sum_{i=1}^r\kappa_{T_i}\), provided neither problem terminates with an infeasibility or unboundedness certificate.
special_cases_latex: Row-singleton elimination fixes one variable and stores its substitution formula.
Zero-row, zero-column, forcing-row, redundant-bound, and free-column-singleton reductions are members when their exact domain tests hold.
immediate_consequences_latex: The order of reductions matters computationally because one rule can expose the pattern required by another.
The final interior-point system is formed for \(P_r\), while returned solutions are expressed in the variables of \(P\).
boundary_notes: Heuristic deletion based only on a numerical tolerance is not exact unless its perturbation semantics are stated.
Presolve transformations need not preserve sparsity or conditioning even when they preserve optimal solutions.

notation.meaning: primal recovery map for reduction T

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence-preserving reductions applied before barrier iterations, together with a reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a constrained problem \(\min\{f(x):c(x)=0,\ l\leq x\leq u\}\), first declare the bound set infeasible if some finite bounds satisfy \(l_i>u_i\). For every component satisfying the exact equality \(l_i=u_i=\alpha_i\in\mathbb{R}\), substitute \(x_i=\alpha_i\) in the objective and all constraints and remove that variable. Remove any equality constraint that becomes identically zero after substitution, and declare infeasibility if an equality constraint becomes a nonzero constant. Apply only bijective affine domain transformations to the remaining one-sided, two-sided, or free variables, recording every substitution. Stop when no selected exact reduction applies. Output either an infeasibility certificate from an exact contradiction or the reduced problem with a reconstruction map \(R\). Every feasible reduced point \(z\) then reconstructs to an original feasible point \(x=R(z)\), and every original feasible point has a corresponding reduced representation with the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact presolve detects contradictory bounds or nonzero constant equalities, eliminates exactly fixed variables and zero identities, applies recorded domain transformations, and returns either a valid infeasibility certificate or an equivalent reduced problem with a reconstruction map.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\) are defined on the points considered.
Bounds may be finite or infinite.
Only exact contradictions, exact fixed bounds, exact constant constraints, and bijective affine substitutions are used for the stated equivalence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The output is either an exact infeasibility certificate or an equivalent reduced problem with reconstruction map }R.\)

notation.meaning: Exact fixed value of variable component i.
Map reconstructing original variables from reduced variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Presolve transformation preceding interior iterations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the bounded-form linear model \(P:\min c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(\ell\leq x\leq u\), allowing infinite bound components. Let \(T\) be a finite sequence of exact structural reductions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve completed before the first barrier iteration, with postsolve recovery of eliminated primal and dual quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interior-point presolve is a map \[T:(A,b,c,ell,u)\mapsto(\bar A,bar b,bar c,bar\ell,bar u;mathcal R)\] executed before interior iterations, where \(\mathcal R\) is recovery data and the reduced model has the same optimization status as the original. If the reduced model is solved at \(\bar x\), postsolve recovery returns \(x=rho_{\mathcal R}(\bar x)\) satisfying \[Ax=b,qquad \ell\leq x\leq u,qquad c^Tx=bar c^T\bar x+kappa.\] The presolve may instead return a valid infeasibility or unboundedness certificate. Its interior-point specialization requires the barrier and Newton systems to be constructed only after \(T\) terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior-point presolve is an exact preprocessing map applied before any barrier iterations. It reduces variables, constraints, and bounds, retains recovery data, and preserves feasibility status and objective values up to a stored constant. The interior-point method solves only the reduced model; postsolve reconstructs an original-space solution. Presolve may also certify infeasibility or unboundedness without calling the interior solver.
assumptions_latex: Every applied reduction satisfies its exact structural test on the current model.
The recovery record \(\mathcal R\) contains substitutions, deleted-row information, objective offsets, and any dual recovery data required by the chosen rules.
If a reduced solution is returned, it satisfies the reduced constraints to the postsolve acceptance tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced barrier problem is solved in \(\bar x\), and \(\rho_{\mathcal R}(\bar x)\) reconstructs a status- and value-consistent solution of the original model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Presolve followed by postsolve is an optimization-equivalent reduction when \(\operatorname{argmin}P\) contains \(\rho_{\mathcal R}(\operatorname{argmin}\bar P)\) and \(\inf P=inf\bar P+kappa\).
special_cases_latex: For a row singleton \(A_{kj}x_j=b_k\), presolve fixes \(x_j=b_k/A_{kj}\) and declares infeasibility if this value violates its bounds.
For a free column singleton, presolve eliminates the variable using its unique row and stores the substitution needed for postsolve.
immediate_consequences_latex: Reduction of rows or columns reduces the dimensions of the subsequently formed primal-dual linear systems.
Recursive application is permitted because one elimination can expose another singleton or redundant bound.
boundary_notes: Presolve is distinct from iteration-dependent regularization and scaling.
A numerically approximate reduction requires explicit tolerances and may not preserve exact status.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact transformations for fixed, bounded, one-sided, and free variables
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a scalar model variable have domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R\). A domain transformation represents it as \(x=\phi(w)\) with auxiliary variables \(w\) in a standard nonnegative orthant or removes it when its value is fixed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine exact transformations used before an interior-point solve; nonlinear reparameterizations are outside scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variable-domain transformation taxonomy consists of the following exact affine cases. A fixed variable with \(D=\{a\}\) is eliminated by \(x=a\). A lower-bounded variable with \(D=[ell,infty)\) is represented by \(x=ell+w\), \(w\geq0\). An upper-bounded variable with \(D=(-infty,u]\) is represented by \(x=u-w\), \(w\geq0\). A free variable with \(D=mathbb R\) may be kept free or split as \(x=w^+-w^-\), \(w^+,w^-\geq0\). A doubly bounded variable with \(D=[ell,u]\) may be kept with explicit bounds or represented by \(x=ell+w\), \(w+v=u-ell\), \(w,v\geq0\). Each case includes its inverse recovery formula on the represented domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy classifies exact affine representations by the original variable domain. Fixed variables are substituted out. One-sided variables become a shifted nonnegative variable. Free variables are either retained or split into positive and negative parts. Doubly bounded variables are retained with bounds or represented by a nonnegative variable and an upper-bound slack. Each transformation must include a recovery formula.
assumptions_latex: For a doubly bounded variable, \(\ell\leq u\).
Introduced auxiliary variables satisfy every displayed nonnegativity and linking constraint.
Objective and constraint coefficients are transformed by substitution of the selected affine representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every listed case, the image of the auxiliary feasible domain under \(\phi\) is exactly the original scalar domain \(D\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The split-free representation is nonunique because \((w^+,w^-)\) and \((w^++t,w^-+t)\) represent the same \(x\) for every \(t\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: A zero-width interval \(\ell=u\) is the fixed-variable case.
A native free-variable KKT formulation avoids the duplicated columns introduced by splitting.
immediate_consequences_latex: Splitting a free variable can create an unbounded auxiliary solution set even when the represented variable converges.
Keeping explicit upper bounds can yield a smaller Newton system than converting every bound to standard form.
boundary_notes: These transformations preserve feasible points and objective values but need not preserve conditioning or uniqueness in auxiliary variables.
Integer, semicontinuous, and disjunctive domains are not covered.

notation.meaning: affine recovery map from auxiliary to original variable

children.title: Free-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Alternative interior-point representations for variables without finite bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Free-Variable Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference-of-nonnegative-variables representation of an unrestricted scalar variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an unrestricted scalar variable \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), introduce \(x^{+},x^{-}\geq0\) and substitute
\[
x=x^{+}-x^{-}.
\]
The map \((x^{+},x^{-})\mapsto x\) is surjective: one representation is \(x^{+}=\max\{x,0\}\) and \(x^{-}=\max\{-x,0\}\). It is not injective, since \((x^{+}+t,x^{-}+t)\) represents the same \(x\) for every \(t\geq0\). Consequently, replacing \(x\) by this difference preserves feasible objective and constraint values after substitution, but introduces one extra degree of representation and two nonnegativity-bound variables for barrier treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted variable equals the difference of two nonnegative variables. The representation is always possible but nonunique, introducing a redundant direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x^{+}-x^{-}:x^{+},x^{-}\geq0\}=\mathbb{R}\), and the representation is nonunique.

children.title: Fixed-Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal or substitution of variables fixed by coincident bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact substitution that removes a variable whose lower and upper bounds coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a problem with variable \(x=(x_i,x_{-i})\) and coincident finite bounds \(l_i=u_i=\alpha\). Replace every occurrence of \(x_i\) in the objective and constraints by \(\alpha\), producing reduced functions
\[
\widehat f(x_{-i})=f(\alpha,x_{-i}),\qquad
\widehat c(x_{-i})=c(\alpha,x_{-i}).
\]
Projection onto \(x_{-i}\) is a bijection between feasible points of the original problem and feasible points of the reduced problem; its inverse inserts \(x_i=\alpha\). Corresponding objective values agree. Thus the variable and its bound constraints may be removed exactly, provided all affected expressions and derivative structures are updated by substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a variable has equal finite bounds, substitute that fixed value everywhere and remove the variable. Feasible points and objective values correspond bijectively under insertion and deletion.
assumptions_latex: The original functions are defined at every point considered after inserting \(x_i=\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and reduced feasible sets are bijective, with equal corresponding objective values.

notation.meaning: Vector of all variables except the fixed component.
Common lower and upper bound of the fixed variable.

children.title: Lower-Bound Transformations
children.top_down_role: Representations tailored to variables with finite lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of a finite lower-bounded variable to a nonnegative variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a scalar variable satisfying \(x\geq l\), where \(l\in\mathbb{R}\), define
\[
y=x-l.
\]
Then \(x=l+y\), and the map \(x\mapsto y\) is a bijection from \([l,\infty)\) onto \([0,\infty)\). Substituting \(x=l+y\) in every objective and constraint therefore preserves feasibility and objective values. On the strict interior, \(x>l\) is equivalent to \(y>0\), and the logarithmic lower-bound barrier transforms exactly as \(-\mu\log(x-l)=-\mu\log y\) for every \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a finite lower bound converts the variable into a nonnegative one through a bijection and leaves the logarithmic barrier in standard form.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu>0\) when the barrier identity is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in[l,\infty)\Longleftrightarrow y=x-l\in[0,\infty)\), with \(-\mu\log(x-l)=-\mu\log y\) on the interior.

knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reflection and translation of a finite upper-bounded variable to a nonnegative variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a scalar variable satisfying \(x\leq u\), where \(u\in\mathbb{R}\), define
\[
y=u-x.
\]
Then \(x=u-y\), and the map \(x\mapsto y\) is a bijection from \(( -\infty,u]\) onto \([0,\infty)\). Substitution of \(x=u-y\) in every objective and constraint preserves feasibility and objective values. On the strict interior, \(x<u\) is equivalent to \(y>0\), and the logarithmic upper-bound barrier transforms exactly as \(-\mu\log(u-x)=-\mu\log y\) for every \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the variable from its finite upper bound yields a nonnegative variable through a bijection and converts the upper-bound barrier to standard form.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu>0\) when the barrier identity is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in(-\infty,u]\Longleftrightarrow y=u-x\in[0,\infty)\), with \(-\mu\log(u-x)=-\mu\log y\) on the interior.

children.title: Two-Sided Bound Transformations
children.top_down_role: Interior representations for variables confined to finite intervals.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Bound Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine normalization of a nondegenerate finite interval to the unit interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(l,u\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(l<u\), and let \(l\leq x\leq u\). Define
\[
t=\frac{x-l}{u-l},\qquad x=l+(u-l)t.
\]
This is a bijection between \([l,u]\) and \([0,1]\), with strict interiors corresponding. For \(\mu>0\), the two-sided logarithmic barrier satisfies
\[
-\mu\log(x-l)-\mu\log(u-x)
=-\mu\log t-\mu\log(1-t)-2\mu\log(u-l).
\]
Thus affine normalization preserves minimizers of each barrier subproblem after substitution because the final term is constant in \(t\). The degenerate case \(l=u\) instead requires fixed-variable elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite nondegenerate interval maps bijectively to the unit interval. Its two-sided logarithmic barrier changes only by a constant, while equal bounds require elimination.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu>0\) when the barrier identity is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\leftrightarrow t\) bijects \([l,u]\) with \([0,1]\), and the transformed barrier differs by the constant \(-2\mu\log(u-l)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distributed block factorization through local eliminations and a coupling Schur complement
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\) be a symmetric block-arrow matrix with local blocks \(K_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times n_i}\), coupling blocks \(B_i\in\mathbb R^{p\times n_i}\), and global block \(C\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic definition for exact finite-dimensional block elimination; communication schedules and fault tolerance are not specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed block factorization of \[K=\begin{bmatrix}K_1&&&B_1^T\\&K_2&&B_2^T\\&&\ddots&\vdots\\B_1&B_2&\cdots&C\end{bmatrix}\] is a factorization protocol in which each nonsingular \(K_i\) is factored locally, each local process forms \(S_i=B_iK_i^{-1}B_i^T\), and the coupling process factors the Schur complement \[S=C-sum_{i=1}^N S_i.\] A solve first computes the reduced coupling right-hand side, solves with \(S\), and then recovers every local component independently by back-substitution with \(K_i\). The defining distribution property is that local factors and local right-hand sides are not required outside their owning blocks; only Schur contributions and coupling vectors are exchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed block factorization applies to a block-arrow system. Each local block is factored where it is stored and contributes a small Schur-complement matrix to the global coupling system. After solving the coupling system, all local unknowns are recovered independently. Distribution is defined algebraically by exchanging only coupling-sized contributions rather than entire local factors.
assumptions_latex: The assembled Schur complement \(S\) is nonsingular.
All block dimensions conform to the displayed matrix and the local solves represent \(K_i^{-1}\) exactly for this definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local factorizations together with a factorization of \(S=C-sum_iB_iK_i^{-1}B_i^T\) determine a factorization and exact solve of \(K\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The construction is block Gaussian elimination with all local variables eliminated before the coupling variables.
special_cases_latex: If \(C=0\), the coupling matrix is \(-sum_iB_iK_i^{-1}B_i^T\).
With one local block, the definition reduces to the ordinary two-by-two block Schur-complement factorization.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local factorizations can be performed concurrently.
The global communication volume is governed by coupling dimension \(p\), although Schur contributions may be dense.
boundary_notes: Singular local blocks require generalized elimination, regularization, or a different partition and are excluded.
No inspected source in the supplied locator set stated this distributed definition with the same scope.
review_flags: A precise authoritative source for distributed block-arrow factorization in an interior-point context is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed block factorization through local eliminations and a coupling Schur complement

children.title: Block-Angular Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition patterns arising from block-angular constraint structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Angular Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bordered block-diagonal representation separating independent local equations from global linking equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After compatible row and column permutations, a block-angular linear system has the form
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
A_1&0&\cdots&0\\
0&A_2&\cdots&0\\
\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\
0&0&\cdots&A_p\\
B_1&B_2&\cdots&B_p
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\\vdots\\x_p\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}b_1\\b_2\\\vdots\\b_p\\d\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The equations \(A_i x_i=b_i\) are block-local, whereas \(\sum_{i=1}^{p}B_i x_i=d\) couples the blocks. Hence matrix-vector products and eligible local factorizations involving distinct \(A_i\) can be performed independently; only operations involving the linking row require cross-block coordination. This representation applies equally to compatible blocks extracted from a permuted interior-point Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-angular form isolates independent local equation blocks and a smaller linking row. Local products and factorizations can proceed independently before coordination through the coupling equations.
assumptions_latex: Rows and columns admit compatible permutations into the displayed form.
Each \(A_i\) acts only on the local variable block \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local equations decouple by block, and all cross-block dependence occurs through \(\sum_{i=1}^{p}B_i x_i=d\).

notation.meaning: Contribution of local variables to linking equations.

children.title: Schur-Complement Block Elimination
children.top_down_role: Block elimination interfaces for reduced interior-point systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Block Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of invertible local blocks to obtain a reduced coupling system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\begin{pmatrix}D&E^{\mathsf T}\\E&C\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}r\\s\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(D\) is nonsingular. Eliminating \(x=D^{-1}(r-E^{\mathsf T}y)\) gives the Schur-complement equation
\[
Sy=s-ED^{-1}r,\qquad S=C-ED^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}.
\]
If \(S\) is nonsingular, solve this reduced system and recover \(x\) from the elimination formula; the recovered pair is the unique solution of the original system. When \(D=\operatorname{diag}(D_1,\ldots,D_p)\), the applications of \(D_i^{-1}\) needed to assemble or apply \(S\) are independent across blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating an invertible local block yields an exact Schur-complement system for coupling variables. With block-diagonal local structure, inverse applications can run independently.
assumptions_latex: \(S=C-ED^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\) is nonsingular for unique recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving \(Sy=s-ED^{-1}r\) and setting \(x=D^{-1}(r-E^{\mathsf T}y)\) yields the unique original-system solution.

notation.meaning: Schur complement of the eliminated block.

children.title: Parallel Sparse Factorization
children.top_down_role: Concurrent factorization strategies for sparse interior-point matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Sparse Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination-tree scheduling for a sparse symmetric indefinite interior-point system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a sparse symmetric matrix \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), a fill-reducing permutation \(P\), and a processor set, form the elimination tree of \(PKP^{T}\). Assign independent frontal matrices at each tree level to processors. Each processor assembles its front, selects numerically admissible \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) pivots, computes its local contribution to an \(LDL^{T}\) factorization, and sends the Schur update to its parent. A parent is processed after all child updates arrive. The output is distributed factors satisfying \(PKP^{T}=LDL^{T}+E\), together with a reported backward-error estimate for \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor independent elimination-tree fronts concurrently, pass Schur updates upward, and return distributed sparse indefinite factors with a backward-error estimate.
assumptions_latex: Pivoting preserves numerical stability and a valid dependency order.
Communication delivers every child contribution before its parent is eliminated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(PKP^{T}=LDL^{T}+E\), with \(E\) monitored by a backward-error estimate.

children.title: Distributed Factorization Coordination
children.top_down_role: Data placement, communication, and synchronization concerns in distributed factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Factorization Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-respecting coordination of block eliminations and Schur updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a block-sparse matrix be partitioned among workers and let a directed acyclic graph encode elimination dependencies. Initialize every dependency-free block as ready. A ready worker factors its assigned diagonal block, applies the permitted local pivot rule, forms update messages for adjacent uneliminated blocks, and atomically records completion. A block becomes ready only after all predecessor updates have been accumulated in a fixed reproducible order. Continue until the root blocks are eliminated or a worker reports pivot failure. Return the distributed factors and completion log; on failure, return the offending block and its unresolved dependency state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers factor ready blocks, exchange Schur updates, and release dependent blocks only after all predecessor contributions have arrived.
assumptions_latex: Every update is delivered exactly once or detected as missing.
Local pivot decisions satisfy the global factorization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful coordination produces globally consistent distributed factors and an auditable dependency-completion log.

notation.meaning: Schur update sent from block task i to block task j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the coordination leaf, but the exactly-once delivery, atomic completion, fixed accumulation order, global pivot convention, and failure-reporting semantics define a specific distributed protocol without evidence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certification pipeline from an interior iterate to a returned solution object
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the standard-form linear program \(\min c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), let an interior solver return \((x,lambda,s)\) with \(x,s>0\), and let \(\mathcal R\) be optional postsolve recovery data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-programming interface that separates approximate termination, optional finite termination or crossover, and original-model recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interior solution certification pipeline is an ordered partial map \[\mathcal C=rho_{\mathcal R}\circ C_{\mathrm{post}}\circ C_{\mathrm{term}}\] whose termination stage accepts only if prescribed scaled primal residual, scaled dual residual, and relative duality-gap tests hold; whose optional post stage either preserves the approximate point, projects to an exactly complementary primal-dual point, or recovers an optimal basis; and whose recovery stage maps reduced-model variables to the original model. Its output is a tuple \((x^{\mathrm{out}},lambda^{\mathrm{out}},s^{\mathrm{out}},mathsf{status},mathsf{metrics})\) with every reported status supported by the associated residual and certificate fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certification pipeline is an ordered interface. It first checks scaled primal and dual residuals and the relative gap. It may then perform finite termination or basis crossover, or retain the approximate interior solution. Finally, it reverses presolve transformations. The returned object contains the recovered variables, status, and numerical metrics that support that status.
assumptions_latex: Every stage is applied only when its input-domain checks succeed.
Termination tolerances and scaling denominators are fixed and reported.
If postsolve recovery is used, its substitutions and objective offsets correspond to the solved reduced model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful pipeline output is traceable to explicit termination metrics and, when invoked, valid postprocessing and recovery maps.
special_cases_latex: With no presolve and no crossover, \(\mathcal C=C_{\mathrm{term}}\) returns the accepted approximate primal-dual point.
A finite-termination stage may replace a sufficiently advanced path-following iterate by an exact complementary solution.
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of an optional crossover stage need not invalidate a point already accepted as an approximate solution.
Residual metrics must be recomputed after any postprocessing that changes the returned variables.
boundary_notes: The pipeline definition does not make approximate residual tests into a mathematical certificate of exact optimality.
Infeasibility and unboundedness certificates require additional rays or embedding variables not specified here.

children.title: Primal-Dual Termination Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Stopping families based on scaled residuals, complementarity, and primal-dual gap.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled primal-dual approximate-optimality certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), with dual \(\max b^Ty\) subject to \(A^Ty+s=c\), \(s\geq0\). Let \(\epsilon_p,epsilon_d,epsilon_g>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate stopping certificate for finite-dimensional linear programming; it certifies tolerance satisfaction, not exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-dual termination certificate is a triple \((x,y,s)\) with \(x,s\geq0\) satisfying \[\eta_p=frac{\|Ax-b\|}{1+\|b\|}\leq\epsilon_p,qquad \eta_d=frac{\|A^Ty+s-c\|}{1+\|c\|}\leq\epsilon_d,\] and \[\eta_g=frac{|c^Tx-b^Ty|}{1+|c^Tx|}\leq\epsilon_g.\] The certificate system is the acceptance set \(\mathcal T(epsilon_p,epsilon_d,epsilon_g)=\{(x,y,s):x,s\geq0,eta_p\leq\epsilon_p,eta_d\leq\epsilon_d,eta_g\leq\epsilon_g\}\), together with the reported values of all three metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual termination certificate is a nonnegative primal-dual triple whose scaled primal residual, scaled dual residual, and relative objective gap are each below their stated tolerances. The certificate system is the set of all triples passing these tests together with the actual metric values. It is an approximate numerical certificate rather than a claim of exact optimality.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual use the displayed common sign convention.
The same vector norm is used in each corresponding residual numerator and denominator.
All tolerances are positive and fixed before the acceptance decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y,s)\in\mathcal T(epsilon_p,epsilon_d,epsilon_g)\) exactly when nonnegativity and all three scaled tests hold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(Ax=b\) and \(A^Ty+s=c\) hold exactly, \(c^Tx-b^Ty=x^Ts\), so the gap test may be written using complementarity.
special_cases_latex: A single-tolerance system sets \(\epsilon_p=epsilon_d=epsilon_g=epsilon\).
For an exactly feasible triple, only the complementarity or gap test remains nontrivial.
immediate_consequences_latex: Reporting only the duality gap is insufficient when the current iterate is infeasible.
The denominators reduce sensitivity of the stopping decision to uniform changes in data magnitude.
boundary_notes: Small residuals do not by themselves bound distance to the solution set without conditioning or error-bound assumptions.
Different solver conventions may use alternative denominators or infinity norms and therefore define different certificate systems.

children.title: Primal Residual Criteria
children.top_down_role: Stopping assessments based on scaled primal feasibility residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Residual Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled feasibility test for equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\geq0\), define the primal residual by \[r_{\mathrm p}(x)=\max\!\left\{\lVert h(x)\rVert_{\infty},\lVert[-g(x)]_{+}\rVert_{\infty}\right\}.\] Given absolute and relative tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\) and a finite scale \(S_{\mathrm p}(x)\geq1\), the primal criterion holds precisely when \[r_{\mathrm p}(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{rel}}S_{\mathrm p}(x).\] The positive-part operator is applied componentwise, so the test measures both equality violation and the negative part of each required nonnegative constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility is accepted when the largest equality or inequality violation is below an absolute-plus-relative scaled tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(S_{\mathrm p}(x)\) is finite and at least one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm p}(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{rel}}S_{\mathrm p}(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Residual Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled stationarity and dual-sign test for a primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) be continuously differentiable at \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For multipliers \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^q\), use the convention \(g(x)\geq0\), \(z\geq0\), and define \(L(x,y,z)=f(x)-y^Th(x)-z^Tg(x)\). Define \[r_{\mathrm d}(x,y,z)=\max\!\left\{\lVert\nabla_xL(x,y,z)\rVert_{\infty},\lVert[-z]_{+}\rVert_{\infty}\right\}.\] Given \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm d}^{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm d}^{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\) and a finite scale \(S_{\mathrm d}(x,y,z)\geq1\), the dual criterion holds precisely when \[r_{\mathrm d}(x,y,z)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm d}^{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm d}^{\mathrm{rel}}S_{\mathrm d}(x,y,z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual criterion holds when both the stationarity error and any multiplier-sign violation are below the stated absolute-plus-relative scaled tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(z\in\mathbb{R}^q\), and the multiplier sign convention is \(z\geq0\) for \(g(x)\geq0\).
\(S_{\mathrm d}(x,y,z)\) is finite and at least one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm d}(x,y,z)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm d}^{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm d}^{\mathrm{rel}}S_{\mathrm d}(x,y,z)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise and average complementarity tests for inequality pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) with \(q\geq1\), let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(z\in\mathbb{R}^q\) be the multipliers for inequalities \(g(x)\geq0\), under the convention \(z\geq0\). For \(i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), define \(c_i=z_i g_i(x)\) and define the average complementarity \(\mu=q^{-1}z^Tg(x)\). Given \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm c}\geq0\), the componentwise complementarity criterion is \[\lVert z\odot g(x)\rVert_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm c}.\] An additional average criterion may require \(\lvert\mu\rvert\leq\varepsilon_{\mu}\), where \(\varepsilon_{\mu}\geq0\), but the average criterion does not replace the componentwise criterion unless \(g(x)\geq0\) and \(z\geq0\) have been certified componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate complementarity requires every multiplier-times-slack product to be small. A small average may be used additionally, but it cannot replace the componentwise test unless primal and dual sign feasibility has been certified.
assumptions_latex: The products and average are computed using consistent constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert z\odot g(x)\rVert_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm c}\), optionally together with \(\lvert q^{-1}z^Tg(x)\rvert\leq\varepsilon_{\mu}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Average and Maximum Complementarity Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative equivalence of average and componentwise complementarity under sign feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s,z\in\mathbb R^q_+\), \(q\geq1\), set \(c=z\odot s\), and let \(\mu=q^{-1}z^Ts\). Then \[\mu\leq\lVert c\rVert_\infty\leq q\mu.\] Consequently, \(\lVert c\rVert_\infty\leq\varepsilon\) implies \(\mu\leq\varepsilon\), whereas \(\mu\leq\varepsilon\) implies \(\lVert c\rVert_\infty\leq q\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative slacks and multipliers, average and maximum complementarity are equivalent up to the number of inequality pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu\leq\lVert z\odot s\rVert_\infty\leq q\mu\).

children.title: Primal–Dual Gap Criteria
children.top_down_role: Absolute and relative gap measures used for termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-program termination test using a certified dual lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex problem \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x)=0,\quad g(x)\geq0,\] where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is affine, and every component of \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is concave. For \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^q_+\), define \(L(u,y,z)=f(u)-y^Th(u)-z^Tg(u)\) and \(q(y,z)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n}L(u,y,z)\). If \(x\) is primal feasible and \(q(y,z)\) is finite, weak duality gives \(G(x,y,z)=f(x)-q(y,z)\geq0\). Given \(\varepsilon_G^{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_G^{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\), the primal–dual gap criterion holds when \[0\leq G(x,y,z)\leq\varepsilon_G^{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_G^{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,\lvert f(x)\rvert,\lvert q(y,z)\rvert\}.\] Without certified primal and dual feasibility, this inequality alone is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex problem, a primal-feasible point and dual-feasible multipliers satisfy the gap criterion when the certified primal objective minus the dual lower bound is nonnegative and below the stated absolute-plus-relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, \(h\) is affine, and each component of \(g\) is concave under the convention \(g(x)\geq0\).
\(q(y,z)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n}L(u,y,z)\) is finite and is evaluated or bounded rigorously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq f(x)-q(y,z)\leq\varepsilon_G^{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_G^{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,\lvert f(x)\rvert,\lvert q(y,z)\rvert\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective-Error Bounds from a Certified Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a feasible primal-dual gap into separate primal and dual objective-error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*\) be the finite optimal value of a convex minimization problem. If \(x\) is primal feasible and \(q(y,z)\) is a finite valid dual lower bound, then \[q(y,z)\leq p^*\leq f(x).\] Therefore \[0\leq f(x)-p^*\leq f(x)-q(y,z),\qquad 0\leq p^*-q(y,z)\leq f(x)-q(y,z).\] Thus a certified gap at most \(\varepsilon\) bounds both errors by \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified feasible primal-dual gap bounds both primal suboptimality and the error in the dual lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(q(y,z)\) is a finite valid dual lower bound.
The finite optimal value \(p^*\) is attained or is otherwise well defined.
