knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local KKT Degeneracy Taxonomy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\), where all functions are continuously differentiable. For a feasible point \(x^*\), let \(\mathcal A_I(x^*)=\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\mathcal E\cup\mathcal A_I(x^*)\), and let \(\Lambda(x^*)\) be the set of KKT multiplier vectors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming at a feasible KKT point. The taxonomy records first-order local degeneracies relevant to primal-dual interior-point systems; it does not include Hessian degeneracy or purely global failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KKT point \(x^*\) lies on the local degeneracy boundary when at least one of the following holds: \[\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sc}}(x^*):\ \forall\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\ \exists i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)\text{ such that }\lambda_i=0,\] \[\mathcal D_{\lambda}(x^*):\ |\Lambda(x^*)|>1,\qquad \mathcal D_J(x^*):\ \operatorname{rank}J_{\mathcal A}(x^*)<|\mathcal A(x^*)|,\] where \(J_{\mathcal A}(x^*)\) has rows \(\nabla c_i(x^*)^T\), \(i\in\mathcal A(x^*)\). Thus \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{loc}}=\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sc}}\cup\mathcal D_{\lambda}\cup\mathcal D_J\). The three classes may overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth nonlinear program, a feasible KKT point is locally degenerate when strict complementarity is unavailable for every KKT multiplier, the KKT multiplier set has more than one member, or the Jacobian of the equality and active inequality constraints is row-rank deficient. These classes are not mutually exclusive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{loc}}\iff x^*\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sc}}\cup\mathcal D_{\lambda}\cup\mathcal D_J\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x^*\in\mathcal D_J\) exactly when the active constraint gradients are linearly dependent, that is, LICQ fails at \(x^*\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\Lambda(x^*)=\{\lambda^*\}\), then \(x^*\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sc}}\) exactly when some active inequality has \(\lambda_i^*=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The standard local central-path regularity assumptions exclude \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sc}}\cup\mathcal D_J\) and impose a second-order sufficient condition in addition.
boundary_notes: This union is a synthesized taxonomy of standard degeneracy conditions, not a named definition in the cited source.
Failure of a second-order sufficient condition is outside this first-order taxonomy.

children.title: Lack of Strict Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Endpoint and local-rate degradation in non-strictly complementary regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Square-Root Central-Path Endpoint Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar barrier family exhibiting endpoint-rate degradation without strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\ge0}\tfrac12x^2.\] With multiplier z\ge0 for x\ge0, its unique KKT pair is (x^*,z^*)=(0,0). The central-path equations x-z=0 and xz=\mu with x,z>0 give \[x(\mu)=z(\mu)=\sqrt\mu.\] Hence the path approaches the endpoint at order \sqrt\mu, and its derivative with respect to \mu is unbounded as \mu\downarrow0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar non-strictly-complementary problem has slack and multiplier proportional to the square root of the barrier parameter.
assumptions_latex: The stationarity convention is x-z=0 for the constraint x\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x(\mu)=z(\mu)=\sqrt\mu,\qquad\|(x(\mu),z(\mu))\|=\Theta(\sqrt\mu).
knowledge_statements.title: Square-Root Central-Path Endpoint Rate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degenerate Complementarity Linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar first-order degeneration at a weakly active complementarity pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a slack-multiplier pair (s,z)\in\mathbb R_+^2, let \phi(s,z)=sz. Its derivative is \[D\phi(s,z)=[z\ \ s].\] At a non-strictly complementary pair (s,z)=(0,0), this derivative is zero. The complementarity equation therefore does not distinguish the branches s=0 and z=0 to first order; nonsingularity or branch identification must come from additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero-slack, zero-multiplier pair, complementarity has zero derivative and cannot distinguish its two branches to first order.
assumptions_latex: Strict complementarity fails at the pair, so s=z=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Complementarity Linearization
Lack of Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-strictly complementary KKT points and the guarantees lost there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider inequalities \(g_i(x)\ge0\) with multipliers \(z_i\ge0\). At a KKT point \((x^*,z^*)\), complementarity gives \(g_i(x^*)z_i^*=0\). Strict complementarity requires \[g_i(x^*)+z_i^*>0\qquad\text{for every }i.\] It fails precisely when some index satisfies \(g_i(x^*)=z_i^*=0\). At such an index, the complementarity linearization does not distinguish the primal-active and dual-active branches. Therefore nonsingularity of the primal-dual Newton system, finite active-set identification, and fast local convergence cannot be inferred from otherwise standard regularity assumptions alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity fails when an active constraint has zero multiplier, removing standard guarantees for identification, nonsingularity, and fast local convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Strict Complementarity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the smooth nonlinear program \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), let \(x^*\) be a feasible KKT point and \(\Lambda(x^*)\) its KKT multiplier set. Write \(\mathcal A_I(x^*)=\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The primary definition is solution-level and allows nonunique multipliers. A separate pair-level formulation is included because strict complementarity is often stated for a particular KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KKT pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) lacks strict complementarity if \[\exists i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)\quad \lambda_i^*=0.\] The KKT point \(x^*\) lacks strict complementarity if no KKT multiplier is strictly complementary: \[\forall\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\ \exists i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)\quad \lambda_i=0.\] Equivalently, there is no \(\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\) satisfying \(\lambda_i>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT pair lacks strict complementarity when an active inequality has zero multiplier. A KKT point lacks strict complementarity when this defect occurs for every admissible KKT multiplier, so that no multiplier is positive on all active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\text{ lacks strict complementarity}\iff \nexists\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\text{ with }\lambda_i>0\ \forall i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because KKT complementarity already gives \(\lambda_i c_i(x^*)=0\), strict complementarity for a pair means exactly one of \(c_i(x^*)\) and \(\lambda_i\) is zero for every \(i\in\mathcal I\).
special_cases_latex: When the KKT multiplier is unique, failure is simply \(\min_{i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)}\lambda_i^*=0\), provided the active inequality set is nonempty.
immediate_consequences_latex: The usual local central-path nonsingularity statement based on strict complementarity does not apply when this condition fails.
boundary_notes: An inactive inequality has zero multiplier by complementarity and therefore does not witness failure of strict complementarity.
This definition does not assert that every algorithm converges slowly in the non-strictly complementary regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Convergence Does Not Determine a Dual Endpoint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limit on dual conclusions under multiplier nonuniqueness, without attributing the sequence to a particular algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda^a\ne\lambda^b\) belong to \(\Lambda(x^*)\), set \(x_k=x^*\) and alternate \(\lambda_k\) between \(\lambda^a\) and \(\lambda^b\). Then every \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) is a KKT pair, \(x_k\to x^*\), and the KKT residual vanishes, but \(\lambda_k\) does not converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating between two valid multipliers gives a converged primal sequence and zero KKT residuals but no convergent dual sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\to x^*,\quad R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x_k,\lambda_k)=0,\quad\text{but }\lambda_k\text{ does not converge}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Structure of the Multiplier Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of all KKT multipliers at a fixed feasible stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I(x^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). Under the convention \(g(x)\ge0\), \(\Lambda(x^*)\) is the intersection of the affine stationarity set with \(\{z_{I(x^*)}\ge0,\ z_{I(x^*)^c}=0\}\). Hence it is a closed convex polyhedron, and it is nonunique exactly when it contains a nonconstant line segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed primal point, the multiplier set is a closed convex polyhedron; nonuniqueness is equivalent to containing a nontrivial segment.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,g\) are continuously differentiable at the feasible point \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Lambda(x^*)\text{ is a closed convex polyhedron, and }|\Lambda(x^*)|>1\iff\Lambda(x^*)\text{ contains a nonconstant segment}.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Structure of the Multiplier Set
Multiplier Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity of KKT multipliers at a fixed primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality constraints \(h(x)=0\) and inequalities \(g(x)\ge0\), define the multiplier set at a feasible point \(x^*\) by \[\Lambda(x^*)=\{(y,z):
abla f(x^*)-
abla h(x^*)^Ty-
abla g(x^*)^Tz=0,\ z\ge0,\ z_i g_i(x^*)=0\}.\] Multiplier nonuniqueness holds when \(\Lambda(x^*)\) contains at least two distinct elements. Then the primal point does not select a unique dual endpoint, so different barrier or primal-dual trajectories may converge to different members of \(\Lambda(x^*)\), and local systems that require a unique dual solution may be singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers are nonunique when two distinct dual vectors satisfy stationarity, sign, and complementarity at the same feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonuniqueness of KKT Multipliers
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x^*\) be feasible for a continuously differentiable nonlinear program, and define \(\Lambda(x^*)\) as the set of vectors \(\lambda\) satisfying stationarity, multiplier signs, and complementarity at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming. The definition concerns dual nonuniqueness at one fixed primal KKT point, not nonuniqueness of primal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The KKT multiplier is nonunique at \(x^*\) if \[\exists\lambda^{(1)},\lambda^{(2)}\in\Lambda(x^*)\quad	ext{such that}\quad\lambda^{(1)}
e\lambda^{(2)}.\] Equivalently, \(|\Lambda(x^*)|>1\). With the sign convention \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i c_i(x)\), every \(\lambda\in\Lambda(x^*)\) satisfies \[
abla f(x^*)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal A(x^*)}\lambda_i
abla c_i(x^*)=0,\quad \lambda_i\ge0\ \ (i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)).\] Thus nonuniqueness means that this affine stationarity system and its sign restrictions admit at least two solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT multipliers are nonunique at a fixed feasible point when two distinct multiplier vectors satisfy stationarity, sign, and complementarity conditions at that same primal point. This is dual ambiguity, not multiplicity of primal solutions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exists a nonzero difference \(d_\lambda=\lambda^{(1)}-\lambda^{(2)}\) between two feasible multiplier vectors, with \(J_{\mathcal A}(x^*)^Td_\lambda=0\) and with both endpoints respecting the inequality-multiplier signs.
special_cases_latex: If LICQ holds at \(x^*\), then the KKT multiplier is unique; consequently multiplier nonuniqueness can occur only when LICQ fails, although LICQ failure alone need not produce multiple sign-feasible multipliers.
immediate_consequences_latex: A primal point with nonunique multipliers does not determine a unique limiting dual vector without an additional selection rule.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require \(\Lambda(x^*)\) to contain a continuum, although convexity of the KKT multiplier set makes this typical once two multipliers exist.
Approximate numerical disagreement between multiplier estimates is not itself exact multiplier nonuniqueness.

notation.meaning: All KKT multipliers associated with the fixed primal point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Left-Null Rank-Deficiency Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and approximate certificates for dependent active-constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}, a nonzero y\in\mathbb R^m satisfying J^{\mathsf T}y=0 certifies \operatorname{rank}J<m. Define the row-dependence margin \[\gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(J)=\inf_{\|y\|=1}\|J^{\mathsf T}y\|.\] A unit y with \|J^{\mathsf T}y\|\le\varepsilon certifies \gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(J)\le\varepsilon; exact row-rank deficiency is equivalent to \gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(J)=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left-null vector certifies exact active-gradient dependence, while a small left residual certifies a small row-dependence margin.
assumptions_latex: J stores active constraint gradients as rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ y\ne0\Longrightarrow\operatorname{rank}J<m.

notation.meaning: coefficients of a dependence among constraint rows
minimum left residual over unit coefficient vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Left-Null Rank-Deficiency Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-Deficiency Kernel of the Bordered KKT Matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact singularity consequence for the standard unregularized bordered KKT representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}, H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}, and \[M=\begin{bmatrix}H&J^{\mathsf T}\\J&0\end{bmatrix}.\] If \operatorname{rank}J<m and 0\ne y\in\ker J^{\mathsf T}, then \[M\begin{bmatrix}0\\y\end{bmatrix}=0.\] Therefore M is singular independently of H.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left-null vector of a rank-deficient constraint Jacobian is a null vector of the standard unregularized bordered KKT matrix.
assumptions_latex: The Newton matrix has the displayed unregularized bordered form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker M\ne\{0\}.

notation.meaning: active-constraint Jacobian with gradients in rows

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficiency Kernel of the Bordered KKT Matrix
Constraint-Jacobian Rank Deficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear dependence among equality and active-inequality gradients at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be feasible, let \(I(x^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\), and form the active-constraint Jacobian \[J_A(x^*)= egin{bmatrix}
abla h(x^*)^T\ 
abla g_{I(x^*)}(x^*)^T\end{bmatrix}.\] Constraint-Jacobian rank deficiency holds when \(\operatorname{rank}J_A(x^*)\) is smaller than its number of rows. Equivalently, there exists a nonzero coefficient vector \((u,v)\) such that \(
abla h(x^*)^Tu+
abla g_{I(x^*)}(x^*)^Tv=0\). This dependence violates the linear-independence constraint qualification and can make the KKT or primal-dual Newton matrix singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency occurs when active constraint gradients are linearly dependent, violating LICQ and potentially singularizing the primal-dual system.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable at the feasible point \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}J_A(x^*)<\operatorname{rows}J_A(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of equality and active inequality constraints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active Constraint-Jacobian Rank Deficiency
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth nonlinear program at a feasible point \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal A(x)=\mathcal E\cup\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x)=0\}\). Define \(J_{\mathcal A}(x)\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal A(x)|\times n}\) by placing \(\nabla c_i(x)^T\) in the row indexed by \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The relevant Jacobian contains all equality constraints and only active inequalities. Inactive inequalities are excluded from the local constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The active constraint Jacobian is rank deficient at \(x\) if \[\operatorname{rank}J_{\mathcal A}(x)<|\mathcal A(x)|.\] Equivalently, there exists a nonzero vector \(v\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal A(x)|}\) such that \[J_{\mathcal A}(x)^Tv=0,\] or the active gradients \(\{\nabla c_i(x):i\in\mathcal A(x)\}\) are linearly dependent. This condition is precisely failure of the linear independence constraint qualification at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraint Jacobian is locally rank deficient when the rows formed by equality-constraint gradients and active-inequality gradients are linearly dependent. Equivalently, a nonzero linear combination of those gradients is zero, so LICQ fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}J_{\mathcal A}(x)<|\mathcal A(x)|\iff\ker J_{\mathcal A}(x)^T\ne\{0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The smallest singular value satisfies \(\sigma_{\min}(J_{\mathcal A}(x))=0\) when \(|\mathcal A(x)|\le n\); if \(|\mathcal A(x)|>n\), row-rank deficiency is automatic.
special_cases_latex: A zero active constraint gradient immediately causes rank deficiency.
Redundant equality constraints cause rank deficiency at every point where their dependence persists.
immediate_consequences_latex: The standard LICQ-based uniqueness conclusion for KKT multipliers is unavailable.
KKT systems using this Jacobian may be singular unless curvature or regularization supplies additional nonsingularity.
boundary_notes: Near rank deficiency, where \(\sigma_{\min}\) is small but nonzero, is an ill-conditioning notion rather than exact rank deficiency.
The full Jacobian including inactive inequalities can be rank deficient while the active Jacobian still satisfies LICQ.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of all equality and active inequality constraints.

More generally, a unit vector \(y\) with \(\|J^{\mathsf T}y\|\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\sigma_{\min}(J)\le\varepsilon\), identifying an approximately dependent combination of constraint gradients.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and form \[M=\begin{bmatrix}H&J^{\mathsf T}\\J&0\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(J\) lacks full row rank, choose \(0\ne y\in\ker J^{\mathsf T}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularization of a rank-deficient primal-dual interior-point system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior-point specialization for singularity caused by a rank-deficient equality-constraint Jacobian, coupled with Hessian-block inertia control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
When \operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm E}(x))<l, use the regularized primal-dual matrix
\[
K_{\delta,\gamma}=\begin{bmatrix}
\nabla_{xx}^{2}\mathcal L+\delta I&0&A_{\mathrm E}(x)^T&A_{\mathrm I}(x)^T\\
0&\Sigma&0&-I\\
A_{\mathrm E}(x)&0&-\gamma I&0\\
A_{\mathrm I}(x)&-I&0&0
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad \gamma\ge 0,
\]
with the Hessian shift \delta I retained for inertia control. At each interior-point iteration, choose \gamma and \delta by the regularization procedure so that
\[
\operatorname{In}(K_{\delta,\gamma})=(n+m,l+m,0).
\]
Thus the selected matrix is nonsingular. The block \begin{bmatrix}A_{\mathrm I}(x)&-I\end{bmatrix} is structurally full row rank, so this additional singularity safeguard addresses rank deficiency of A_{\mathrm E}(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If dependent equality constraints make the primal-dual matrix singular, add a negative gamma identity regularization to the equality-multiplier block while retaining the delta identity shift of the Lagrangian Hessian. At every interior-point iteration, select the two parameters so that the matrix has the required inertia and is nonsingular. The inequality-slack constraint block is already full row rank because it contains a negative identity block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{In}(K_{\delta,\gamma})=(n+m,l+m,0)\quad\text{and hence}\quad \det K_{\delta,\gamma}\ne0\ \text{for the selected parameters}.

children.title: Boundary Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning deterioration as central trajectories approach active boundaries.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary-Induced Ill-Conditioning of Primal-Dual Systems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k,s_k,y_k,z_k)\) be strictly interior primal-dual iterates with \(s_k>0\), \(z_k>0\), barrier parameters \(\mu_k\downarrow0\), and \(S_k=\operatorname{Diag}(s_k)\), \(Z_k=\operatorname{Diag}(z_k)\). Let \(K_k\) denote a chosen symmetric primal-dual Newton or condensed KKT coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns conditioning that deteriorates along an interior sequence approaching active inequality boundaries. Exact singularity and fixed poor scaling are distinguished from asymptotic boundary-induced ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formulation exhibits boundary ill-conditioning along the sequence if every \(K_k\) is nonsingular but \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\kappa_2(K_k)=\infty.\] It is complementarity-induced when the divergence is associated with \(D_k=S_k^{-1}Z_k\), whose diagonal entries satisfy \((D_k)_{ii}=z_{k,i}/s_{k,i}\), and \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\max_i z_{k,i}/s_{k,i}}{\min_i z_{k,i}/s_{k,i}}=\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary ill-conditioning occurs when the primal-dual or condensed Newton matrices remain nonsingular at every interior iterate but their spectral condition numbers become unbounded as the barrier parameter tends to zero. It is complementarity-induced when the ratios of dual variables to slacks become increasingly disparate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\kappa_2(K_k)=\infty\), with \(K_k\) nonsingular for each finite \(k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the diagonal scaling matrix \(D_k=S_k^{-1}Z_k\), \(\kappa_2(D_k)=\max_i(z_{k,i}/s_{k,i})/\min_i(z_{k,i}/s_{k,i})\).
special_cases_latex: Under strict complementarity, active constraints typically have \(s_{k,i}\to0\) with \(z_{k,i}\) bounded away from zero, while inactive constraints have the reverse behavior; hence entries of \(D_k\) separate toward infinity and zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: Stable direct factorization can still compute accurate directions for the structured primal-dual system even when its unscaled condition number is large.
boundary_notes: If some \(K_k\) is singular, the phenomenon has crossed from ill-conditioning into singularity.
The definition is representation-dependent: scaling or preconditioning can change \(\kappa_2(K_k)\).

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number \(\sigma_{\max}(K)/\sigma_{\min}(K)\) for nonsingular K.
Diagonal complementarity scaling in the symmetric primal-dual system.

children.title: Complementarity Scale Separation
children.top_down_role: Numerical difficulty caused by widely separated primal and dual scales.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Complementarity Without Scale Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balanced regime showing that small complementarity products do not force ill-conditioned diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every component satisfies \(s_i=z_i=\sqrt\mu\), then \(s_i z_i=\mu\to0\) while \(D=I\) and \(\kappa_2(D)=1\). More generally, uniformly comparable slack ratios, equivalently multiplier ratios, keep \(\kappa_2(D)\) uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity may vanish while primal and dual scales remain perfectly balanced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i z_i\to0\) while \(\kappa_2(D)=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Complementarity Without Scale Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Central-Path Scaling Separation Law
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between diagonal primal-dual scaling and slack or multiplier spread on the central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(s_i z_i=\mu>0\) componentwise and \(D=\operatorname{diag}((s_i/z_i)^{1/2})\), then \[D=\mu^{-1/2}S=\sqrt\mu\,Z^{-1},\qquad \kappa_2(D)=\frac{\max_i s_i}{\min_i s_i}=\frac{\max_i z_i}{\min_i z_i}.\] If one pair converges to \((s_i^*,0)\) with \(s_i^*>0\) and another to \((0,z_j^*)\) with \(z_j^*>0\), then \(\kappa_2(D)=\Theta(\mu^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the exact central path, the scaling condition number equals the spread of either slacks or multipliers. Coexisting strictly inactive and strictly active constraints create inverse-parameter separation.
assumptions_latex: the stated active and inactive limits hold for the asymptotic conclusion
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(D)=\max_i s_i/\min_i s_i=\max_i z_i/\min_i z_i\), with \(\Theta(\mu^{-1})\) growth in the mixed strict regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Scaling Separation Law
Complementarity Scale Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative diagnostic for incompatible primal-slack and dual-multiplier scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive slack and multiplier vectors \(s,z\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), define \(d_i=(s_i/z_i)^{1/2}\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\). Complementarity scale separation at level \(M>1\) occurs when \[\kappa_2(D)=\frac{\max_i d_i}{\min_i d_i}\ge M.\] Although products \(s_i z_i\) may all be comparable to the barrier parameter, some pairs can have a very small slack and large multiplier while others have the reverse. The resulting scaling has a large condition number and amplifies rounding errors in scaled primal-dual equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale separation occurs when slack-to-multiplier ratios vary widely, making the standard primal-dual diagonal scaling ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(\operatorname{diag}((s_i/z_i)^{1/2}))\ge M\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagonal slack-multiplier scaling is standard in primal-dual methods
threshold convention and numerical consequence need exact source locator

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementarity Scaling Separation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s_k,z_k\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) be slack and inequality-multiplier vectors in a primal-dual interior-point sequence. Put \(S_k=\operatorname{Diag}(s_k)\), \(Z_k=\operatorname{Diag}(z_k)\), and \(D_k=S_k^{-1}Z_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is numerical and coordinate-dependent. It quantifies separation among the diagonal coefficients entering a standard symmetric primal-dual Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence has complementarity scale separation if \[\kappa_2(D_k)=\frac{\max_{1\le i\le m}z_{k,i}/s_{k,i}}{\min_{1\le i\le m}z_{k,i}/s_{k,i}}\longrightarrow\infty.\] A finite-iterate separation factor is \[\rho_k:=\kappa_2(D_k)\ge1.\] For a prescribed numerical threshold \(\rho_{\max}>1\), iterate \(k\) is in the scale-separated regime when \(\rho_k>\rho_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity scales separate when the largest ratio of an inequality multiplier to its slack becomes arbitrarily larger than the smallest such ratio. The condition number of the diagonal primal-dual scaling matrix measures this separation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k=\kappa_2(S_k^{-1}Z_k)\to\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(D_k\) is positive diagonal, scale separation is equivalent to \(\max_{i,j}(z_{k,i}s_{k,j})/(s_{k,i}z_{k,j})\to\infty\).
special_cases_latex: If \(s_{k,i}z_{k,i}\approx\mu_k\), an active index with \(s_{k,i}=\Theta(\mu_k)\) has \(z_{k,i}/s_{k,i}=\Theta(\mu_k^{-1})\), whereas an inactive index has ratio \(\Theta(\mu_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Unscaled iterative solution of the primal-dual equations can become difficult, motivating complementarity-aware scaling or preconditioning.
boundary_notes: Uniform rescaling of individual constraints changes the numerical ratios, so the definition presupposes a fixed constraint scaling.
Small complementarity products alone do not imply separation if all ratios remain comparable.

notation.meaning: Condition number of the positive diagonal complementarity scaling matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Scale Separation in Uniform-Activity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that small complementarity alone does not force an ill-conditioned diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(s_i z_i=\mu\) and the multiplier ratios satisfy \(0<c\leq z_i/z_j\leq C<\infty\) uniformly for all \(i,j\), then \(\kappa_2(D)\leq C\), independently of \(\mu\). In particular, if all pairs satisfy \(s_i=z_i=\sqrt\mu\), then \(D=I\) although every complementarity product tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small complementarity products do not themselves cause scale separation; comparable multiplier ratios keep the primal-dual scaling uniformly conditioned.
assumptions_latex: all multiplier ratios are uniformly bounded above and below
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\mu}\kappa_2(D)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Scale Separation in Uniform-Activity Regimes

children.title: Reduced-System Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Condition amplification introduced by normal equations and related reductions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduction Without Condition Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that range-space reduction need not worsen conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H=I\) and \(AA^T=I_m\), then \(S=AH^{-1}A^T=I_m\) and \(\kappa_2(S)=1\). Thus reduction can square the weighted operator's condition number, but it does not inherently make every system ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthonormal constraint rows with an identity primal block produce a perfectly conditioned reduced system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=I_m\) and \(\kappa_2(S)=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Without Condition Amplification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-System Rank Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact loss of positive definiteness when the constraint operator loses row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H\succ0\), \[y^TAH^{-1}A^Ty=\|H^{-1/2}A^Ty\|_2^2.\] Hence \(AH^{-1}A^T\) is positive definite exactly when \(A\) has full row rank. If \(A\) is row-rank deficient, the Schur complement is singular and its ordinary spectral condition number is infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite primal block, the multiplier-space reduced system is nonsingular exactly when the constraint rows are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AH^{-1}A^T\succ0\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Rank Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Schur-Complement Condition Identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact singular-value representation of the range-space reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and set \(B=AH^{-1/2}\). Then \[S=AH^{-1}A^T=BB^T\succ0,\qquad \kappa_2(S)=\kappa_2(B)^2=\kappa_2(AH^{-1/2})^2,\] where the rectangular condition number uses the largest and smallest nonzero singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced Schur complement is a weighted normal-equation matrix, so its condition number exactly squares that of the weighted constraint operator.
assumptions_latex: the rectangular condition number uses nonzero singular values
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Schur-Complement Condition Identity
Reduced-System Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-number amplification caused by forming a primal-dual Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Eliminating the primal variable from the saddle-point system produces the symmetric positive-definite Schur complement \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\). Its spectral condition number satisfies \[\kappa_2(S)\le \kappa_2(A)^2\kappa_2(H).\] Thus forming the reduced system can square the conditioning contribution of the constraint operator. In particular, even moderately ill-conditioned rows of \(A\), combined with barrier-induced ill-conditioning in \(H\), can yield a substantially harder reduced linear solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Schur-complement reduction can square the constraint matrix’s conditioning and multiply it by the primal Hessian’s conditioning.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\succ0\) and \(\kappa_2(S)\le\kappa_2(A)^2\kappa_2(H)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows from standard singular-value bounds for an SPD Schur complement
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

No inspectable source or locator is supplied for that convention and bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning of the Condensed Primal-Dual System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At an interior iterate, let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,y,z)\), let \(A_E\) and \(A_I\) be equality and inequality Jacobians, and let \(D=S^{-1}Z\succ0\). Eliminating slack and inequality-multiplier steps yields a condensed coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns the particular reduced system obtained by algebraic elimination. It does not claim that reduction always worsens conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condensed primal-dual matrix is \[K_{\mathrm{red}}=\begin{bmatrix}H+A_I^TDA_I&A_E^T\\A_E&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Its reduced-system condition number is \[\kappa_{\mathrm{red}}:=\kappa_2(K_{\mathrm{red}}),\] with \(\kappa_{\mathrm{red}}=\infty\) if \(K_{\mathrm{red}}\) is singular. Relative to a nonsingular unreduced matrix \(K_{\mathrm{full}}\), the conditioning amplification factor is \[\gamma_{\mathrm{red}}:=\frac{\kappa_2(K_{\mathrm{red}})}{\kappa_2(K_{\mathrm{full}})}.\] A sequence is reduction-amplified when \(\limsup_k\gamma_{\mathrm{red},k}=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-system conditioning is the spectral conditioning of the condensed KKT matrix obtained after eliminating slack and inequality-multiplier steps. Conditioning amplification is measured by comparing this condition number with that of the corresponding unreduced primal-dual matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_{\mathrm{red}}=\kappa_2\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}H+A_I^TDA_I&A_E^T\\A_E&0\end{bmatrix}\right)\).
special_cases_latex: For simple bound constraints, \(A_I^TDA_I\) is diagonal, so condensation need not introduce off-diagonal fill from this term.
When \(A_I^TDA_I\) has substantial fill, the reduced matrix may be smaller yet more expensive to store and factor.
immediate_consequences_latex: The choice between full indefinite factorization and condensed factorization depends on both conditioning and sparsity, not dimension alone.
boundary_notes: A large \(\kappa_{\mathrm{red}}\) may originate in \(H\), a nearly rank-deficient Jacobian, or complementarity scaling; the definition does not assign a unique cause.
Condition numbers depend on scaling and norm.

notation.meaning: Condition-number ratio between reduced and unreduced formulations.

children.title: Barrier-Curvature Growth
children.top_down_role: Extreme curvature growth near active inequality boundaries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature Blow-Up Without Condition-Number Blow-Up
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing that divergent curvature alone does not imply ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B_\mu(x)=-\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) at \(x=t\mathbf1\), \[\nabla^2B_\mu(t\mathbf1)=\frac{\mu}{t^2}I.\] As \(t\downarrow0\), every eigenvalue diverges while \(\kappa_2(\nabla^2B_\mu)=1\). Condition-number growth therefore requires anisotropic spectral growth or interaction with blocks on different scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform approach to identical bounds makes every barrier eigenvalue diverge equally, leaving the Hessian perfectly conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla^2B_\mu(t\mathbf1)\|_2\to\infty\) while \(\kappa_2(\nabla^2B_\mu(t\mathbf1))=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Blow-Up Without Condition-Number Blow-Up

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Central-Path Active-Normal Curvature Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-normal curvature growth along a strictly complementary central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(s_i(\mu)z_i(\mu)=\mu\), \(z_i(\mu)\to z_i^*>0\), and the limiting constraint normal is nonzero. Then \[s_i(\mu)=\frac{\mu}{z_i(\mu)}=\Theta(\mu),\qquad \frac{\mu}{s_i(\mu)^2}=\frac{z_i(\mu)^2}{\mu}=\Theta(\mu^{-1}).\] Thus the rank-one barrier-normal coefficient for this active constraint grows at order \(1/\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity makes an active slack proportional to the barrier parameter and its rank-one barrier-normal coefficient inversely proportional to that parameter.
assumptions_latex: the limiting constraint normal is nonzero
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i(\mu)=\Theta(\mu)\) and \(\mu/s_i(\mu)^2=\Theta(\mu^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Active-Normal Curvature Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear Log-Barrier Hessian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian representation identifying inverse-square normal growth for smooth nonlinear inequality barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth nonlinear log barrier contains an inverse-square rank-one normal term and an inverse-slack constraint-curvature term.
review_flags: for nonlinear inequalities the total Hessian need not inherit a lower bound from the rank-one term without controlling the constraint-curvature terms
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Log-Barrier Hessian
Barrier-Curvature Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature blow-up of the logarithmic barrier near an active inequality boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For affine slacks \(s_i(x)=a_i^Tx-b_i>0\), the logarithmic barrier \(B_\mu(x)=-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log s_i(x)\) has Hessian \[\nabla^2B_\mu(x)=\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{a_i a_i^T}{s_i(x)^2}.\] If \(a_j\ne0\) and \(s_j(x_k)\downarrow0\) while \(\mu>0\) is fixed, then the curvature in direction \(a_j\) diverges at least on the order of \(\mu/s_j(x_k)^2\). Consequently, approaching an active boundary can make the barrier Hessian and the associated Newton system severely ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The log-barrier Hessian grows like the inverse square of a vanishing affine slack, causing severe boundary ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_j^T\nabla^2B_\mu(x_k)a_j\to+\infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct standard Hessian formula for an affine logarithmic barrier
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalization Failure Taxonomy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(w_k\) collect the primal-dual variables of an interior-point method, let \(R(w_k)\ge0\) be a KKT residual, and let \(p_k\) be a trial direction controlled by a line search, filter, trust region, or feasibility-restoration mechanism.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-relative definition for smooth, possibly nonconvex nonlinear programming. It separates failure of global progress from local Newton-system degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A run has a globalization failure if at least one of the following occurs: \[\text{stagnation: }\liminf_{k\to\infty}R(w_k)>0\ \text{ and }\ \|w_{k+1}-w_k\|\to0;\] \[\text{restoration failure: a restoration sequence cannot produce an accepted point with the required reduction in infeasibility};\] \[\text{undesirable limit: some accumulation point }\bar x\text{ is infeasible, non-KKT, or KKT but not a local minimizer}.\] The globalization-failure set is the union of these algorithmic outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globalization fails when accepted progress vanishes while the KKT residual stays positive, feasibility restoration cannot produce an acceptable reduction, or the run accumulates at an infeasible, non-KKT, or nonminimizing stationary point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{glob}}=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{stag}}\cup\mathcal F_{\mathrm{rest}}\cup\mathcal F_{\mathrm{lim}}\).
special_cases_latex: In a filter line search, arbitrarily small acceptable step lengths constitute the stagnation branch.
In a trust-region method, repeated rejection with radius tending to zero can enter either stagnation or restoration failure.
immediate_consequences_latex: A local fast-convergence model does not by itself rule out any of these global outcomes.
boundary_notes: This is a synthesized taxonomy; the cited source discusses its constituent outcomes rather than naming their union.
Termination at a first-order stationary point is not a failure for an algorithm whose stated guarantee is only first-order stationarity, unless minimizing character is explicitly required.

notation.meaning: Chosen nonnegative residual that vanishes at the intended KKT system.

children.title: Globalization Acceptance Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Repeated step rejection, shortening, or insufficient accepted progress.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Acceptance-Induced Stagnation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(w_{k+1}=w_k+\alpha_kp_k\) denote accepted line-search iterates, with \(0<\alpha_k\le1\), or let \(\Delta_k>0\) be the radius of a trust-region globalization. Let \(R(w)\) be a continuous KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers stagnation caused by the acceptance mechanism, not small steps caused solely by convergence to a regular solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search run has globalization acceptance stagnation if \[\alpha_k\|p_k\|\to0,\qquad \liminf_{k\to\infty}R(w_k)>0.\] A strong finite-length form additionally satisfies \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|p_k\|<\infty\). A trust-region run has acceptance stagnation if infinitely many trial steps are rejected, \(\Delta_k\to0\), and \(\liminf_kR(w_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance stagnation occurs when accepted line-search displacements tend to zero, or a trust-region radius collapses under repeated rejection, while the optimality residual remains bounded away from zero. The finite-length variant requires the total accepted path length to be finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|w_{k+1}-w_k\|\to0\) while \(\liminf_kR(w_k)>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For line-search iterates, \(\|w_{k+1}-w_k\|=\alpha_k\|p_k\|\).
special_cases_latex: A filter line search that requires arbitrarily small \(\alpha_k\) to obtain acceptability is in the precursor regime identified by this definition if the residual does not decrease to zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: A feasibility-restoration phase can be triggered when \(\alpha_k\) falls below a prescribed threshold or when trust-region rejection makes the step-generation subproblem infeasible.
boundary_notes: The condition \(\alpha_k\to0\) alone is insufficient: step lengths commonly shrink near a solution.
Repeated rejected trial points do not constitute stagnation if accepted iterates still drive \(R(w_k)\to0\).

notation.meaning: Residual for the target first-order optimality system.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 15, §15.4, paragraphs preceding the feasibility-restoration problem and Algorithm 15.1, pp. 438–440

review_flags: The residual-based condition formalizes the source’s qualitative statement that arbitrarily small accepted step lengths can make the algorithm stall and fail.

children.title: Line-Search Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Persistent shortening or rejection within line-search globalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-Search Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent line-search shortening produces accepted step lengths tending to zero while neither termination nor vanishing proposed directions explains the loss of movement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) be accepted line-search updates and let \(R(x)\geq0\) be the declared termination residual. Line-search stagnation occurs along an infinite set \(K\) when
\[
\alpha_k\to0,\qquad \inf_{k\in K}\|p_k\|>0,\qquad \liminf_{\substack{k\to\infty\\k\in K}}R(x_k)>0.
\]
Thus the line search accepts only after asymptotically severe shortening, away from the declared termination condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A line search stagnates when accepted step lengths tend to zero even though proposed directions remain nonvanishing and the termination residual stays bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\to0\) along \(K\) while \(\|p_k\|\) and \(R(x_k)\) remain bounded away from zero.
review_flags: Definition is mechanism-specific: it attributes negligible movement to accepted line-search lengths rather than merely to vanishing directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Stagnation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Armijo Step Bound Excludes Line-Search Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed general Armijo lower-bound theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under Lipschitz-gradient, uniform-descent, and fixed-start backtracking assumptions, accepted Armijo lengths admit a positive uniform lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard Armijo assumptions can exclude accepted lengths tending to zero.
assumptions_latex: The merit gradient is Lipschitz on trial segments.
Directions satisfy a uniform descent bound.
Initial trial lengths have a positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_k\alpha_k>0\).
review_flags: The theorem belongs primarily under Armijo backtracking or line-search convergence theory; retain only a cross-index from this pathology leaf.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Armijo Step Bound Excludes Line-Search Stagnation

intermediate_metadata.reason: The accepted new definition resolves the previously deferred predicate by identifying shortening attributable to the line search while excluding ordinary convergence through vanishing directions. The proposed Armijo theorem is deferred to general line-search theory. Filter stagnation, complete rejection, vanishing accepted motion, and merit-ratio failure remain excluded sibling scopes.

children.title: Filter Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Failure of filter acceptance mechanisms to produce sustained progress.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pareto-Only Filter Can Stagnate Away from Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing why strict nondominance without margins is insufficient for progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a filter accepting every pair not dominated by a stored pair, with no sufficient-improvement margin. The sequence \[(\theta_k,f_k)=\left(1+\frac1k,0\right)\] consists of successively smaller violations and can be accepted after deleting the preceding dominated pair, yet \(\theta_k\to1>0\) and the changes in both filter coordinates tend to zero. Pareto nondominance alone therefore does not exclude vanishing accepted progress away from feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A marginless filter can endlessly accept smaller violation values whose improvements vanish and whose limit remains infeasible.
assumptions_latex: dominated old entries may be deleted
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted filter pairs may have vanishing coordinate changes while \(\inf_k\theta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Only Filter Can Stagnate Away from Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Dimensional Filter Acceptance Convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit objective–violation filter convention needed to state filter-specific stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) contain stored pairs \((\theta_j,f_j)\), where \(\theta_j\geq0\) measures constraint violation. Under the fixed convention \(\gamma_\theta,\gamma_f\in(0,1)\), a trial pair \((\theta,f)\) is acceptable if, for every \((\theta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\), \[\theta\leq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_j\quad\text{or}\quad f\leq f_j-\gamma_f\theta_j.\] Dominated entries may be removed after acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under one standard convention, a trial passes the filter when it sufficiently improves violation or objective relative to every stored pair.
assumptions_latex: the displayed filter convention is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance requires at least one displayed sufficient-improvement inequality against every filter entry.
review_flags: filter algorithms use multiple margin conventions; this record fixes one rather than asserting uniqueness
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Dimensional Filter Acceptance Convention

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter-Specific Stagnation Diagnostic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window diagnostic separating filter stagnation from convergence and generic step stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a window length \(q\), coordinate-progress tolerances \(\delta_\theta,\delta_f>0\), and declared feasibility and stationarity termination tolerances. Suspected filter stagnation at iteration \(k\) is reported when the last \(q\) accepted iterations were accepted through the filter, \[\max_{j=k-q,\ldots,k-1}|\theta_{j+1}-\theta_j|\leq\delta_\theta,\qquad \max_{j=k-q,\ldots,k-1}|f_{j+1}-f_j|\leq\delta_f,\] while feasibility or the declared stationarity residual remains above tolerance. This is a diagnostic of negligible movement in filter coordinates, not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter stagnation is suspected when filter-accepted iterates show negligible objective and violation changes over a window while termination residuals remain excessive.
assumptions_latex: a fixed finite window and declared coordinate-progress tolerances are used
the steps were accepted specifically through the filter
complete feasibility and stationarity termination tests are available
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Small changes in both filter coordinates with nonterminal residuals certify suspected filter stagnation, not optimality.
review_flags: window length and thresholds are implementation parameters rather than universal constants
knowledge_statements.title: Filter-Specific Stagnation Diagnostic
Filter Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of filter globalization to obtain nonvanishing objective or feasibility progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta(x)\ge0\) measure constraint violation, let \(f(x)\) be the objective, and let accepted trial points be required to improve either coordinate relative to the current filter. Filter stagnation occurs when an infinite accepted subsequence \(K\) satisfies \[\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\to0,\qquad \inf_{k\in K}\theta(x_k)>0,\qquad \inf_{k\in K}\|\nabla f(x_k)+J(x_k)^Ty_k\|>0.\] The filter continues to admit or repeatedly reconsider points with vanishing displacement, while neither feasibility nor first-order stationarity is approached; restoration, altered margins, or regularization is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter stagnates when accepted displacements vanish while constraint violation and a first-order residual stay bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the constraint functions are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\to0\) while feasibility and stationarity residuals remain positive along an infinite subsequence.
review_flags: filter acceptance conventions vary across algorithms
exact source needed for a canonical stagnation formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits Filter Stagnation, but filter acceptance rules vary and no source supports this particular predicate. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Dimensional Filter Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical objective–violation filter representation with explicit sufficient-improvement margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) contain stored pairs \((\theta_j,f_j)\), where \(\theta_j\geq0\) measures constraint violation. For fixed \(\gamma_\theta,\gamma_f\in(0,1)\), a trial pair \((\theta,f)\) is acceptable to the filter if, for every \((\theta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\), \[\theta\leq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_j\quad\text{or}\quad f\leq f_j-\gamma_f\theta_j.\] After acceptance, pairs dominated by the new pair may be removed. The positive margins prevent acceptance based solely on arbitrarily small coordinate improvement relative to a fixed filter entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial passes a standard objective–violation filter when it sufficiently improves violation or objective relative to every stored pair.
assumptions_latex: the displayed filter convention is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance requires one of the two sufficient-improvement inequalities against every filter entry.
review_flags: filter algorithms use several equivalent margin conventions; this record explicitly fixes one
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Dimensional Filter Acceptance

children.title: Repeated Step Rejection
children.top_down_role: Recurring rejection patterns across successive globalization attempts.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Step Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a backtracking globalization procedure to accept any trial step at infinitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k\) be an interior iterate, \(d_k\neq 0\) a computed search direction, and \(\alpha_{k,j}=\beta^j\bar\alpha_k\), where \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(\bar\alpha_k>0\) preserves strict interiority. Let \(A_k(\alpha)\) denote the prescribed merit-function or filter acceptance predicate. Repeated step rejection occurs when there is an infinite index set \(K\) such that
\[
A_k(\alpha_{k,j})=\mathrm{false}\quad\text{for every }j=0,1,\ldots,J_k\text{ and every }k\in K,
\]
where \(J_k\) is the maximum permitted number of reductions. Consequently, the globalization procedure cannot produce a new accepted iterate at each \(k\in K\) without changing the direction, acceptance model, or restoration mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated rejection occurs when every permitted backtracking length fails the acceptance test at infinitely many iterations, preventing the algorithm from producing accepted iterates without intervention.
assumptions_latex: \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and each iteration permits finitely many reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k(\alpha_{k,j})=\mathrm{false}\) for all permitted \(j\) on an infinite index set, so no ordinary accepted update is produced there.

notation.meaning: globalization acceptance predicate at iteration k

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5 Restricted Step Methods p. 95

review_flags: acceptance predicate intentionally covers merit and filter globalizations

children.title: Vanishing Accepted Steps
children.top_down_role: Accepted-step sequences whose effective movement becomes negligible.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Accepted Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted interior-point steps become asymptotically too small to move the primal-dual iterates materially.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k\) denote the primal-dual iterate, \(d_k\) an accepted search direction, and \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_k d_k\) with \(\alpha_k>0\). Vanishing accepted steps occur when
\[
\alpha_k\to 0\quad\text{and}\quad \|\alpha_k d_k\|\to 0,
\]
while a termination residual \(R(z_k)\) remains bounded away from zero: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}R(z_k)>0\). Thus acceptance alone does not yield convergence progress; the iterates may stagnate because their actual displacements vanish before approximate first-order optimality or feasibility is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepted steps vanish when their lengths and actual displacements approach zero while the optimality or feasibility residual remains positively bounded, causing nonterminal stagnation.
assumptions_latex: \(R(z)\geq 0\) vanishes at the chosen termination condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z_{k+1}-z_k\|\to0\) while \(\liminf_k R(z_k)>0\), so accepted updates stagnate away from termination.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5 Restricted Step Methods p. 95

review_flags: residual convention requires alignment with surrounding interior-point nodes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5 Restricted Step Methods p. 95

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Accepted Displacements Can Converge Away from Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A stronger vanishing-motion regime in which accepted iterates converge but their limit remains nonterminal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k\) in \(\mathbb R^n\). If
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|s_k\|<\infty,
\]
then \((z_k)\) converges to a finite point \(z_*\). If a termination residual \(R\) is continuous at \(z_*\) and \(\liminf_kR(z_k)>0\), then \(R(z_*)>0\), so the limit is nonterminal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolutely summable accepted displacements force convergence to a finite point, but a continuous residual bounded away from zero makes that limit nonterminal.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is continuous at the resulting limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k\to z_*\), and \(\liminf_kR(z_k)>0\) implies \(R(z_*)>0\).

notation.meaning: finite limit of the accepted iterates

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Accepted Displacements Can Converge Away from Termination

children.title: Insufficient Merit Progress
children.top_down_role: Regimes where accepted iterates deliver inadequate feasibility or objective progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Merit Progress
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted steps fail to deliver a nonnegligible fraction of the merit decrease predicted by the globalization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi_k\) be the merit function used at iteration \(k\), let \(d_k\) be the computed direction, and let \(\Delta_k>0\) be its predicted merit decrease. For accepted steps \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), define the achieved-to-predicted ratio
\[
\rho_k=\frac{\Phi_k(x_k)-\Phi_k(x_{k+1})}{\Delta_k}.
\]
Insufficient merit progress occurs along an infinite index set \(K\) when
\[
\liminf_{\substack{k\to\infty\\k\in K}}\Delta_k>0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\rho_k\to0\quad\text{as }k\to\infty,a0k\in K.
\]
Thus the achieved reduction is asymptotically negligible relative to a predicted decrease bounded away from zero, and the accepted updates do not realize the globalization model's predicted progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merit progress is insufficient along an infinite set of accepted iterations when the predicted decrease remains bounded away from zero but the achieved decrease becomes a vanishing fraction of that prediction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\liminf_{k\to\infty,\,k\in K}\Delta_k>0\) and \(\rho_k\to0\) along \(K\), then the achieved merit reduction is asymptotically negligible relative to the predicted reduction along \(K\).

notation.meaning: infinite index set of accepted iterations under consideration

children.title: Restoration Failure
children.top_down_role: Failure to recover acceptable feasibility progress.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonzero-Residual Local Minimum of a Restoration Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A feasible constraint system whose squared-residual restoration objective has a spurious nonzero-residual local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
c(x)=(x^2+1)(x^2-4),
\qquad \psi(x)=\tfrac12c(x)^2.
\]
The feasibility equation \(c(x)=0\) has solutions \(x=\pm2\). Nevertheless,
\[
c(0)=-4,
\qquad \psi'(0)=0,
\qquad \psi''(0)=24>0.
\]
Thus \(x=0\) is a strict local minimizer of the squared-violation restoration objective with nonzero constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even when feasible points exist, squared-residual restoration can have a strict local minimum with nonzero violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system is feasible at \(x=\pm2\), but \(x=0\) is a strict local minimizer of \(\psi\) with \(c(0)\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonzero-Residual Local Minimum of a Restoration Objective

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restoration Failure Relative to the Declared Return Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-neutral failure of a restoration phase to return an admissible point meeting its declared feasibility-progress condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) be the admissible domain, let \(\theta:\mathcal D\to[0,\infty)\) measure constraint violation, and let \(A_{\mathrm{ret}}(z;z^0)\) be the restoration method's declared predicate for returning from starting point \(z^0\) to the main phase. Restoration fails if it terminates without producing any \(z\in\mathcal D\) satisfying \(A_{\mathrm{ret}}(z;z^0)=\mathrm{true}\), or if it cannot generate an admissible trial. This algorithmic failure is not, by itself, a certificate that the original constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration fails when it cannot return an admissible point satisfying the method's declared feasibility-progress interface; such failure alone does not prove infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The admissible domain \(\mathcal D\), violation measure \(\theta\), and return predicate \(A_{\mathrm{ret}}\) are declared by the method.
The restoration phase terminates or reports inability to generate an admissible trial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No generated admissible point satisfies \(A_{\mathrm{ret}}(z;z^0)\), and this fact alone does not certify infeasibility.

notation.meaning: declared predicate for return to the main phase

review_flags: The concrete return predicate may be a fractional-reduction, filter, trust-region, or other method-specific condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Failure Relative to the Declared Return Interface
Restoration Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A restoration phase cannot recover an acceptable reduction of constraint violation while maintaining the interior domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega^\circ\) be the strict interior domain and let \(\theta:\Omega^\circ\to[0,\infty)\) measure constraint violation. Starting from \(z^0\in\Omega^\circ\), a restoration procedure generates trial points \(z^j\in\Omega^\circ\). For a required factor \(\eta\in(0,1)\), restoration fails if it terminates without finding any trial point satisfying
\[
\theta(z^j)\leq \eta\,\theta(z^0).
\]
Failure also occurs if no admissible interior trial point can be generated. In either case, the algorithm lacks a restoration output that both preserves strict interiority and supplies the feasibility progress required for return to the main globalization phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration fails when no admissible interior trial point achieves the required fractional reduction in constraint violation, so the main globalization phase cannot safely resume.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta\in(0,1)\) is the required restoration reduction factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No generated \(z^j\in\Omega^\circ\) satisfies \(\theta(z^j)\leq\eta\theta(z^0)\), or no such admissible trial can be generated.

notation.meaning: strict interior domain of the barrier formulation

review_flags: no supplied locator specifically supports interior-point restoration failure
restoration acceptance convention may be implementation-dependent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, and the proposed condition is internally coherent, but the fixed fractional-reduction rule is an implementation-specific restoration acceptance convention. No source is supplied to establish that this is the intended interior-point restoration-failure criterion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonzero-Residual Stationarity of a Restoration Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual minimization can terminate stationarily without recovering feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the restoration phase minimize \(\psi(x)=\tfrac12\|c(x)\|^2\). Its stationarity condition is
\[
\nabla\psi(x)=J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}c(x)=0,
\]
which does not imply \(c(x)=0\) unless additional regularity is imposed. For \(c(x)=x^2+1\),
\[
\psi(x)=\tfrac12(x^2+1)^2,
\qquad \psi'(0)=0,
\qquad c(0)=1.
\]
Thus a restoration solver may reach a stationary point with strictly positive violation even though the original feasibility system has no solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity of the squared constraint-violation objective need not imply feasibility; the constraint x²+1 has a stationary restoration point at zero with nonzero residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}c(x)=0\) may hold while \(c(x)\neq0\); specifically, this occurs at \(x=0\) for \(c(x)=x^2+1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonzero-Residual Stationarity of a Restoration Objective

children.title: Maratos-Type Step Rejection
children.top_down_role: Rejection of locally fast steps due to nonlinear constraint mismatch.

knowledge_statements.title: Maratos-Type Step Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A locally fast step satisfying the linearized equality constraints is rejected because nonlinear constraints produce a second-order mismatch not represented by the first-order model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, and consider the equality constraints \(c(x)=0\). At a feasible point \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(d_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy the linearized constraints \(c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d_k=0\). Then
\[
c(x_k+d_k)=\tfrac12 c''(x_k)[d_k,d_k]+o(\!\|d_k\|^2),
\]
so the full step generally has a nonzero second-order constraint residual. A Maratos-type rejection occurs when this mismatch causes the full step \(\alpha=1\) to fail the prescribed merit-function or filter acceptance test even though \(d_k\) is the locally fast step predicted by the first-order constrained model. A second-order correction or a suitable modified acceptance rule may be used to prevent systematic full-step rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Maratos-type rejection occurs when a locally fast full step satisfies the linearized equality constraints but is rejected because the nonlinear constraints produce a second-order residual detected by the globalization test.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is twice continuously differentiable near a feasible point \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual \(c(x_k+d_k)=O(\|d_k\|^2)\) can cause the full step to fail globalization acceptance despite satisfaction of the first-order linearized constraints.

notation.meaning: componentwise second directional derivative of the constraint mapping
step predicted by the first-order constrained model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Correction for Maratos Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction of the nonlinear equality-constraint residual left by a first-order tangential step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(c(x_k)=0\), \(J_c(x_k)d_k=0\), and choose a uniformly bounded right inverse \(B_k\) of \(J_c(x_k)\). Define
\[
w_k=-B_kc(x_k+d_k)+r_k,
\qquad \|r_k\|=o(\|d_k\|^2),
\]
with \(J_c(x_k)r_k=o(\|d_k\|^2)\). If \(c\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(\|d_k\|\to0\), then
\[
\|w_k\|=O(\|d_k\|^2),
\qquad c(x_k+d_k+w_k)=o(\|d_k\|^2).
\]
The corrected trial \(x_k+d_k+w_k\) can then be tested by the declared globalization rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A controlled right-inverse correction cancels the primary step's quadratic constraint residual, has quadratic size, and leaves a residual smaller than second order.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(J_c(x_k)\) admits a uniformly bounded right inverse \(B_k\).
The correction solve is controlled so that no large null-space component is introduced.

notation.meaning: uniformly bounded right inverse of the constraint Jacobian

review_flags: Actual acceptance of the corrected full step additionally depends on the chosen merit or filter rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Correction for Maratos Rejection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maratos-Type Rejection of Locally Fast Steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\) be iterates for a smooth constrained problem, and let \(p_k\) be trial steps generated by a local Newton or SQP model. Let \(\mathcal T_k\) denote the full-step acceptance test of a merit-function or filter globalization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth constrained optimization. The definition identifies rejection caused by second-order nonlinear constraint mismatch, not rejection of a genuinely poor local-model step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Maratos-type step rejection occurs along a subsequence if the full trial steps are locally fast, \[\frac{\|x_k+p_k-x^*\|}{\|x_k-x^*\|}\to0,\] but \(\mathcal T_k(x_k+p_k)=\mathrm{reject}\) for all sufficiently large indices because the nonlinear objective or feasibility measures fail the acceptance test, even though the linearized constraints are satisfied to first order. In the classical quadratic case, \(\|x_k+p_k-x^*\|=O(\|x_k-x^*\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maratos-type rejection occurs when a full Newton or SQP step would give superlinear, often quadratic, local progress but a merit function or filter rejects it because nonlinear constraint curvature produces an adverse second-order change in objective or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_k+p_k-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\) and the full step is eventually rejected by the globalization test.
special_cases_latex: In the classical example, both the objective value and constraint violation increase after a step whose distance to the solution is quadratic in the current error.
immediate_consequences_latex: Persistent Maratos rejection can prevent superlinear convergence.
A second-order correction, suitable nonmonotone acceptance rule, or merit function without this defect can remove the rejection mechanism.
boundary_notes: Rejection caused by an inaccurate direction, indefiniteness, or a large first-order constraint residual is not Maratos-type rejection.
One isolated rejection does not establish an asymptotic Maratos effect.

notation.meaning: Iteration-dependent merit-function or filter acceptance test.

children.title: Nonminimizing Stationary Limits
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex convergence to stationary points lacking minimizing character.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Reduced Curvature Certifies a Nonminimizing KKT Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained second-order certificate excluding local minimality at a first-order stationary limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable. Let \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) satisfy
\[
c(x_*)=0,
\qquad \nabla f(x_*)+J_c(x_*)^{\mathsf T}\lambda_*=0,
\]
and suppose \(J_c(x_*)\) has full row rank. With \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\), if there exists \(v\ne0\) such that
\[
J_c(x_*)v=0,
\qquad v^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_*,\lambda_*)v<0,
\]
then \(x_*\) is not a constrained local minimizer, although a first-order KKT-residual test may accept the limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular equality-constrained KKT point, negative Lagrangian curvature along a tangent direction certifies that the stationary limit is not a local minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of \(v\in\ker J_c(x_*)\setminus\{0\}\) with \(v^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_*,\lambda_*)v<0\) excludes constrained local minimality.

notation.meaning: feasible tangent direction under full-row-rank regularity

review_flags: Inequality-constrained variants use the appropriate critical cone and multiplier assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Reduced Curvature Certifies a Nonminimizing KKT Limit
Nonminimizing Stationary Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order convergence reaches a KKT point possessing a feasible direction of negative Lagrangian curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with twice continuously differentiable data. Let \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) satisfy the KKT equations \(c(x_*)=0\) and \(\nabla f(x_*)+J_c(x_*)^{\mathsf T}\lambda_*=0\). Define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). The stationary limit is nonminimizing when there exists a nonzero tangent direction \(v\) such that
\[
J_c(x_*)v=0,
\qquad
v^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_*,\lambda_*)v<0.
\]
Then the second-order necessary condition for a constrained local minimum fails, although a first-order residual-based interior-point stopping test may declare convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary limit is nonminimizing when it satisfies KKT conditions but has negative Lagrangian curvature along a feasible tangent direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of \(v\neq0\) with \(J_c(x_*)v=0\) and \(v^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_*,\lambda_*)v<0\) excludes a constrained local minimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonminimizing KKT Accumulation Point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a smooth, possibly nonconvex nonlinear program with feasible set \(\Omega\). Let \(x_k\) be primal iterates and let \(\bar x\in\Omega\) be an accumulation point satisfying the KKT conditions for some multiplier \(\bar\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex finite-dimensional optimization. The definition distinguishes first-order stationarity from local minimizing character.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(\bar x\) is a nonminimizing stationary limit if \[\exists k_j\uparrow\infty:\ x_{k_j}\to\bar x,\qquad \bar x\text{ satisfies the KKT conditions},\] but \(\bar x\) is not a local minimizer over \(\Omega\). Equivalently, \[\forall r>0\ \exists x_r\in\Omega:\ \|x_r-\bar x\|<r\quad\text{and}\quad f(x_r)<f(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonminimizing stationary limit is an accumulation point of the iterates that satisfies the KKT conditions but is not a local minimizer. Arbitrarily close feasible points have strictly smaller objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is KKT and \(\forall r>0\ \exists x_r\in\Omega\cap B_r(\bar x)\) with \(f(x_r)<f(\bar x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Non-local-minimality is equivalent to the existence of a feasible sequence \(u_j\to\bar x\) with \(f(u_j)<f(\bar x)\) for every \(j\).
special_cases_latex: Under twice differentiability and a suitable constraint qualification, a direction in the critical cone with \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)d<0\) is a standard second-order witness against local minimality.
For unconstrained problems, a stationary point with a negative Hessian eigenvalue is a nonminimizing stationary point.
immediate_consequences_latex: A globalization theorem guaranteeing only convergence to first-order stationary points does not exclude this outcome in a nonconvex problem.
boundary_notes: A stationary point with positive-semidefinite Hessian can still fail to be a local minimizer because higher-order behavior may dominate.
In convex optimization, every feasible KKT point under the usual sufficiency conditions is globally minimizing, so this boundary is specifically nonconvex.

notation.meaning: Open Euclidean ball of radius r centered at the accumulation point.
